5.85.d: पर सम्राजे बर्हद अर्चा गभीरम बरह्म परियं वरुणाय शरुताय | वि यो जघान शमितेव चर्मोपस्तिरे पर्थिवीं सूर्याय ||
5.85.e: SING forth a hymn sublime and solemn, grateful to glorious. Varuṇa, imperial Ruler,  Who hath struck out, like one who slays the victim, earth as a skin to spread in front of Sūrya.

5.85.d: वनेषु वय अन्तरिक्षं ततान वाजम अर्वत्सु पय उस्रियासु | हर्त्सु करतुं वरुणो अप्स्व अग्निं दिवि सूर्यम अदधात सोमम अद्रौ ||
5.85.e: In the tree-tops the air he hath extended, put milk in kine and vigorous speed in horses,  Set intellect in hearts, fire in the waters, Siurya in heaven and Soma on the mountain.

5.85.d: नीचीनबारं वरुणः कवन्धम पर ससर्ज रोदसी अन्तरिक्षम | तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वर्ष्टिर वय उनत्ति भूम ||
5.85.e: Varuṇa lets the big cask, opening downward, flow through the heaven and earth and air's mid-region.  Therewith the universe's Sovran waters earth as the shower of rain bedews the barley.

5.85.d: उनत्ति भूमिम पर्थिवीम उत दयां यदा दुग्धं वरुणो वष्ट्य आद इत | सम अभ्रेण वसत पर्वतासस तविषीयन्तः शरथयन्त वीराः ||
5.85.e: When Varuṇa is fain for milk he moistens the sky, the land, and earth to her foundation.  Then straight the mountains clothe them in the rain-cloud: the Heroes, putting forth their vigour, loose them.

5.85.d: इमाम ऊ षव रसुरस्य शरुतस्य महीम मायां वरुणस्य पर वोचम | मानेनेव तस्थिवां अन्तरिक्षे वि यो ममे पर्थिवीं सूर्येण ||
5.85.e: I will declare this mighty deed of magic, of glorious Varuṇa the Lord Immortal,  Who standing in the firmament hath meted the earth out with the Sun as with a measure.

5.85.d: इमाम ऊ नु कवितमस्य मायाम महीं देवस्य नकिर आ दधर्ष | एकं यद उद्ना न पर्णन्त्य एनीर आसिञ्चन्तीर अवनयः समुद्रम ||
5.85.e: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God's mighty deed of magic,  Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.

5.85.d: अर्यम्यं वरुण मित्र्यं वा सखायं वा सदम इद भरातरं वा | वेशं वा नित्यं वरुणारणं वा यत सीम आगश चक्र्मा शिश्रथस तत ||
5.85.e: If we have sinned against the man who loves us, have ever wronged a brother, friend, or comrade,  The neighbour ever with us, or a stranger, O Varuṇa, remove from us the trespass.

5.85.d: कितवासो यद रिरिपुर न दीवि यद वा घा सत्यम उत यन न विद्म | सर्वा ता वि षय शिथिरेव देवाधा ते सयाम वरुण परियासः ||
5.85.e: If we, as gamesters cheat at play, have cheated, done wrong unwittingly or sinned of purpose,  Cast all these sins away like loosened fetters, and, Varuṇa let us be thine own beloved.

5.86.d: इन्द्राग्नी यम अवथ उभा वाजेषु मर्त्यम | दर्ळ्हा चित स पर भेदति दयुम्ना वाणीर इव तरितः ||
5.86.e: THE mortal man whom ye, the Twain, Indra and Agni, help in fight,  Breaks through e’en strongly-guarded wealth as Tṛta burst his way through reeds.

5.86.d: या पर्तनासु दुष्टरा या वाजेषु शरवाय्या | या पञ्च चर्षणीर अभॄन्द्राग्नी ता हवामहे ||
5.86.e: The Twain invincible in war, worthy to be renowned in frays,  Lords of the Fivefold. People, these, Indra and Agni, we invoke.

5.86.d: तयोर इद अमवच छवस तिग्मा दिद्युन मघोनोः | परति दरुणा गभस्त्योर गवां वर्त्रघ्न एषते ||
5.86.e: Impetuous is their strength, and keen the lightning of the mighty Pair,  Which from their arms speeds with the car to Vṛtra's slayer for the kine.

5.86.d: ता वाम एषे रथानाम इन्द्राग्नी हवामहे | पती तुरस्य राधसो विद्वांसा गिर्वणस्तमा ||
5.86.e: Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, as such, to send your cars:  Lords of quick-coming bounty, ye who know, chief lovers of the song.

5.86.d: ता वर्धन्ताव अनु दयून मर्ताय देवाव अदभा | अर्हन्ता चित पुरो दधे ऽंशेव देवाव अर्वते ||
5.86.e: These who give increase day by day, Gods without guile for mortal man,  Worthy themselves, I honour most, Two Gods as partners, for my horse.

5.86.d: एवेन्द्राग्निभ्याम अहावि हव्यं शूष्यं घर्तं न पूतम अद्रिभिः | ता सूरिषु शरवो बर्हद रयिं गर्णत्सु दिध्र्तम इषं गर्णत्सु दिध्र्तम ||
5.86.e: The strength-bestowing offering thus to Indra-Agni hath been paid, as butter, purified by stones.  Deal to our princes high renown, deal wealth to those who sing your praise, deal food to those who sing your praise.

5.87.d: पर वो महे मतयो यन्तु विष्णवे मरुत्वते गिरिजा एवयामरुत | पर शर्धाय परयज्यवे सुखादये तवसे भन्ददिष्टये धुनिव्रताय शवसे ||
5.87.e: To Viṣṇu, to the Mighty whom the Maruts follow let your hymns born in song go forth, Evayamarut;  To the impetuous, strong band, adorned with bracelets, that rushes on in joy and ever roars for vigour.

5.87.d: पर ये जाता महिना ये च नु सवयम पर विद्मना बरुवत एवयामरुत | करत्वा तद वो मरुतो नाध्र्षे शवो दाना मह्ना तद एषाम अध्र्ष्टासो नाद्रयः ||
5.87.e: They who with might were manifest, and who willingly by their own knowledge told it forth, Evayamarut.  Maruts, this strength of yours no wisdom comprehendeth: through their gifts' greatness they are moveless as the mountains.

5.87.d: पर ये दिवो बर्हतः शर्ण्विरे गिरा सुशुक्वानः सुभ्व एवयामरुत | न येषाम इरी सधस्थ ईष्ट आं अग्नयो न सवविद्युतः पर सयन्द्रासो धुनीनाम ||
5.87.e: Who by the psalm they sing are heard, from lofty heaven, the strong, the brightly shining Ones, Evayamarut;  In whose abode there is no mightier one to move them, whose lightnings are as fires, who urge the roaring rivers.

5.87.d: स चक्रमे महतो निर उरुक्रमः समानस्मात सदस एवयामरुत | यदायुक्त तमना सवाद अधि षणुभिर विष्पर्धसो विमहसो जिगाति शेव्र्धो नर्भिः ||
5.87.e: He of the Mighty Stride forth strode, Evayamarut, out of the spacious dwelling-place, their home in common.  When he, himself, hath yoked his emulous strong horses on heights, he cometh forth, joy-giving, with the Heroes.

5.87.d: सवनो न वो ऽमवान रेजयद वर्षा तवेषो ययिस तविष एवयामरुत | येना सहन्त रञ्जत सवरोचिष सथारश्मानो हिरण्ययाः सवायुधास इष्मिणः ||
5.87.e: Like your tremendous roar, the rainer with light flashing, strong, speeding, hath made all tremble, Evayamarut,  Wherewith victorious ye, self-luminous, press onward, with strong reins, decked with gold, impetuous and well-weaponed.

5.87.d: अपारो वो महिमा वर्द्धशवसस तवेषं शवो ऽवत्व एवयामरुत | सथातारो हि परसितौ संद्र्शि सथन ते न उरुष्यता निदः शुशुक्वांसो नाग्नयः ||
5.87.e: Unbounded is your greatness, ye of mighty power: may your bright vigour be our aid, Evayamarut;  For ye are visible helpers in the time of trouble: like fires, aglow with light, save us from shame and insult.

5.87.d: ते रुद्रासः सुमखा अग्नयो यथा तुविद्युम्ना अवन्त्व एवयामरुत | दीर्घम पर्थु पप्रथे सद्म पार्थिवं येषाम अज्मेष्व आ महः शर्धांस्य अद्भुतैनसाम ||
5.87.e: So may the Rudras, mighty warriors, Evayamarut, with splendid brilliancy, like fires, be our protectors;  They whose terrestrial dwelling-place is wide-extended, whom none suspect of sin, whose bands have lofty courage.

5.87.d: अद्वेषो नो मरुतो गातुम एतन शरोता हवं जरितुर एवयामरुत | विष्णोर महः समन्यवो युयोतन समद रथ्यो न दंसनाप दवेषांसि सनुतः ||
5.87.e: Come in a friendly spirit, come to us, O Maruts, and hear his call who praises you, Evayamarut.  Like car-borne men, one-minded with the mighty Viṣṇu, keep enmity far from us with your deeds of wonder.

5.87.d: गन्ता नो यज्ञं यज्ञियाः सुशमि शरोता हवम अरक्ष एवयामरुत | जयेष्ठासो न पर्वतासो वयोमनि यूयं तस्य परचेतसः सयात दुर्धर्तवो निदः ||
5.87.e: Come to our sacrifice, ye Hnly Ones, to bless it, and, free from demons, hear our call, Evayamarut.

6.1.d: तवं हयग्ने परथमो मनोतास्या धियो अभवो दस्म होता | तवं सीं वर्षन्नक्र्णोर्दुष्टरीतु सहो विश्वस्मै सहसे सहध्यै ||
6.1.e: THOU, first inventor of this prayer, O Agni, Worker of Marvels, hast become our Herald.  Thou, Bull, hast made us strength which none may conquer, strength that shall overcome all other prowess.

6.1.d: अधा होता नयसीदो यजीयानिळस पद इषयन्नीड्यः सन | तं तवा नरः परथमं देवयन्तो महो राये चितयन्तो अनु गमन ||
6.1.e: As Priest thou sattest at the seat of worship, furthering us, best Offerer, meet for honour.  So first to thee have pious men resorted, turning thy mind to thoughts of ample riches.

6.1.d: वर्तेव यन्तं बहुभिर्वसव्यैस्त्वे रयिं जाग्र्वांसो अनु गमन | रुशन्तमग्निं दर्शतं बर्हन्तं वपावन्तं विश्वहा दीदिवांसम ||
6.1.e: In thee, still watching, they have followed riches, who goest with much wealth as with an army,  The radiant Agni, lofty, fair to look on, worshipped with marrow, evermore resplendent.

6.1.d: पदं देवस्य नमसा वयन्तः शरवस्यवः शरव आपन्नम्र्क्तम | नामानि चिद दधिरे यज्ञियानि भद्रायां ते रणयन्तसन्द्र्ष्टौ ||
6.1.e: They who approached the God's abode with homage, eager for glory, won them perfect glory:  Yea, they gained even sacrificial titles, and found delight in thine auspicious aspect.

6.1.d: तवां वर्धन्ति कषितयः पर्थिव्यां तवां राय उभयासो जनानाम | तवं तराता तरणे चेत्यो भूः पिता माता सदमिन मानुषाणाम ||
6.1.e: On earth the people magnify thee greatly, thee their celestial and terrestrial riches.  Thou, Helper, must be known as our Preserver, Father and Mother of mankind for ever.

6.1.d: सपर्येण्यः स परियो विक्ष्वग्निर्होता मन्द्रो नि षसादा यजीयान | तं तवा वयं दम आ दीदिवांसमुप जञुबाधो नमसा सदेम ||
6.1.e: Dear priest among mankind, adorable Agni hath seated him, joy-giver, skilled in worship.  Let us approach thee shining in thy dwelling, kneeling upon our knees, with adoration.

6.1.d: तं तवा वयं सुध्यो नव्यमग्ने-सुम्नायव ईमहे देवयन्तः | तवं विशो अनयो दीद्यानो दिवो अग्ने बर्हता रोचनेन ||
6.1.e: Longing for bliss, pure-minded, God-devoted, Agni, we seek thee, such, meet to be lauded.  Thou, Agni, leddest forth our men to battle, refulgent with the heaven's exalted splendour.

6.1.d: विशां कविं विश्पतिं शश्वतीनां नितोशनं वर्षभं चर्षणीनाम | परेतीषणिमिषयन्तं पावकं राजन्तमग्निं यजतं रयीणाम ||
6.1.e: Sage of mankind, all peoples' Lord and Master, the Bull of men, the sender down of blessings,  Still pressing on, promoting, purifying, Agni the Holy One, the Lord of riches.

6.1.d: सो अग्न ईजे शशमे च मर्तो यस्त आनट समिधा हव्यदातिम | य आहुतिं परि वेदा नमोभिर्विश्वेत स वामा दधतेत्वोतः ||
6.1.e: Agni, the mortal who hath toiled and worshipped, brought thee oblations with his kindled fuel,  And well knows sacrifice with adoration, gains every joy with thee to guard and help him.

6.1.d: अस्मा उ ते महि महे विधेम नमोभिरग्ने समिधोत हव्यैः | वेदी सूनो सहसो गीर्भिरुक्थैरा ते भद्रायां सुमतौयतेम ||
6.1.e: Mightily let us worship thee the Mighty, with reverence, Agni! fuel and oblations,  With songs, O Son of Strength, with hymns, with altar: so may we strive for thine auspicious favour.

6.1.d: आ यस्ततन्थ रोदसी वि भासा शरवोभिश्च शरवस्यस्तरुत्रः | बर्हद्भिर्वाजै सथविरेभिरस्मे रेवद्भिरग्ने वितरं वि भाहि ||
6.1.e: Thou who hast covered heaven and earth with splendour and with thy glories, glorious and triumphant.  Continue thou to shine on us, O Agni, with strength abundant, rich, and long enduring.

6.1.d: नर्वद वसो सदमिद धेह्यस्मे भूरि तोकाय तनयाय पश्वः | पूर्वीरिषो बर्हतीरारेघा अस्मे भद्रा सौश्रवसानि सन्तु ||
6.1.e: Vouchsafe us ever, as man needs, O Vasu, abundant wealth of kine for son and offspring.  Food noble, plenteous, far from sin and evil, he with us, and fair fame to make us happy.

6.1.d: पुरूण्यग्ने पुरुधा तवाया वसूनि राजन वसुता ते अश्याम | पुरूणि हि तवे पुरुवार सन्त्यग्ने वसु विधते राजनि तवे ||
6.1.e: May I obtain much wealth in many places by love of thee and through thy grace, King Agni;  For in thee Bounteous One, in thee the Sovran, Agni, are many boons for him who serves thee.

6.2.d: तवं हि कषैतवद यशो.अग्ने मित्रो न पत्यसे | तवं विचर्षणे शरवो वसो पुष्टिं न पुष्यसि ||
6.2.e: THOU, Agni, even as Mitra, hast a princely glory of thine own.  Thou, active Vasu, makest fame increase like full prosperity.

6.2.d: तवां हि षमा चर्षणयो यज्ञेभिर्गीर्भिरीळते | तवां वाजी यात्यव्र्को रजस्तूर्विश्वचर्षणिः ||
6.2.e: For, verily, men pray to thee with sacrifices and with songs.  To thee the Friendly Courser, seen of all, comes speeding through the air.

6.2.d: सजोषस्त्वा दिवो नरो यज्ञस्य केतुमिन्धते | यद ध सय मानुषो जनः सुम्नायुर्जुह्वे अध्वरे ||
6.2.e: Of one accord men kindle thee Heaven's signal of the sacrifice,  When, craving bliss, this race of man invites thee to the solemn rite.

6.2.d: रधद यस्ते सुदानवे धिया मर्तः शशमते | ऊती ष बर्हतो दिवो दविषो अंहो न तरति ||
6.2.e: Let the man thrive who travails sore, in prayer, far thee the Bountiful.  He with the help of lofty Dyaus comes safe through straits of enmity.

6.2.d: समिधा यस्त आहुतिं निशितिं मर्त्यो नशत | वयावन्तंस पुष्यति कषयमग्ने शतायुषम ||
6.2.e: The mortal who with fuel lights thy flame and offers unto thee,  Supports a house with many a branch, Agni, to live a hundred years.

6.2.d: तवेषस्ते धूम रण्वति दिवि षञ्छुक्र आततः | सूरो न हि दयुता तवं कर्पा पावक रोचसे ||
6.2.e: Thy bright smoke lifts itself aloft, and far-extended shines in heaven.  For, Purifier! like the Sun thou beamest with thy radiant glow.

6.2.d: अधा हि विक्ष्वीड्यो.असि परियो नो अतिथिः | रण्वः पुरीव जूर्यः सूनुर्न तरययाय्यः ||
6.2.e: For in men's houses thou must be glorified as a well-loved guest,  Gay like an elder in a fort, claiming protection like a son.

6.2.d: करत्वा हि दरोणे अज्यसे.अग्ने वाजी न कर्त्व्यः | परिज्मेवस्वधा गयो.अत्यो न हवार्यः शिशुः ||
6.2.e: Thou, Agni, like an able steed, art urged by wisdom in the wood.  Thou art like wind; food, home art thou, like a young horse that runs astray.

6.2.d: तवं तया चिदच्युताग्ने पशुर्न यवसे | धामा ह यत ते अजर वना वर्श्चन्ति शिक्वसः ||
6.2.e: E’en things imperishable, thou, O Agni, like a gazing ox,  Eatest, when hosts, Eternal One! of thee the Mighty rend the woods.

6.2.d: वेषि हयध्वरीयतामग्ने होता दमे विशाम | सम्र्धो विश्पते कर्णु जुषस्व हव्यमङगिरः ||
6.2.e: Agni, thou enterest as Priest the home of men who sacrifice.  Lord of the people, prosper them. Accept the ofrering, Aṅgiras!

6.2.d: अछा नो मित्रमहो देव देवानग्ने वोचः सुमतिं रोदस्योः | वीहि सवस्तिं सुक्षितिं दिवो नॄन दविषो अंहांसि दुरितातरेम ता तरेम तवावसा तरेम ||
6.2.e: O Agni, God with Mitra's might, call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven.  Bring weal from heaven, that men may dwell securely. May we o’ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o’ercome them, through thy help o’ercome them.

6.3.d: अग्ने स कषेषद रतपा रतेजा उरु जयोतिर्नशते देवयुष टे | यं तवं मित्रेण वरुणः सजोषा देव पासि तयजसा मर्तमंहः ||
6.3.e: TRUE, guardian of the Law, thy faithful servant wins ample light and dwells in peace, O Agni,  Whom thou, as Varuṇa in accord with Mitra, guardest, O God, by banishing his trouble.

6.3.d: ईजे यज्ञेभिह शशमे शमीभिर्र्धद्वारायाग्नये ददाश | एवा चन तं यशसामजुष्टिर्नांहो मर्तं नशते न परद्र्प्तिः ||
6.3.e: He hath paid sacrifices, toiled in worship, and offered gifts to wealth-increasing Agni.  Him the displeasure of the famous moves not, outrage and scorn affect not such a mortal.

6.3.d: सूरो न यस्य दर्शतिररेपा भीमा यदेति शुचतस्त आ धीः | हेषस्वतः शुरुधो नायमक्तोः कुत्रा चिद रण्वो वसतिर्वनेजाः ||
6.3.e: Bright God, whose look is free from stain like Sūrya's, thou, swift, what time thou earnestly desirest,  Hast gear to give us. Come with joy at evening, where, Child of Wood, thou mayest also tarry.

6.3.d: तिग्मं चिदेम महि वर्पो अस्य भसदश्वो न यमसान आसा | विजेहमानः परशुर्न जिह्वां दरविर्न दरावयति दारु धक्षत ||
6.3.e: Fierce is his gait and vast his wondrous body: he champeth like a horse with bit and bridle,  And, darting forth his tongue, as ’twere a hatchet, burning the woods, smelteth them like a smelter.

6.3.d: स इदस्तेव परति धादसिष्यञ्छिशीत तेजो.अयसो न धाराम | चित्रध्रजतिररतिर्यो अक्तोर्वेर्न दरुषद्वा रघुपत्मजंहाः ||
6.3.e: Archer-like, fain toshoot, he sets his arrow, and whets his splendour like the edge of iron:  The messenger of night with brilliant pathway, like a tree-roosting bird of rapid pinion.

6.3.d: स ईं रेभो न परति वस्त उस्राः शोचिषा रारपीति मित्रमहाः | नक्तं य ईमरुषो यो दिवा नॄनमर्त्यो अरुषो यो दिवा नॄन ||
6.3.e: In beams of morn he clothes him like the singer, and bright as Mitra with his splendour crackles.  Red in the night, by day the men's possession: red, he belongs to men by day, Immortal.

6.3.d: दिवो न यस्य विधतो नवीनोद वर्षा रुक्ष ओषधीषु नूनोत | घर्णा न यो धरजसा पत्मना यन्ना रोदसी वसुनादं सुपत्नी ||
6.3.e: Like Heaven's when scattering beams his voice was uttered: among the plants the radiant Hero shouted,  Who with his glow in rapid course came hither to fill both worlds, well-wedded Dames, with treasure.

6.3.d: धायोभिर्वा यो युज्येभिरर्कैर्विद्युन न दविद्योत सवेभिःशुष्मैह | शर्धो वा यो मरुतां ततक्ष रभुर्न तवेषोरभसानो अद्यौत ||
6.3.e: Who, with supporting streams and rays that suit him, hath flashed like lightning with his native vigour.  Like the deft Maker of the band of Maruts, the bright impetuous One hath shone refulgent.

6.4.d: यथा होतर्मनुषो देवताता यज्ञेभिः सूनो सहसो यजासि | एवा नो अद्य समना समानानुशन्नग्न उशतो यक्षि देवान ||
6.4.e: As at man's service of the Gods, Invoker, thou, Son of Strength, dost sacrifice and worship,  So bring for us to-day all Gods together, bring willingly the willing Gods, O Agni.

6.4.d: स नो विभावा चक्षणिर्न वस्तोरग्निर्वन्दारु वेद्यश्चनो धात | विश्वायुर्यो अम्र्तो मर्त्येषूषर्भुद भूदतिथिर्जातवेदाः ||
6.4.e: May Agni, radiant Herald of the morning, meet to be known, accept our praise with favour.  Dear to all life, mid mortal men Immortal, our guest, awake at dawn, is Jātavedas.

6.4.d: दयावो न यस्य पनयन्त्यभ्वं भासांसि वस्ते सूर्यो न शुक्रः | वि य इनोत्यजरः पावको.अश्नस्य चिच्छिश्नथत पूर्व्याणि ||
6.4.e: Whose might the very heavens regard with wonder: bright as the Sun he clothes himself with lustre.  He who sends forth,, Eternal Purifier, hath shattered e’en the ancient works of Aśna.

6.4.d: वद्मा हि सूनो अस्यद्मसद्वा चक्रे अग्निर्जनुषाज्मान्नम | स तवं न ऊर्जसन ऊर्जं धा राजेव जेरव्र्के कषेष्यन्तः ||
6.4.e: Thou art a Singer, Son! our feast-companion: Agni at birth prepared his food and pathway.  Therefore vouchsafe us strength, O Strength-bestower. Win like a King: foes trouble not thy dwelling.

6.4.d: नितिक्ति यो वारणमन्नमत्ति वायुर्न राष्ट्र्यत्येत्यक्तून | तुर्याम यस्त आदिशामरातीरत्यो न हरुतः पततः परिह्रुत ||
6.4.e: Even he who cats his firm hard food with swiftness,and overtakes the nights as Vāyu kingdoms.  May we o’ercome those who resist thine orders, like a steed casting down the flying foemen.

6.4.d: आ सूर्यो न भानुमद्भिरर्कैरग्ने ततन्थ रोदसी वि भासा | चित्रो नयत परि तमांस्यक्तः शोचिषा पत्मन्नौशिजो न दीयन ||
6.4.e: Like Sūrya with his fulgent rays, O Agni, thou overspreadest both the worlds with splendour.  Decked with bright colour he dispels the darkness, like Auśija, with clear flame swifily flying.

6.4.d: तवां हि मन्द्रतममर्कशोकैर्वव्र्महे महि नः शरोष्यग्ने | इन्द्रं न तवा शवसा देवता वायुं पर्णन्ति राधसान्र्तमाः ||
6.4.e: We have elected thee as most delightful for thy beams' glow: hear our great laud, O Agni.  The best men praise thee as the peer of Indra in strength, mid Gods, like Viyu in thy bounty.

6.4.d: नू नो अग्ने.अव्र्केभिः सवस्ति वेषि रायः पथिभिः पर्ष्यंहः | ता सूरिभ्यो गर्णते रासि सुम्नं मदेम शतहिमाःसुवीराः ||
6.4.e: Now, Agni, on the tranquil paths of riches come to us for our weal: save us from sorrow.  Grant chiefs and bard this boon. May we live happy, with hero children, through a hundred winters.

6.5.d: हुवे वः सूनुं सहसो युवानमद्रोघवाचं मतिभिर्यविष्ठम | य इन्वति दरविणानि परचेता विश्ववाराणि पुरुवारोध्रुक ||
6.5.e: I INVOCATE your Son of Strength, the Youthful, with hymns, the Youngest God, whose speech is guileless;  Sage who sends wealth comprising every treasure, bringer of many boons, devoid of malice.

6.5.d: तवे वसूनि पुर्वणीक होतर्दोषा वस्तोरेरिरे यज्ञियासः | कषामेव विश्वा भुवनानि यस्मिन सं सौभगानि दधिरेपावके ||
6.5.e: At eve and morn thy pious servants bring thee their precious gifts, O Priest of many aspects,  On whom, the Purifier, all things living as on firm. ground their happiness have stablished.

6.5.d: तवं विक्षु परदिवः सीद आसु करत्वा रथीरभवो वार्याणाम | अत इनोषि विधते चिकित्वो वयानुषग जातवेदो वसूनि ||
6.5.e: Thou from of old hast dwelt among these people, by mental power the charioteer of blessings.  Hence sendest thou, O sapient Jātavedas, to him who serves thee treasures in succession.

6.5.d: यो नः सनुत्यो अभिदासदग्ने यो अन्तरो मित्रमहो वनुष्यात | तमजरेभिर्व्र्षभिस्तव सवैस्तपा तपिष्ठ तपसा तपस्वान ||
6.5.e: Agni, whoever secretly attacks us, the neighbour, thou with Mitra's might! who harms us,  Burn him with thine own Steers for ever youthful, burning with burning heat, thou fiercest burner.

6.5.d: यस्ते यज्ञेन समिधा य उक्थैरर्केभिः सूनो सहसो ददाशत | स मर्त्येष्वम्र्त परचेता राया दयुम्नेन शरवसा वि भाति ||
6.5.e: He who serves thee with sacrifice and fuel, with hymn, O Son of Strength, and chanted praises,  Shines out, Immortal! in the midst of mortals, a sage, with wealth, with splendour and with glory.

6.5.d: स तत कर्धीषितस्तूयमग्ने सप्र्धो बाधस्व सहसा सहस्वान | यच्छस्यसे दयुभिरक्तो वचोभिस्तज्जुषस्व जरितुर्घोषि मन्म ||
6.5.e: Do this, O Agni, when we urge thee, quickly, triumphant in thy might subdue our foemen.  When thou art praised with words and decked with brightness, accept this chanted hymn, the singer's worship.

6.5.d: अश्याम तं काममग्ने तवोती अश्याम रयिं रयिवः सुवीरम | अश्याम वाजमभि वाजयन्तो.अश्याम दयुम्नमजराजरं ते ||
6.5.e: Help us, that we may gain this wish, O Agni, gain riches, Wealthy One! with store of heroes.  Desiring strength from thee may we be strengthened, and win, Eternal! thine eternal glory.

6.6.d: पर नव्यसा सहसः सूनुमछा यज्ञेन गातुमव इछमानः | वर्श्चद्वनं कर्ष्णयामं रुशन्तं वीती होतारन्दिव्यं जिगाति ||
6.6.e: HE who seeks furtherance and grace to help him goes to the Son of Strength with newest worship,  Calling the heavenly Priest to share the banquet, who rends the wood, bright, with his blackened pathway.

6.6.d: स शवितानस्तन्यतू रोचनस्था अजरेभिर्नानदद्भिर्यविष्ठः | यः पावकः पुरुतमः पुरूणि पर्थून्यग्निरनुयाति भर्वन ||
6.6.e: White-hued and thundering he dwells in splendour, Most Youthful, with the loudvoiced and eternal-  Agni, most variform, the Purifier, who follows crunching many ample forests.

6.6.d: वि ते विष्वग वातजूतासो अग्ने भामासः शुचे शुचयश्चरन्ति | तुविम्रक्षासो दिव्या नवग्वा वना वनन्ति धर्षता रुजन्तः ||
6.6.e: Incited by the wind thy flames, O Agni, move onward, Pure One! pure, in all directions.  Thy most destructive heavenly Navagvas break the woods down and devastate them boldly.

6.6.d: ये ते शुक्रासः शुचयः शुचिष्मः कषां वपन्ति विषितासो अश्वाः | अध भरमस्त उर्विया वि भाति यातयमानो अधि सानु पर्श्नेः ||
6.6.e: Thy pure white horses from their bonds are loosened: O Radiant One, they shear the ground beneath them,  And far and wide shines out thy flame, and flickers rapidly moving over earth's high ridges.

6.6.d: अध जिह्वा पापतीति पर वर्ष्णो गोषुयुधो नाशनिः सर्जाना | शूरस्येव परसितिः कषातिरग्नेर्दुर्वर्तुर्भीमो दयते वनानि ||
6.6.e: Forth darts the Bull's tongue like the sharp stone weapon discharged by him who fights to win the cattle.  Agni's fierce flame is like a hero's onset: dread and resistless he destroys the forests.

6.6.d: आ भानुना पार्थिवानि जरयांसि महस्तोदस्य धर्षता ततन्थ | स बाधस्वाप भया सहोभि सप्र्धो वनुष्यन वनुषो नि जूर्व ||
6.6.e: Thou with the sunlight of the great Impeller hast boldly over-spread the earth's expanses.  So drive away with conquering might all perils. fighting out foemen burn up those who harm us.

6.6.d: स चित्र चित्रं चितयन्तमस्मे चित्रक्षत्र चित्रतमं वयोधाम | चन्द्रं रयिं पुरुवीरं बर्हन्तं चन्द्र चन्द्राभिर्ग्र्णते युवस्व ||
6.6.e: Wondrous! of wondrous power! give to the singer wealth wondrous, marked, most wonderful, life-giving.  Wealth bright, O Bright One, vast, with many heroes, give with thy bright flames to the man who lauds thee.

6.7.d: मूर्धानं दिवो अरतिं पर्थिव्या वैश्वानरं रत आ जातमग्निम | कविं सम्राजमतिथिं जनानामासन्ना पात्रं जनयन्त देवाः ||
6.7.e: Him, messenger of earth and head of heaven, Agni Vaiśvānara, born in holy Order,  The Sage, the King, the guest of men, a vessel fit for their mouths, the Gods have generated.

6.7.d: नाभिं यज्ञानां सदनं रयीणां महामाहावमभिसं नवन्त | वैश्वानरं रथ्यमध्वराणां यज्ञस्य केतुं जनयन्त देवाः ||
6.7.e: Him have they praised, mid-point of sacrifices, great cistern of libations, seat of riches.  Vaiśvānara, conveyer of oblations, ensign of worship, have the Gods engendered.

6.7.d: तवद विप्रो जायते वाज्यग्ने तवद वीरासो अभिमातिषाहः | वैश्वानर तवमस्मासु धेहि वसूनि राजन सप्र्हयाय्याणि ||
6.7.e: From thee, O Agni, springs the mighty singer, from thee come heroes who subdue the foeman.  O King, Vaiśvānara, bestow thou on us excellent treasures worthy to belonged fo r.

6.7.d: तवां विश्वे अम्र्त जायमानं शिशुं न देवा अभि सं नवन्ते | तव करतुभिरम्र्तत्वमायन वैश्वानर यत पित्रोरदीदेः ||
6.7.e: To thee, Immortal! when to life thou springest, all the Gods sing for joy as to their infant.  They by thy mental powers were made immortal, Vaiśvānara, when thou shonest from thy Parents.

6.7.d: वैश्वानर तव तानि वरतानि महान्यग्ने नकिरा दधर्ष | यज्जायमानः पित्रोरुपस्थे.अविन्दः केतुं वयुनेष्वह्नाम ||
6.7.e: Agni Vaiśvānara, no one hath ever resisted these thy mighty ordinances,  When thou, arising from thy Parents' bosom, foundest the light for days' appointed courses.

6.7.d: वैश्वानरस्य विमितानि चक्षसा सानूनि दिवो अम्र्तस्य केतुना | तस्येदु विश्वा भुवनाधि मूर्धनि वया इव रुरुहुःसप्त विस्रुहः ||
6.7.e: The summits of the heaven are traversed through and through by the Immortal's light, Vaiśvānara's brilliancy.  All creatures in existence rest upon his head. The Seven swift-flowing Streams have grown like branches forth,

6.7.d: वि यो रजांस्यमिमीत सुक्रतुर्वैश्वानरो वि दिवो रोचना कविः | परि यो विश्वा भुवनानि पप्रथे.अदब्धो गोपा अम्र्तस्य रक्षिता ||
6.7.e: Vaiśvānara, who measured out the realms of air, Sage very wise who made the lucid spheres of heaven,  The Undeceivable who spread out all the worlds, keeper is he and guard of immortality.

6.8.d: पर्क्षस्य वर्ष्णो अरुषस्य नू सहः पर नु वोचं विदथाजातवेदसः | वैश्वानराय मतिर्नव्यसी शुचिः सोम इवपवते चारुरग्नये ||
6.8.e: AT Jātavedas' holy gathering I will tell aloud the conquering might of the swift red-hued Steer.  A pure and fresher hymn flows to Vaiśvānara, even as for Agni lovely Soma is made pure.

6.8.d: स जायमानः परमे वयोमनि वरतान्यग्निर्व्रतपा अरक्षत | वयन्तरिक्षममिमीत सुक्रतुर्वैश्वानरो महिना नाकमस्प्र्शत ||
6.8.e: That Agni, when in loftiest heaven he sprang to life, Guardian of Holy Laws, kept and observed them well.  Exceeding wise, he measured out the firmament. Vaiśvānara attained to heaven by mightiness.

6.8.d: वयस्तभ्नाद रोदसी मित्रो अद्भुतो.अन्तर्वावदक्र्णोज्ज्योतिषा तमः | वि चर्मणीव धिषणे अवर्तयद वैश्वानरो विश्वमधत्त वर्ष्ण्यम ||
6.8.e: Wonderful Mitra propped the heaven and earth apart, and covered and concealed  the darkness with his light.  He made the two bowls part asunder like two skins. Vaiśvānara put forth all his creative power.

6.8.d: अपामुपस्थे महिषा अग्र्भ्णत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्र्ग्मियम | आ दूतो अग्निमभरद विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ||
6.8.e: The Migbty seized him in the bosom of the floods: the people waited on the King who should be praised.  As envoy of Vivasvān MatariSvan brought Agni Vaiśvānara hither from far away.

6.8.d: युगे-युगे विदथ्यं गर्णद्भ्यो.अग्ने रयिं यशसं धेहि नव्यसीम | पव्येव राजन्नघशंसमजर नीचा नि वर्श्च वनिनं न तेजसा ||
6.8.e: In every age bestow upon the singers wealth, worthy of holy synods, glorious, ever new.  King, undecaying, as it were with sharpened bolt, smite down the sinner like a tree with lightning-flash.

6.8.d: अस्माकमग्ने मघवत्सु धारयानामि कषत्रमजरं सुवीर्यम | वयं जयेम शतिनं सहस्रिणं वैश्वानर वाजमग्ने तवोतिभिः ||
6.8.e: Do thou bestow, O Agni, on our wealthy chiefs, rule, with good heroes, undecaying, bending not.  So may we win for us strength. O Vaiśvānara, hundredfold, thousandfold, O Agni, by thy help.

6.8.d: अदब्धेभिस्तव गोपाभिरिष्टे.अस्माकं पाहि तरिषधस्थ सूरीन | रक्षा च नो ददुषां शर्धो अग्ने वैश्वानर पर चतारी सतवानः ||
6.8.e: O thou who dwellest in three places, Helper, keep with effective guards our princely patrons.  Keep our band, Agni, who have brought thee presents. Lengthen their lives, Vaiśvānara, when lauded.

6.9.d: अहश्च कर्ष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः | वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्ज्योतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ||
6.9.e: ONE half of day is dark, and bright the other: both atmospheres move on by sage devices.  Agni Vaiśvānara, when born as Sovran, hath with his lustre overcome the darkness.

6.9.d: नाहं तन्तुं न वि जानाम्योतुं न यं वयन्ति समरेऽतमानाः | कस्य सवित पुत्र इह वक्त्वानि परो वदात्यवरेण पित्रा ||
6.9.e: I know not either warp or woof, I know not the web they weave when moving to the contest.  Whose son shall here speak words that must be spoken without assistance from the Father near him?

6.9.d: स इत तन्तुं स वि जानात्योतुं स वक्त्वान्य रतुथा वदाति | य ईं चिकेतदम्र्तस्य गोपा अवश्चरन परो अन्येन पश्यन ||
6.9.e: For both the warp and woof he understandeth, and in due time shall speak what should be spoken,  Who knoweth as the immortal world's Protector, descending, seeing with no aid from other.

6.9.d: अयं होता परथमः पश्यतेममिदं जयोतिरम्र्तं मर्त्येषु | अयं स जज्ञे धरुव आ निषत्तो.अमर्त्यस्तन्वा वर्धमानः ||
6.9.e: He is the Priest, the first of all: behold him. Mid mortal men he is the light immortal.  Here was he born, firm-seated in his station Immortal, ever waxing in his body.

6.9.d: धरुवं जयोतिर्निहितं दर्शये कं मनो जविष्ठं पतयत्स्वन्तः | विश्वे देवाः समनसः सकेता एकं करतुमभिवि यन्ति साधु ||
6.9.e: A firm light hath been set for men to look on: among all things that fly the mind is swiftest.  All Gods of one accord, with one intention, move unobstructed to a single purpose.

6.9.d: वि मे कर्णा पतयतो वि चक्षुर्वीदं जयोतिर्ह्र्दय आहितं यत | वि मे मनश्चरति दूराधीः किं सविद वक्ष्यामिकिमु नू मनिष्ये ||
6.9.e: Mine ears unclose to hear, mine eye to see him; the light that harbours in my spirit broadens.  Far roams my mind whose thoughts are in the distance. What shall I speak, what shall I now imagine?

6.9.d: विश्वे देवा अनमस्यन भियानास्त्वामग्ने तमसि तस्थिवांसम | वैश्वानरो.अवतूतये नो.अमर्त्यो.अवतूतये नः ||
6.9.e: All the Gods bowed them down in fear before thee, Agni, when thou wast dwelling in the darkness.  Vaiśvānara be gracious to assist us, may the Immortal favour us and help us.

6.10.d: पुरो वो मन्द्रं दिव्यं सुव्र्क्तिं परयति यज्ञे अग्निमध्वरेदधिध्वम | पुर उक्थेभिः स हि नो विभावा सवध्वरा करति जातवेदाः ||
6.10.e: INSTALL at sacrifice, while the rite advances, your pleasant, heavenly Agni, meet for praises.  With hymns-for he illumines us-install him. He, Jātavedas, makes our rites successful.

6.10.d: तमु दयुमः पुर्वणीक होतरग्ने अग्निभिर्मनुष इधानः | सतोमं यमस्मै ममतेव शूषं घर्तं न शुचि मतयः पवन्ते ||
6.10.e: Hear this laud, Radiant Priest of many aspects, O Agni with the fires of man enkindled,  Laud which bards send forth pure as sacred butter, strength to this man, as ’twere for self-advantage.

6.10.d: पीपाय स शरवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्थैः | चित्राभिस्तमूतिभिश्चित्रशोचिर्व्रजस्य साता गोमतो दधाति ||
6.10.e: Mid mortal men that singer thrives in glory who offers gifts with hymns of praise to Agni,  And the God, wondrous bright, with wondrous succours helps him to win a stable filled with cattle.

6.10.d: आ यः पप्रौ जायमान उर्वी दूरेद्र्शा भासा कर्ष्णाध्वा | अध बहु चित तम ऊर्म्यायास्तिरः शोचिषा दद्र्शे पावकः ||
6.10.e: He, at his birth, whose path is black behind him, filled heaven and earth with far-apparent splendour:  And he himself hath been. through night's thick darkness, made manifest by light, the Purifier.

6.10.d: नू नश्चित्रं पुरुवाजाभिरूती अग्ने रयिं मघवद्भ्यश्च धेहि | ये राधसा शरवसा चात्यन्यान सुवीर्येभिश्चाभि सन्ति जनान ||
6.10.e: With thy most mighty aid, confer, O Agni, wonderful wealth on us and on our princes,  Who stand preeminent, surpassing others in liberal gifts, in fame, and hero virtues.

6.10.d: इमं यज्ञं चनो धा अग्न उशन यं त आसानो जुहुते हविष्मान | भरद्वाजेषु दधिषे सुव्र्क्तिमवीर्वाजस्य गध्यस्य सातौ ||
6.10.e: Agni, accept this sacrifice with gladness, which, seated here, the worshipper presenteth.  Fair hymns hadst thou among the Bharadvājas, and holpest them to gain abundant vigour.

6.10.d: वि दवेषांसीनुहि वर्धयेळां मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ||
6.10.e: Scatter our foes, increase our store. May we he glad a hundred winters with brave sons.

6.11.d: यजस्व होतरिषितो यजीयानग्ने बाधो मरुतां न परयुक्ति | आ नो मित्रावरुणा नासत्या दयावा होत्राय पर्थिवी वव्र्त्याः ||
6.11.e: EAGERLY Sacrifice thou, most skilful, Agni! Priest, pressing on as if the Maruts sent thee.  To our oblation bring the two Nāsatyas, Mitra and Varuṇa and Earth and Heaven.

6.11.d: तवं होता मन्द्रतमो नो अध्रुगन्तर्देवो विदथा मर्त्येषु | पावकया जुह्वा वह्निरासाग्ने यजस्व तन्वं तव सवाम ||
6.11.e: Thou art our guileless, most delightful Herald, the God, among mankind, of holy synods.  A Priest with purifying tongue, O Agni, sacrifice with thy mouth to thine own body.

6.11.d: धन्या चिद धि तवे धिषणा वष्टि पर देवाञ जन्म गर्णते यजध्यै | वेपिष्ठो अङगिरसां यद ध विप्रो मधु छन्दो भनति रेभ इष्टौ ||
6.11.e: For even the blessed longing that is in thee would bring the Gods down to the singer's worship,  When the Aṅgirases' sagest Sage, the Poet, sings the sweet measure at the solemn service.

6.11.d: अदिद्युतत सवपाको विभावाग्ने यजस्व रोदसी उरूची | आयुं न यं नमसा रातहव्या अञ्जन्ति सुप्रयसं पञ्च जनाः ||
6.11.e: Bright hath he beamed, the wise, the far-refulgent. Worship the two widespreading Worlds, O Agni,  Whom as the Living One rich in oblations the Five Tribes, bringing gifts, adorn with homage.

6.11.d: वर्ञ्जे ह यन नमसा बर्हिरग्नावयामि सरुग घर्तवती सुव्र्क्तिः | अम्यक्षि सद्म सदने पर्थिव्या अश्रायि यज्ञः सूर्ये न चक्षुः ||
6.11.e: When I with reverence clip the grass for Agni, when the trimmed ladle, fullof oil, is lifted,  Firm on the seat of earth is based the altar: eye-like, the sacrifice is directed Sun-ward.

6.11.d: दशस्या नः पुर्वणीक होतर्देवेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिधानः | रायः सूनो सहसो वावसाना अति सरसेम वर्जनं नांहः ||
6.11.e: Enrich us, O thou Priest of many aspects, with the Gods, Agni, with thy fires, enkindled.  O Son of Strength, clad in the robe of riches, may we escape from woe as from  a prison.

6.12.d: मध्ये होता दुरोणे बर्हिषो राळ अग्निस्तोदस्य रोदसी यजध्यै | अयं स सूनुः सहस रतावा दूरात सूर्यो न शोचिषा ततान ||
6.12.e: KING of trimmed grass, Herald within the dwelling, may Agni worship the Impeller's World-halves.  He, Son of Strength, the Holy, from a distance hath spread himself abroad with light like Sūrya.

6.12.d: आ यस्मिन तवे सवपाके यजत्र यक्षद राजन सर्वतातेव नुद्यौः | तरिषधस्थस्ततरुषो न जंहो हव्या मघानि मानुषा यजध्यै ||
6.12.e: In thee, most wise, shall Dyaus, for full perfection, King! Holy One! pronounce the call to worship.  Found in three places, like the Speeder's footstep, come to present men's riches as oblations!

6.12.d: तेजिष्ठा यस्यारतिर्वनेराट तोदो अध्वन न वर्धसानो अद्यौत | अद्रोघो न दरविता चेतति तमन्नमर्त्यो.अवर्त्र ओषधीषु ||
6.12.e: Whose blaze most splendid, sovran in the forest, shines waxing on his way like the - Impeller.  He knows himself, like as a guileless smelter, not to be stayed among the plants, Immortal.

6.12.d: सास्माकेभिरेतरी न शूषैरग्नि षटवे दम आ जातवेदाः | दर्वन्नो वन्वन करत्वा नार्वोस्रः पितेव जारयायि यज्ञैः ||
6.12.e: Our friends extol him like a steed for vigour even Agni in the dwelling, jatave~as.  Trce-fed, he fights with power as doth a champion, like Dawn's Sire to be praised with sacrifices.

6.12.d: अध समास्य पनयन्ति भासो वर्था यत तक्षदनुयाति पर्थ्वीम | सद्यो यः सयन्द्रो विषितो धवीयान रणो न तायुरति धन्वा राट ||
6.12.e: Men wonder at his shining glows when, paring the woods with case, o’er the broad earth he goeth,  And, like a rushing flood, loosed quickly, burneth, swift as a guilty thief, o’er desert places.

6.12.d: स तवं नो अर्वन निदाया विश्वेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिधानः | वेषि रायो वि यासि दुछुना मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ||
6.12.e: So mighty thou protectest us from slander, O Champion, Agni! with all fires enkindled.  Bring opulence and drive away affliction. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.13.d: तवद विश्वा सुभग सौभगान्यग्ने वि यन्ति वनिनो न वयाः | शरुष्टी रयिर्वाजो वर्त्रतूर्ये दिवो वर्ष्टिरीड्यो रीतिरपाम ||
6.13.e: FROM thee, as branches from a tree, O Agni, from thee, Auspicious God! spring all our blessings-  Wealth swiftly, strength in battle with our foemen, the rain besought of heaven, the flow of waters.

6.13.d: तवं भगो न आ हि रत्नमिषे परिज्मेव कषयसि दस्मवर्चाः | अग्ने मित्रो न बर्हत रतस्यासि कषत्ता वामस्य देव भूरेः ||
6.13.e: Thou art our Bhaga to send wealth thou dwellest, like circumambient air, with wondrous splendour.  Friend art thou of the lofty Law, like Mitra, Controller, Agni! God! of many a blessing.

6.13.d: स सत्पतिः शवसा हन्ति वर्त्रमग्ने विप्रो वि पणेर्भर्तिवाजम | यं तवं परचेत रतजात राया सजोषा नप्त्रापां हिनोषि ||
6.13.e: Agni! the hero slays with might his foeman; the singer bears away the Paṇi's booty-  Even he whom thou, Sage, born in Law, incitest by wealth, accordant with the Child of Waters.

6.13.d: यस्ते सूनो सहसो गीर्भिरुक्थैर्यज्ञैर्मर्तो निशितिं वेद्यानट | विश्वं स देव परति वारमग्ने धत्ते धान्यं पत्यते वसव्यैः ||
6.13.e: The man who, Son of Strength 1 with sacrifices, hymns, lauds, attracts thy fervour to the altar,  Enjoys each precious thing, O God, O Agni, gains wealth of corn and is the lord of treasures.

6.13.d: ता नर्भ्य आ सौश्रवसा सुवीराग्ने सूनो सहसः पुष्यसेधाः | कर्णोषि यच्छवसा भूरि पश्वो वयो वर्कायारयेजसुरये ||
6.13.e: Grant, Son of Strength, to men for their subsistence such things as bring high fame and hero children.  For thou with might givest much food in cattle even to the wicked wolf when he is hungry.

6.13.d: वद्मा सूनो सहसो नो विहाया अग्ने तोकं तनयं वाजि नो दाः | विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरभि पूर्तिमश्यां मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ||
6.13.e: Eloquent, Son of Strength, Most Mighty, Agni, vouchsafe us seed and offspring, full of vigour.  May I by all my songs obtain abundance. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.14.d: अग्ना यो मर्त्यो दुवो धियं जुजोष धीतिभिः | भसन नुष पर पूर्व्य इषं वुरीतावसे ||
6.14.e: WHOSO to Agni hath endeared his thought and service by his hymns,  That mortal cats before the rest, and finds sufficiency of food.

6.14.d: अग्निरिद धि परचेता अग्निर्वेधस्तम रषिः | अग्निं होतारमीळते यज्ञेषु मनुषो विशः ||
6.14.e: Agni, in truth, is passing wise, most skilled in ordering, a Seer.  At sacrifices Manus' sons glorify Agni as their Priest.

6.14.d: नाना हयग्ने.अवसे सपर्धन्ते रायो अर्यः | तूर्वन्तो दस्युमायवो वरतैः सीक्षन्तो अव्रतम ||
6.14.e: The foeman's wealth in many a place, Agni, is emulous to help.  Men fight the fiend, and seek by rites to overcome the riteless foe.

6.14.d: अग्निरप्सां रतीषहं वीरं ददाति सत्पतिम | यस्य तरसन्ति शवसः संचक्षि शत्रवो भिया ||
6.14.e: Agni bestows the hero chief, winner of waters, firm in fray.  Soon as they look upon his might his enemies tremble in alarm.

6.14.d: अग्निर्हि विद्मना निदो देवो मर्तमुरुष्यति | सहावा यस्याव्र्तो रयिर्वाजेष्वव्र्तः ||
6.14.e: For with his wisdom Agni, God, protects the mortal from reproach,  Whose conquering wealth is never checked, is never checked in deeds of might.

O Agni, God with Mitra's might call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven.  Bring weal from heaven that men may dwell securely. May we o’ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o’ercome them, through thy help o’ercome them.

6.15.d: इममू षु वो अतिथिमुषर्बुधं विश्वासां विशां पतिम्र्ञ्जसे गिरा | वेतीद दिवो जनुषा कच्चिदा शुचिर्ज्योक चिदत्ति गर्भो यदच्युतम ||
6.15.e: WITH this my song I strive to reach this guest of yours, who wakes at early morn, the Lord of all the tribes.  Each time he comes from heaven, the Pure One from of old: from ancient days the Child cats everlasting food.

6.15.d: मित्रं न यं सुधितं भर्गवो दधुर्वनस्पतावीड्यमूर्ध्वशोचिषम | स तवं सुप्रीतो वीतहव्ये अद्भुत परशस्तिभिर्महयसे दिवे दिवे ||
6.15.e: Whom, well-dis sed, the Blirgus stablished as a rriend, whom men must glorify, high-flaming in the wood.  As such, most friendly, thou art every day extolled in lauds by Vitahavya, O thou wondrous God.

6.15.d: स तवं दक्षस्याव्र्को वर्धो भूरर्यः परस्यान्तरस्य तरुषः | रायः सूनो सहसो मर्त्येष्वा छर्दिर्यछ वीतहव्याय सप्रथो भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः ||
6.15.e: Be thou the foeless helper of the skilful man, subduer of the enemy near or far away.  Bestow a wealthy home on men, O Son of Strength. Give Vitahavya riches spreading far and wide, give Bharadvāja wide-spread wealth.

6.15.d: दयुतानं वो अतिथिं सवर्णरमग्निं होतारं मनुषः सवध्वरम | विप्रं न दयुक्षवचसं सुव्र्क्तिभिर्हव्यवाहमरतिं देवं रञ्जसे ||
6.15.e: Him, your refulgent guest, Agni who comes from heaven, the Herald of mankind, well-skilled in sacred rites,  Who, like a holy singer, utters heavenly words, oblation-bearer, envoy, God, I seek with hymns.

6.15.d: पावकया यश्चितयन्त्या कर्पा कषामन रुरुच उषसो न भानुना | तूर्वन न यामन्नेतशस्य नू रण आ यो घर्णे न तत्र्षाणो अजरः ||
6.15.e: Who with his purifying, eye-attracting form hath shone upon the earth as with the light of Dawn;  Who speeding on, as in the fight of Etaia, cometh, untouched by age, as one athirst in heat.

6.15.d: अग्निम-अग्निं वः समिधा दुवस्यत परियम-परियं वो अतिथिं गर्णीषणि | उप वो गीर्भिरम्र्तं विवासत देवो देवेषु वनते हि वार्यं देवो देवेषु वनते हि नो दुवः ||
6.15.e: Worship ye Agni, Agni, with your log of wood; praise your beloved, your beloved guest with songs.  Invite ye the Immortal hither with your hymns. A God among the Gods, he loveth what is choice, loveth our service, God mid Gods.

6.15.d: समिद्धमग्निं समिधा गिरा गर्णे शुचिं पावकं पुरो अध्वरे धरुवम | विप्रं होतारं पुरुवारमद्रुहं कविं सुम्नैरीमहे जातवेदसम ||
6.15.e: Agni inflamed with fuel in my song I sing, pure, Cleanser, steadlast, set in tront at sacrifice.  Wise Jātavedas we implore with prayers for bliss the Priest, the holy Singer, bounteous, void of guile.

6.15.d: तवां दूतमग्ने अम्र्तं युगे-युगे हव्यवाहं दधिरे पायुमीड्यम | देवासश्च मर्तासश्च जाग्र्विं विभुं विश्पतिं नमसा नि षेदिरे ||
6.15.e: Men, Agni, in each age have made thee, Deathiess One, their envoy, offering-bearer, guard adorable.  With reverence Gods and mortals have established thee, the ever-watchful, omnipresent Household Lord.

6.15.d: विभूषन्नग्न उभयाननु वरता दूतो देवानां रजसी समीयसे | यत ते धीतिं सुमतिमाव्र्णीमहे.अध समा नस्त्रिवरूथः शिवो भव ||
6.15.e: Thou, Agni, ordering the works and ways of both, as envoy of the Gods traversest both the worlds.  When we lay claim to thy regard and gracious fare, be thou to us a thriceprotecting friendly guard.

6.15.d: तं सुप्रतीकं सुद्र्शं सवञ्चमविद्वांसो विदुष्टरं सपेम | स यक्षद विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान पर हव्यमग्निरम्र्तेषु वोचत ||
6.15.e: Him fair of face, rapid, and fair to look on, him very wise may we who know not follow.  Let him who knows all rules invite for worship, Agru announce our offering to the Immortals.

6.15.d: तमग्ने पास्युत तं पिपर्षि यस्त आनट कवये शूर धीतिम | यज्ञस्य वा निशितिं वोदितिं वा तमित पर्णक्षि शवसोत राया ||
6.15.e: Him, Agni, thou deliverest and savest who brings him prayer to thee the Wise, O Hero,  The end of sacrifice or its inception; yea, thou endowest him with power and riches.

6.15.d: तवमग्ने वनुष्यतो नि पाहि तवमु नः सहसावन्नवद्यात | सं तवा धवस्मन्वदभ्येतु पाथः सं रयि सप्र्हयाय्यःसहस्री ||
6.15.e: Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us, O thou Victor, from dishonour.  Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable in thousands.

6.15.d: अग्निर्होता गर्हपतिः स राजा विश्वा वेद जनिमा जातवेदः | देवानामुत यो मर्त्यानां यजिष्ठः स पर यजतां रतावा ||
6.15.e: Agni, the Priest, is King, Lord of the homestead, he, Jatayedas, knows all generations.  Most skilful worshipper mid Gods and mortals, may he begin the sacrifice, the Holy.

6.15.d: अग्ने यदद्य विशो अध्वरस्य होतः पावकशोचे वेष टवं हि यज्वा | रता यजासि महिना वि यद भूर्हव्या वह यविष्ठ या ते अद्य ||
6.15.e: Whate’er to-day thou, bright-flamed Priest, enjoyest from the man's rite-for thou art sacrificer-  Worship, for duly dost thou spread in greatness: bear off thine ofrerings of to-day, Most Youthful.

6.15.d: अभि परयांसि सुधितानि हि खयो नि तवा दधीत रोदसी यजध्यै | अवा नो मघवन वाजसातावग्ने विश्वानि दुरिता तरेम ता तरेम तवावसा तरेम ||
6.15.e: Look thou upon the viands duly laid for thee. Fain would he set thee here to worship Heaven and,Earth.  Help us, O liberal Agni, in the strife for spoil, so that we may o’ercome all things that trouble us, o’ercome, o’ercome them with thy help.

6.15.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिः सवनीक देवैरूर्णावन्तं परथमः सीद योनिम | कुलायिनं घर्तवन्तं सवित्रे यज्ञं नय यजमानाय साधु ||
6.15.e: Together with all Gods, O fair-faced Agni, be seated first upon the woollined altar,  Nest-like, bedewed with oil. Bear this our worship to Savitar who sacrifices rightly.

6.15.d: इममु तयमथर्ववदग्निं मन्थन्ति वेधसः | यमङकूयन्तमानयन्नमूरं शयाव्याभ्यः ||
6.15.e: Here the arranging priests, as did Atharvan, rub this Agni forth,  Whom, not bewildered, as he moved in winding ways, they brought from gloom.

6.15.d: जनिष्वा देववीतये सर्वताता सवस्तये | आ देवान वक्ष्यम्र्तान रताव्र्धो यज्ञं देवेषु पिस्प्र्शः ||
6.15.e: For the Gods’ banquet be thou born, for full perfection and for weal.  Bring the Immortal Gods who strengthen holy Law: so let our sacrifice reach the Gods.

6.15.d: वयमु तवा गर्हपते जनानामग्ने अकर्म समिधा बर्हन्तम | अस्थूरि नो गार्हपत्यानि सन्तु तिग्मेन नस्तेजसा सं शिशाधि ||
6.15.e: O Agni, Lord and Master of men's homesteads, with kindled fuel we have made thee mighty.  Let not our household gear be found defective. Sharpen us with thy penetrating splendour.

6.16.d: तवमग्ने यज्ञानां होता विश्वेषां हितः | देवेभिर्मानुषे जने ||
6.16.e: PRIEST of all sacrifices hast thou been appointed by the Gods,  Agni, amid the race of man.

6.16.d: स नो मन्द्राभिरध्वरे जिह्वाभिर्यजा महः | आ देवान वक्षि यक्षि च ||
6.16.e: So with thy joyous tongues for us sacrifice nobly in this rite.  Bring thou the Gods and worship them.

6.16.d: वेत्था हि वेधो अध्वनः पथश्च देवाञ्जसा | अग्ने यज्ञेषु सुक्रतो ||
6.16.e: For well, O God, Disposer, thou knowest, straight on, the paths and ways,  Agni, most wise in sacrifice.

6.16.d: तवामीळे अध दविता भरतो वाजिभिः शुनम | ईजे यज्ञेयत दिवि ||
6.16.e: Thee, too, hath Bhārata of old, with mighty men, implored for bliss.  And worshipped thee the worshipful.

6.16.d: तवमिमा वार्या पुरु दिवोदासाय सुन्वते | भरद्वाजाय दाशुषे ||
6.16.e: Thou givest these abundant boons to Divodāsa pouring forth,  To Bharadvāja offering gifts.

6.16.d: तवं दूतो अमर्त्य आ वहा दैव्यं जनम | शर्ण्वन विप्रस्य सुष्टुतिम ||
6.16.e: Do thou, Immortal Messenger, bring hither the Celestial Folk;  Hearing the singer's eulogy.

6.16.d: तवामग्ने सवाध्यो मर्तासो देव वीतये | यज्ञेषु देवमीळते ||
6.16.e: Mortals with pious thought implore thee, Agni, God, at holy rites,  To come unto the feast of Gods.

6.16.d: तव पर यक्षि सन्द्र्शमुत करतुं सुदानवः | विश्वे जुषन्त कामिनः ||
6.16.e: I glorify thine aspect and the might of thee the Bountilul.  All those who love shall joy in thee,

6.16.d: तवं होता मनुर्हितो वह्निरासा विदुष्टरः | अग्ने यक्षिदिवो विशः ||
6.16.e: Invoker placed by Manus, thou, Agni, art near, the wisest Priest:  Pay worship to the Tribes of Heaven.

6.16.d: अग्न आ याहि वीतये गर्णानो हव्यदातये | नि होता सत्सि बर्हिषि ||
6.16.e: Come, Agni, lauded, to the feast; come to the offering of the gifts.  As Priest be seated on the grass.

6.16.d: तं तवा समिद्भिरङगिरो घर्तेन वर्धयामसि | बर्हच्छोचा यविष्ठ्य ||
6.16.e: So, Aṅgiras, we make thee strong with fuel and with holy oil.  Blaze high, thou youngest of the Gods.

6.16.d: स नः पर्थु शरवाय्यमछा देव विवाससि | बर्हदग्ने सुवीर्यम ||
6.16.e: For us thou winnest, Agni, God, heroic strength exceeding great,  Far-spreading and of high renown.

6.16.d: तवामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमन्थत | मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः ||
6.16.e: Agni, Atharvan brought thee forth, by rubbing, from the lotus-flower,  The head of Visva, of the Priest.

6.16.d: तमु तवा दध्यंं रषिः पुत्र ईधे अथर्वणः | वर्त्रहणं पुरन्दरम ||
6.16.e: Thee. Vṛtra's slayer, breaker down of castles, hath Atharvan's son,  Dadhyac the Ṛṣi, lighted up.

6.16.d: तमु तवा पाथ्यो वर्षा समीधे दस्युहन्तमम | धनंजयं रणे-रणे ||
6.16.e: The hero Pathya kindled thee the Dasyus'. most destructive foe,  Winner of spoil in every fight.

6.16.d: एह्यू षु बरवाणि ते.अग्न इत्थेतरा गिरः | एभिर्वर्धास इन्दुभिः ||
6.16.e: Come, here, O Agni, will I sing verily other songs to thee,  And with these drops shalt thou grow strong.

6.16.d: यत्र कव च ते मनो दक्षं दधस उत्तरम | तत्रा सदः कर्णवसे ||
6.16.e: Where’er thy mind applies itself, vigour preeminent hast thou:  There wilt thou gain a dwelling-place.

6.16.d: नहि ते पूर्तमक्षिपद भुवन नेमानां वसो | अथा दुवो वनवसे ||
6.16.e: Not for a moment only lasts thy bounty, good to many a one!  Our service therefore shalt thou gain.

6.16.d: आग्निरगामि भारतो वर्त्रहा पुरुचेतनः | दिवोदासस्य सत्पतिः ||
6.16.e: Agni, the Bhārata, hath been sought, the Vṛtra-slayer, marked of all,  Yea, Divodāsa's Hero Lord.

6.16.d: स हि विश्वाति पार्थिवा रयिं दाशन महित्वना | वन्वन्नवातो अस्त्र्तः ||
6.16.e: For he gave riches that surpass in greatness all the things of earth,  Fighting untroubled, unsubdued.

6.16.d: स परत्नवन नवीयसाग्ने दयुम्नेन संयता | बर्हत ततन्थभानुना ||
6.16.e: Thou, Agni, as in days of old, with recent glory, gathered light,  Hast overspread the lofty heaven.

6.16.d: पर वः सखायो अग्नये सतोमं यज्ञं च धर्ष्णुया | अर्चगाय च वेधसे ||
6.16.e: Bring to your Agni, O my friends, boldly your laud and sacrifice:  Give the Disposer praise and song.

6.16.d: स हि यो मानुषा युगा सीदद धोता कविक्रतुः | दूतश्च हव्यवाहनः ||
6.16.e: For as sagacious Herald he hath sat through every age of man,  Oblation-bearing messenger.

6.16.d: ता राजाना शुचिव्रतादित्यान मारुतं गणम | वसो यक्षीह रोदसी ||
6.16.e: Bring those Two Kings whose ways are pure, Ādityas, and the Marut host,  Excellent God! and Heaven and Earth.

6.16.d: वस्वी ते अग्ने सन्द्र्ष्टिरिषयते मर्त्याय | ऊर्जो नपादम्र्तस्य ||
6.16.e: For strong and active mortal man, excellent, Agni, is the look Of thee Immortal, Son of Strength

6.16.d: करत्वा दा अस्तु शरेष्ठो.अद्य तवा वन्वन सुरेक्णाः | मर्त आनाश सुव्र्क्तिम ||
6.16.e: Rich through his wisdom, noblest be the giver serving thee to-day:  The man hath brought his hymn of praise.

6.16.d: ते ते अग्ने तवोता इषयन्तो विश्वमायुः | तरन्तो अर्यो अरातीर्वन्वन्तो अर्यो अरातीः ||
6.16.e: These, Agni, these are helped by thee, who strong and active all their lives,  O'ercome the malice of the foe, fight down the malice ofthe foe.

6.16.d: अग्निस्तिग्मेन शोचिषा यासद विश्वं नयत्रिणम | अग्निर्नोवनते रयिम ||
6.16.e: May Agni with his pointed blaze cast down each fierce devouring fiend  May Agni win us wealth by war.

6.16.d: सुवीरं रयिमा भर जातवेदो विचर्षणे | जहि रक्षांसि सुक्रतो ||
6.16.e: O active Jātavedas, bring riches with store of hero sons:  Slay thou the demons, O Most Wise.

6.16.d: तवं नः पाह्यंहसो जातवेदो अघायतः | रक्षा णो बरह्मणस कवे ||
6.16.e: Keep us, O Jātavedas, from the troubling of the man of sin:  Guard us thou Sage who knowest prayer.

6.16.d: यो नो अग्ने दुरेव आ मर्तो वधाय दाशति | तस्मान नः पाह्यंहसः ||
6.16.e: Whatever sinner, Agni, brings oblations to procure our death,  Save us from woe that he would work.

6.16.d: तवं तं देव जिह्वया परि बाधस्व दुष्क्र्तम | मर्तो यो नोजिघांसति ||
6.16.e: Drive from us with thy tongue, O God, the man who doeth evil deeds,  The mortal who would strike us dead.

6.16.d: भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः शर्म यछ सहन्त्य | अग्ने वरेण्यंवसु ||
6.16.e: Give shelter reaching far and wide to Bharadvāja, conquering Lord!  Agni, send wealth most excellent.

6.16.d: अग्निर्व्र्त्राणि जङघनद दरविणस्युर्विपन्यया | समिद्धः शुक्र आहुतः ||
6.16.e: May Agni slay the Vṛtras,—fain for riches, through the lord of song,  Served with oblation, kindled, bright.

6.16.d: गर्भे मातुः पितुष पिता विदिद्युतानो अक्षरे | सीदन्न्र्तस्य योनिमा ||
6.16.e: His Father's Father, shining in his Mother's everlasting side,  Set on the seat of holy Law.

6.16.d: बरह्म परजावदा भर जातवेदो विचर्षणे | अग्ने यद दीद अयद दिवि ||
6.16.e: O active Jātavedas, bring devotion that wins progeny, Agni, that it may shine to heaven.

6.16.d: उप तवा रण्वसन्द्र्शं परयस्वन्तः सहस्क्र्त | अग्ने सस्र्ज्महे गिरः ||
6.16.e: O Child of Strength, to thee whose look is lovely we with dainty food,  O Agni, have poured forth our songs.

6.16.d: उप छायामिव घर्णेरगन्म शर्म ते वयम | अग्ने हिरण्यसन्द्र्शः ||
6.16.e: To thee for shelter are we come, as to the shade from fervent heat  Agni, who glitterest like gold.

6.16.d: य उग्र इव शर्यहा तिग्मश्र्ङगो न वंसगः | अग्ने पुरो रुरोजिथ ||
6.16.e: Mighty as one who slays with shafts, or like a bull with sharpened horn,  Agni, thou breakest down the forts.

6.16.d: आ यं हस्ते न खादिनं शिशुं जातं न बिभ्रति | विशामग्निं सवध्वरम ||
6.16.e: Whom, like an infant newly born, devourer, in their arms they bear,  Men's Agni, skilled in holy rites.

6.16.d: पर देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तमम | आ सवे योनौ नि षीदतु ||
6.16.e: Bear to the banquet of the Gods the God best finder-out of wealth,  Let him he seated in his place.

6.16.d: आ जातं जातवेदसि परियं शिशीतातिथिम | सयोन आ गर्हपतिम ||
6.16.e: In Jātavedas kindle ye the dear guest who hath now appeared  In a soft place, the homestead's Lord.

6.16.d: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि ये तवाश्वासो देव साधवः | अरं वहन्ति मन्यवे ||
6.16.e: Harness, O Agni, O thou God, thy steeds which are most excellent:  They bear thee as thy spirit wills.

6.16.d: अछा नो याह्या वहाभि परयांसि वीतये | आ देवान सोमपीतये ||
6.16.e: Come hither, bring the Gods to us to taste the sacrificial feast,  To drink the draught of Soma juice.

6.16.d: उदग्ने भारत दयुमदजस्रेण दविद्युतत | शोचा वि भाह्यजर ||
6.16.e: O Agni of the Bharatas, blaze high with everlasting might,  Shine forth and gleam, Eternal One.

6.16.d: वीती यो देवं मर्तो दुवस्येदग्निमीळीताध्वरे हविष्मान | होतारं सत्ययजं रोदस्योरुत्तानहस्तो नमसा विवासेत ||
6.16.e: The mortal man who serves the God with banquet, and, bringing gifts at sacrifice, lauds Agni,  May well attract, with prayer and hands uplifted, the Priest of Heaven and Earth, true Sacrificer.

6.16.d: आ ते अग्न रचा हविर्ह्र्दा तष्टं भरामसि | ते ते भवन्तूक्षण रषभासो वशा उत ||
6.16.e: Agni, we bring thee, with our hymn, oblation fashioned in the heart.  Let these be oxen unto thee, let these be bulls and kine to thee.

6.16.d: अग्निं देवासो अग्रियमिन्धते वर्त्रहन्तमम | येना वसून्याभ्र्ता तर्ळ्हा रक्षांसि वाजिनाषु यज्ञियम ||
6.16.e: The Gods enkindle Agni, best slayer of Vṛtra, first in rank,  The Mighty, One who brings us wealth and crushes down the Rākṣasas.

6.17.d: पिबा सोममभि यमुग्र तर्द ऊर्वं गव्यं महि गर्णानैन्द्र | वि यो धर्ष्णो वधिषो वज्रहस्त विश्वा वर्त्रममित्रिया शवोभिः ||
6.17.e: DRINK Soma, Mighty One, for which, when lauded, thou breakest through the cattle-stall, O Indra;  Thou who, O Bold One, armed with thunder smotest Vṛtra with might, and every hostile being.

6.17.d: स ईं पाहि य रजीषी तरुत्रो यः शिप्रवान वर्षभो यो मतीनाम | यो गोत्रभिद वज्रभ्र्द यो हरिष्ठाः स इन्द्र चित्रानभि तर्न्धि वाजान ||
6.17.e: Drink it thou God who art impetuous victor, Lord of our hymns, with beauteousjaws, the Hero,  Render of kine-stalls, car-borne, thunder-wielding, so pierce thy way to wondrous strength, O Indra.

6.17.d: एवा पाहि परत्नथा मन्दतु तवा शरुधि बरह्म वाव्र्धस्वोतगीर्भिः | आविः सूर्यं कर्णुहि पीपिहीषो जहि शत्रून्रभि गा इन्द्र तर्न्धि ||
6.17.e: Drink as of old, and let the draught delight thee. hear thou our prayer and let our songs exalt thee.  Make the Sun visible, make food abundant, slaughter the foes, pierce through and free the cattle.

6.17.d: ते तवा मदा बर्हदिन्द्र सवधाव इमे पीता उक्षयन्त दयुमन्तम | महामनूनं तवसं विभूतिं मत्सरासो जर्ह्र्षन्त परसाहम ||
6.17.e: These gladdening drops, O Indra, Self-sustainer, quaffed shall augment thee in thy mighty splendour.  Yea, let the cheering drops delight thee greatly, great, perfect, strong, powerful, all-subduing.

6.17.d: येभिः सूर्यमुषसं मन्दसानो.अवासयो.अप दर्ल्हानि दर्द्रत | महामद्रिं परि गा इन्द्र सन्तं नुत्था अच्युतं सदसस परि सवात ||
6.17.e: Gladdened whereby, bursting the firm enclosures, thou gavest splendour to the Sun and Morning.  The mighty rock that compassed in the cattle, ne’er moved, thou shookest from its seat, O Indra.

6.17.d: तव करत्वा तव तद दंसनाभिरामासु पक्वं शच्या नि दीधः | और्णोर्दुर उस्रियाभ्यो वि दर्ळ्होदूर्वाद गा अस्र्जो अङगिरस्वान ||
6.17.e: Thou with thy wisdom, power, and works of wonder, hast stored the ripe milk in the raw cows' udders  Unbarred the firm doors for the kine of Morning, and, with the Aṅgirases, set free the cattle.

6.17.d: पप्राथ कषां महि दण्सो वयुर्वीमुप दयां रष्वो बर्हदिन्द्र सतभायः | अधारयो रोदसी देवपुत्रे परत्ने मातरा यह्वी रतस्य ||
6.17.e: Thou hast spread out wide earth, a mighty marvel, and, high thyself, propped lofty heaven, O Indra.  Both worlds, whose Sons are Gods, thou hast supported, young, Mothers from old time ofholy Order.

6.17.d: अध तवा विश्वे पुर इन्द्र देवा एकं तवसं दधिरे भराय | अदेवो यदभ्यौहिष्ट देवान सवर्षाता वर्णत इन्द्रमत्र ||
6.17.e: Yea, Indra, all the Deities installed thee their one strong Champion in the van for battle.  What time the godless was the Gods’ assailant, Indra they chose to win the light of heaven.

6.17.d: अध दयौश्चित ते अप सा नु वज्राद दवितानमद भियसा सवस्य मन्योः | अहिं यदिन्द्रो अभ्योहसानं नि चिद विश्वायुः शयथे जघान ||
6.17.e: Yea, e’en that heaven itself of old bent backward before thy bolt, in terror of its anger,  When Indra, life of every living creature, smote down within his lair the assailing Dragon.

6.17.d: अध तवष्टा ते मह उग्र वज्रं सहस्रभ्र्ष्टिं वव्र्तच्छताश्रिम | निकाममरमणसं येन नवन्तमहिं सं पिणग्र्जीषिन ||
6.17.e: Yea, Strong One! Tvaṣṭar turned for thee, the Mighty, the bolt with thousand spikes and hundred edges,  Eager and prompt at will, wherewith thou crushedst the boasting Dragon, O impetuous Hero.

6.17.d: वर्धान यं विश्वे मरुतः सजोषाः पचच्छतं महिषानिन्द्र तुभ्यम | पूषा विष्णुस्त्रीणि सरांसि धावन वर्त्रहणं मदिरमंशुमस्मै ||
6.17.e: He dressed a hundred buffaloes, O Indra, for thee whom all accordant Maruts strengthen.  He, Pūṣan Viṣṇu, poured forth three great vessels to him, the juice that cheers, that slaughters Vṛtra.

6.17.d: आ कषोदो महि वर्तं नदीनां परिष्ठितमस्र्ज ऊर्मिमपाम | तासामनु परवत इन्द्र पन्थां परार्दयो नीचीरपसः समुद्रम ||
6.17.e: Thou settest free the rushing wave of waters, the floods' great swell encompassed and obstructed.  Along steep slopes their course thou tumedst, Indra, directed downward, speeding to the ocean.

6.17.d: एवा ता विश्वा चक्र्वांसमिन्द्रं महामुग्रमजुर्यं सहोदाम | सुवीरं तवा सवायुधं सुवज्रमा बरह्म नव्यमवसे वव्र्त्यात ||
6.17.e: So may our new prayer bring thee to protect us, thee well-armed Hero with thy bolt of thunder,  Indra, who made these worlds, the Strong, the ty, who never groweth old, the victory-giver.

6.17.d: स नो वाजाय शरवस इषे च राये धेहि दयुमत इन्द्र विप्रान | भरद्वाजे नर्वत इन्द्र सूरीन दिवि च समैधि पार्ये न इन्द्र ||
6.17.e: So, Indra, form us brilliant holy singers for strength, for glory, and for food and riches.  Give Bharadvāja hero patrons, Indra Indra, be ours upon the day of trial.

6.17.d: अया वाजं देवहितं सनेम मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ||
6.17.e: With this may we obtain strength God-appointed, and brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.18.d: तमु षटुहि यो अभिभूत्योजा वन्वन्नवातः पुरुहूत इन्द्रः | अषाळ्हमुग्रं सहमानमाभिर्गीर्भिर्वर्ध वर्षभं चर्षणीनाम ||
6.18.e: GLORIFY him whose might is all-surpassing, Indra the much-invoked who fights uninjured.  Magnify with these songs the never-vanquished, the Strong, the Bull of men, the Mighty Victor.

6.18.d: स युध्मः सत्वा खजक्र्त समद्वा तुविम्रक्षो नदनुमान रजीषी | बर्हद्रेणुश्च्यवनो मानुषीणामेकः कर्ष्टीनामभवत सहावा ||
6.18.e: He, Champion, Hero, Warrior, Lord of battles, impetuous, loudly roaring, great destroyer,  Who whirls the dust on high, alone, oerthrower, hath made all races of mankind his subjects.

6.18.d: तवं ह नु तयददमायो दस्यून्रेकः कर्ष्टीरवनोरार्याय | अस्ति सविन नु वीर्यं तत त इन्द्र न सविदस्ति तद रतुथा वि वोचः ||
6.18.e: Thou, thou alone, hast tamed the Dasyus; singly thou hast subdued the people for the Ārya.  In this, or is it not, thine hero exploit, Indra? Declare it at the proper season.

6.18.d: सदिद धि ते तुविजातस्य मन्ये सहः सहिष्ठ तुरतस्तुरस्य | उग्रमुग्रस्य तवसस्तवीयो.अरध्रस्य रध्रतुरो बभूव ||
6.18.e: For true, I deem, thy strength is, thine the Mighty, thine, O Most Potent, thine the Conquering Victor;  Strong, of the strong, Most Mighty, of the mighty, thine, driver of the churl to acts of bounty.

6.18.d: तन नः परत्नं सख्यमस्तु युष्मे इत्था वदद्भिर्वलमङगिरोभिः | हन्नच्युतच्युद दस्मेषयन्तं रणोः पुरो वि दुरोस्य विश्वाः ||
6.18.e: Be this our ancient bond of friendship with you and with Aṅgirases here who speak of Vala.  Thou, Wondrous, Shaker of things firm, didst smite him in his fresh strength, and force his doors and castles.

6.18.d: स हि धीभिर्हव्यो अस्त्युग्र ईशानक्र्न महति वर्त्रतूर्ये | स तोकसाता तनये स वज्री वितन्तसाय्यो अभवत समत्सु ||
6.18.e: With holy thoughts must he be called, the Mighty, showing his power in the great fight with Vṛtra.  He must be called to give us seed and offspring, the Thunderer must he moved and sped to battle.

6.18.d: स मज्मना जनिम मानुषाणाममर्त्येन नाम्नाति पर सर्स्रे | स दयुम्नेन स शवसोत राया स वीर्येण नर्तमः समोकाः ||
6.18.e: He in his might, with name that lives for ever, hath far surpassed all human generations.  He, most heroic, hath his home with splendour, with glory and with riches and with valour.

6.18.d: स यो न मुहे न मिथू जनो भूत सुमन्तुनामा चुमुरिं धुनिं च | वर्णक पिप्रुं शम्बरं शुष्णमिन्द्रः पुरांच्यौत्नाय शयथाय नू चित ||
6.18.e: Stranger to guile, who ne’er was false or faithless, bearing a name that may be well remembered,  Indra crushed Cumuri, Dhuni, Śambara, Pipru, and Śuṣṇa, that their castles fell in ruin.

6.18.d: उदावता तवक्षसा पन्यसा च वर्त्रहत्याय रथमिन्द्र तिष्ठ | धिष्व वज्रं हस्त आ दक्षिणत्राभि पर मन्द पुरुदत्र मायाः ||
6.18.e: With saving might that must be praised and lauded, Indra, ascend thy car to smite down Vṛtra.  In thy right hand hold fast thy bolt of thunder, and weaken, Bounteous Lord, his art and magic.

6.18.d: अग्निर्न शुष्कं वनमिन्द्र हेती रक्षो नि धक्ष्यशनिर्न भीमा | गम्भीरय रष्वया यो रुरोजाध्वानयद दुरिता दम्भयच्च ||
6.18.e: As Agni, as the dart burns the dry forest, like the dread shaft burn down the fiends, O Indra;  Thou who with high deep-reaching spear hast broken, hast covered over mischief and destroyed it.

6.18.d: आ सहस्रं पथिभिरिन्द्र राया तुविद्युम्न तुविवाजेभिरर्वाक | याहि सूनो सहसो यस्य नू चिददेव ईशे पुरुहूत योतोः ||
6.18.e: With wealth, by thousand paths come hither, Agni, paths that bring ample strength, O thou Most Splendid.  Come, Son of Strength, o’er whom, Invoked of many! the godless hath no power to keep thee distant.

6.18.d: पर तुविद्युम्नस्य सथविरस्य घर्ष्वेर्दिवो ररप्शे महिमा पर्थिव्याः | नास्य शत्रुर्न परतिमानमस्ति न परतिष्ठिःपुरुमायस्य सह्योः ||
6.18.e: From heaven, from earth is bruited forth the greatness of him the firm, the fiery, the resplendent.  No foe hath he, no counterpart, no refuge is there from him the Conqueror full of wisdom

6.18.d: पर तत ते अद्या करणं कर्तं भूत कुत्सं यदायुमतिथिग्वमस्मै | पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशा अभि कषामुत तूर्वयाणं धर्षता निनेथ ||
6.18.e: This day the deed that thou hast done is famous, when thou, for him, with many thousand others  Laidest low Kutsa, Āyu, Atithigva, and boldly didst deliver Tūrvayāṇa.

6.18.d: अनु तवाहिघ्ने अध देव देवा मदन विश्वे कवितमं कवीनाम | करो यत्र वरिवो बाधिताय दिवे जनाय तन्वे गर्णानः ||
6.18.e: In thee, O God, the wisest of the Sages, all Gods were joyful when thou slewest Ahi.  When lauded for thyself, thou gavest freedom to sore-afflicted Heaven and to the people.

6.18.d: अनु दयावाप्र्थिवी तत त ओजो.अमर्त्या जिहत इन्द्र देवाः | कर्ष्वा कर्त्नो अक्र्तं यत ते अस्त्युक्थं नवीयो जनयस्व यज्ञैः ||
6.18.e: This power of thine both heaven and earth acknowledge, the deathless Gods acknowledge it, O Indra.  Do what thou ne’er hast done, O Mighty Worker: beget a new hymn at thy sacrifices.

6.19.d: महानिन्द्रो नर्वदा चर्षणिप्रा उत दविबर्हा अमिनः सहोभिः | अस्मद्र्यग वाव्र्धे विर्यायोरुः पर्थुः सुक्र्तः कर्त्र्भिर्भूत ||
6.19.e: GREAT, hero-like controlling men is Indra, unwasting in his powers, doubled in vastness.  He, turned to us, hath grown to hero vigour: broad, wide, he hath been decked by those who serve him.

6.19.d: इन्द्रमेव धिषणा सातये धाद बर्हन्तं रष्वमजरं युवानम | अषाळ्हेन सवसा शूशुवांसं सद्यश्चिद यो वाव्र्धे असामि ||
6.19.e: The bowl made Indra swift to gather booty, the High, the Lofty, Youthful, Undecaying,  Him who hath waxed by strength which none may conquer, and even at once grown to complete perfection.

6.19.d: पर्थू करस्ना बहुला गभस्ती अस्मद्र्यक सं मिमीहि शरवांसि | यूथेव पश्वः पशुपा दमूना अस्मानिन्द्राभ्या वव्र्त्स्वाजौ ||
6.19.e: Stretch out those hands of thine, extend to us-ward thy wide capacious arms, and grant us glory.  Like as the household herdsman guards the cattle, so move thou round about us in the combat.

6.19.d: तं व इन्द्रं चतिनमस्य शाकैरिह नूनं वाजयन्तो हुवेम | यथा चित पूर्वे जरितार आसुरनेद्या अनवद्या अरिष्टाः ||
6.19.e: Now, fain for strength, let us invite your Indra hither, who lieth hidden with his Heroes,—  Free from all blame, without reproach, uninjured, e’en as were those who sang, of old, his praises.

6.19.d: धर्तव्रतो धनदाः सोमव्र्द्धः स हि वामस्य वसुनः पुरुक्षुः | सं जग्मिरे पथ्या रायो अस्मिन समुद्रे न सिन्धवो यादमानाः ||
6.19.e: With steadfast laws, wealth-giver, strong through Soma, he hath much fair and precious food to feed us.  In him unite all paths that lead to riches, like rivers that commingle with the ocean.

6.19.d: शविष्ठं न आ भर शूर शव ओजिष्ठमोजो अभिभूतौग्रम | विश्वा दयुम्ना वर्ष्ण्या मानुषाणामस्मभ्यं दाहरिवो मादयध्यै ||
6.19.e: Bring unto us the mightiest might, O Hero, strong and most potent force, thou great Subduer!  All splendid vigorous powers of men vouchsafe us, Lord of Bay Steeds, that they may make us joyful.

6.19.d: यस्ते मदः पर्तणाषाळ अम्र्ध्र इन्द्र तं न आ भर शूशुवांसम | येन तोकस्य तनयस्य सातौ मंसीमहि जिगीवांसस्त्वोताः ||
6.19.e: Bring us, grown mighty in its strength, O Indra, thy friendly rapturous joy that wins the battle,  Wherewith by thee assisted and triumphant, we may laud thee in gaining seed and offspring.

6.19.d: आ नो भर वर्षणं शुष्ममिन्द्र धनस्प्र्तं शूशुवांसं सुदक्षम | येन वंसाम पर्तनासु शत्रून तवोतिभिरुत जामीन्रजामीन ||
6.19.e: Indra, bestow on us the power heroic skilled and exceeding strong, that wins the booty,  Wherewith, by thine assistance, we may conquer our foes in battle, be they kin or stranger.

6.19.d: आ ते शुष्मो वर्षभ एतु पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा पुरस्तात | आ विश्वतो अभि समेत्वर्वां इन्द्र दयुम्नं सवर्वद धेह्यस्मे ||
6.19.e: Let thine heroic strength come from behind us, before us, from above us or below us.  From every side may it approach us, Indra. Give us the glory of the realm of splendour.

6.19.d: नर्वत त इन्द्र नर्तमाभिरूती वंसीमहि वामं शरोमतेभिः | ईक्षे हि वस्व उभयस्य राजन धा रत्नं महि सथूरं बर्हन्तम ||
6.19.e: With most heroic aid from thee, like heroes Indra, may we win wealth by deeds glory.  Thou, King, art Lord of earthly, heavenly treasure: vouchsafe us riches vast, sublime, and lasting.
The Bull, whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the Celestial Ruler,  Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.

6.19.d: जनं वज्रिन महि चिन मन्यमानमेभ्यो नर्भ्यो रन्धया येष्वस्मि | अधा हि तवा पर्थिव्यां शूरसातौ हवामहे तनयेगोष्वप्सु ||
6.19.e: Give up the people who are high and haughty to these men and to me, O Thunder-wielder!  Therefore upon the earth do we invoke thee, where heroes win, for sons and kine and waters.

6.19.d: वयं त एभिः पुरुहूत सख्यैः शत्रोः-शत्रोरुत्तर इत्स्याम | घनन्तो वर्त्राण्युभयानि शूर राया मदेम बर्हतात्वोताः ||
6.19.e: Through these thy friendships, God invoked of many! may we be victors over every foeman.  Slaying both kinds of foe, may we, O Hero, be happy, helped by thee, with ample riches.

6.20.d: दयौर्न य इन्द्राभि भूमार्यस्तस्थौ रयिः शवसा पर्त्सु जनान | तं नः सहस्रभरमुर्वरासां दद्धि सूनो सहसो वर्त्रतुरम ||
6.20.e: GIVE us wealth, Indra, that with might, as heaven o’ertops the earth, o’ercomes our foes in battle  Wealth that brings thousands and that wins the corn-lands, wealth, Son of Strength! that vanquishes the foeman.

6.20.d: दिवो न तुभ्यमन्विन्द्र सत्रासुर्यं देवेभिर्धायि विश्वम | अहिं यद वर्त्रमपो वव्रिवांसं हन्न्र्जीषिन विष्णुनासचानः ||
6.20.e: Even as the power of Dyaus, to thee, O Indra, all Asura sway was by the Gods entrusted,  When thou, Impetuous! leagued with Viṣṇu, slewest Vṛtra the Dragon who enclosed the waters.

6.20.d: तूर्वन्नोजीयान तवसस्तवीयान कर्तब्रह्मेन्द्रो वर्द्धमहाः | राजाभवन मधुनः सोम्यस्य विश्वासां यत पुरां दर्त्नुमावत ||
6.20.e: Indra, Strong, Victor, Mightier than the mighty, addressed with prayer and perfect in his splendour,  Lord of the bolt that breaketh forts in pieces, became the King of the sweet juice of Soma..

6.20.d: शतैरपद्रन पणय इन्द्रात्र दशोणये कवये.अर्कसातौ | वधैः शुष्णस्याशुषस्य मायाः पित्वो नारिरेचीत किंचन पर ||
6.20.e: There, Indra, while the light was won, the Paṇis f1ed, 'neath a hundred blows, for wise Dasoni,  And greedy Śuṣṇa's magical devices nor left he any of their food remaining.

6.20.d: महो दरुहो अप विश्वायु धायि वज्रस्य यत पतने पादि शुष्णः | उरु ष सरथं सारथये करिन्द्रः कुत्साय सूर्यस्य सातौ ||
6.20.e: What time the thunder fell and Śuṣṇa perished, all life's support from the great Druh was taken.  Indra made room for his car-drivcr Kutsa who sate beside him, when he gained the sunlight.

6.20.d: पर शयेनो न मदिरमंशुमस्मै शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन | परावन नमीं साप्यं ससन्तं पर्णग राया समिषा सं सवस्ति ||
6.20.e: As the Hawk rent for him the stalk that gladdens, he wrenched the head from Namuci the Dāsa.  He guarded Nam, Sayya's son, in slumber, and sated him with food, success, and riches.

6.20.d: वि पिप्रोरहिमायस्य दर्ळ्हाः पुरो वज्रिञ्छवसा न दर्दः | सुदामन तद रेक्णो अप्रम्र्ष्यं रजिश्वने दात्रं दाशुषे दाः ||
6.20.e: Thou, thunder-armed, with thy great might hast shattered Pipru's strong forts who knew the wiles of serpents.  Thou gavest to thy worshipper Ṛjiśvan imperishable Wealth, O Bounteous Giver.

6.20.d: स वेतसुं दशमायं दशोणिं तूतुजिमिन्द्रः सवभिष्टिसुम्नः | आ तुग्रं शश्वदिभं दयोतनाय मातुर्न सीमुप सर्जा इयध्यै ||
6.20.e: The crafty Vetasu, the swift Dasni, and Tugra speedily with all his servants,  Hath Indra, gladdening with strong assistance, forced near as ’twere to glorify the Mother.

6.20.d: स ईं सप्र्धो वनते अप्रतीतो बिभ्रद वज्रं वर्त्रहणं गभस्तौ | तिष्ठद धरी अध्यस्तेव गर्ते वचोयुजा वहत इन्द्रं रष्वम ||
6.20.e: Resistless, with the hosts he battles, bearing in both his arms the Vṛtra-slaying thunder.  He mounts his Bays, as the car-seat an archer: yoked at a word they bear the lofty Indra.

6.20.d: सनेम ते.अवसा नव्य इन्द्र पर पूरव सतवन्त एना यज्ञैः | सप्त यत पुरः शर्म शारदीर्दर्द धन दासीः पुरुकुत्साय शिक्षन ||
6.20.e: May we, O Indra, gain by thy new favour: so Parus laud thee, with their sacrifices,  That thou hast wrecked seven autumn forts, their shelter, slain Dāsa tribes and aided Purukutsa.

6.20.d: तवं वर्ध इन्द्र पूर्व्यो भूर्वरिवस्यन्नुशने काव्याय | परा नववास्त्वमनुदेयं महे पित्रे ददाथ सवं नपातम ||
6.20.e: Favouring Uśanā the son of Kavi, thou wast his ancient strengthener, O Indra.  Thou gavest Navavāstva. as a present, to the great father gavest back his grandson.
Thou, roaring Indra, drovest on the waters that made a roaring sound like rushing rivers,  What time, O Hero, o’er the sea thou broughtest, in safety broughtest Turvaśa and Yadu.

6.20.d: तव ह तयदिन्द्र विष्वमाजौ सस्तो धुनीचुमुरी या ह सिष्वप | दीदयदित तुभ्यं सोमेभिः सुन्वन दभीतिरिध्मभ्र्तिः पक्थ्यर्कैः ||
6.20.e: This Indra, was thy work in war: thou sentest Dhuni and Cumuri to sleep and slumber.  Dabhīti lit the flame for thee, and worshipped with fuel, hymns, poured Soma, dressed oblations.

6.21.d: इमा उ तवा पुरुतमस्य कारोर्हव्यं वीर हव्या हवन्ते | धियो रथेष्ठामजरं नवीयो रयिर्विभूतिरीयते वचस्या ||
6.21.e: THESE the most constant singer's invocations call thee who art to be invoked, O Hero;  Hymns call anew the chariot-borne, Eternal: by eloquence men gain abundant riches.

6.21.d: तमु सतुष इन्द्रं यो विदानो गिर्वाहसं गीर्भीर्यज्ञव्र्द्धम | यस्य दिवमति मह्ना पर्थिव्याः पुरुमायस्य रिरिचेमहित्वम ||
6.21.e: I praise that Indra, known to all men, honoured with songs, extolled with hymns at sacrifices,  Whose majesty, rich in wondrous arts, surpasseth the magnitude of earth, and heaven in greatness.

6.21.d: स इत तमो.अवयुनं ततन्वत सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार | कदा ते मर्ता अम्र्तस्य धामेयक्षन्तो न मिनन्ति सवधावः ||
6.21.e: He hath made pathways, with the Sun to aid him, throughout the darkness that extended pathless.  Mortals who yearn to worship ne’er dishonour, O Mighty God, thy Law who art Immortal.

6.21.d: यस्ता चकार स कुह सविदिन्द्रः कमा जनं चरति कासु विक्षु | कस्ते यज्ञो मनसे शं वराय को अर्क इन्द्रकतमः स होता ||
6.21.e: And he who did these things, where is that Indra? among what tribes? what people doth he visit?  What sacrifice contents thy mind , and wishes? What priest among them all? what hymn, O Indra?

6.21.d: इदा हि ते वेविषतः पुराजाः परत्नास आसुः पुरुक्र्त सखायः | ये मध्यमास उत नूतनास उतावमस्य पुरुहूत बोधि ||
6.21.e: Yea, here were they who, born of old, have served thee, thy friends of ancient time, thou active Worker.  Bethink thee now of these, Invoked of many! the midmost and the recent, and the youngest.

6.21.d: तं पर्छन्तो.अवरासः पराणि परत्ना त इन्द्र शरुत्यानु येमुः | अर्चामसि वीर बरह्मवाहो यादेव विद्म तात तवा महान्तम ||
6.21.e: Inquiring after him, thy later servants, Indra, have gained thy former old traditions.  Hero, to whom the prayer is brought, we praise thee as great for that wherein we know thee mighty.

6.21.d: अभि तवा पाजो रक्षसो वि तस्थे महि जज्ञानमभि तत सु तिष्ठ | तव परत्नेन युज्येन सख्या वज्रेण धर्ष्णो अपता नुदस्व ||
6.21.e: The demon's strength is gathered fast against thee: great as that strength hath grown, go forth to meet it.  With thine own ancient friend and companion, the thunderbolt, brave Champion! drive it backward.

6.21.d: स तु शरुधीन्द्र नूतनस्य बरह्मण्यतो वीर कारुधायः | तवं हयापिः परदिवि पितॄणां शश्वद बभूथ सुहव एष्टौ ||
6.21.e: Hear, too, the prayer of this thy present beadsman, O Indra, Hero, cherishing the singer.  For thou wast aye our fathers' Friend aforetime, still swift to listen to their supplication.

6.21.d: परोतये वरुणं मित्रमिन्द्रं मरुतः कर्ष्वावसे नो अद्य | पर पूषणं विष्णुमग्निं पुरन्धिं सवितारमोषधीः पर्वतांश्च ||
6.21.e: Bring to our help this day, for our protection, Varuṇa, Mitra , Indra, and the Maruts,  Pūṣan and Viṣṇu, Agni and Purandhi, Savitar also, and the Plants and Mountains.

6.21.d: इम उ तवा पुरुशाक परयज्यो जरितारो अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः | शरुधी हवमा हुवतो हुवानो न तवावानन्यो अम्र्त तवदस्ति ||
6.21.e: The singers here exalt with hymns and praises thee who art very Mighty and Most Holy.  Hear, when invoked, the invoker's invocation. Beside thee there is nonelike thee, Immortal!

6.21.d: नू म आ वाचमुप याहि विद्वान विश्वेभिः सूनो सहसो यजत्रैः | ये अग्निजिह्वा रतसाप आसुर्ये मनुं चक्रुरुपरं दसाय ||
6.21.e: Now to my words come quickly thou who knowest, O Son of Strength, with all who claim our worship,  Who visit sacred rites, whose tongue is Agni, Gods who made Manu stronger than the Dasyu.

6.21.d: स नो बोधि पुरेता सुगेषूत दुर्गेषु पथिक्र्द विदानः | ये अश्रमास उरवो वहिष्ठास्तेभिर्न इन्द्राभि वक्षि वाजम ||
6.21.e: On good and evil ways be thou our Leader, thou who art known to all as Path-preparer.  Bring power to us, O Indra, with thy Horses, Steeds that are best to draw, broad-backed, unwearied.

6.22.d: य एक इद धव्यश्चर्षणीनामिन्द्रं तं गीर्भिरभ्यर्च आभिः | यः पत्यते वर्षभो वर्ष्ण्यावान सत्यः सत्वा पुरुमायः सहस्वान ||
6.22.e: WITH these my hymns I glorify that Indra who is alone to be invoked by mortals,  The Lord, the Mighty One, of manly vigour, victorious, Hero, true, and full of wisdom.

6.22.d: तमु नः पूर्वे पितरो नवग्वाः सप्त विप्रासो अभि वाजयन्तः | नक्षद्दाभं ततुरिं पर्वतेष्ठामद्रोघवाचं मतिभिः शविष्ठम ||
6.22.e: Our sires of old,. Navagvas, sages seven, while urging him to show his might, extolled him,  Dwelling on heights, swift, smiting down opponents, guileless in word, and in his thoughts most mighty.

6.22.d: तमीमह इन्द्रमस्य रायः पुरुवीरस्य नर्वतः पुरुक्षोः | यो अस्क्र्धोयुरजरः सवर्वान तमा भर हरिवो मादयध्यै ||
6.22.e: We seek that Indra to obtain his riches that bring much food, and men, and store of heroes.  Bring us, Lord of Bay Steeds, to make us joyful, celestial wealth, abundant, undecaying.

6.22.d: तन नो वि वोचो यदि ते पुरा चिज्जरितार आनशुः सुम्नमिन्द्र | कस्ते भागः किं वयो दुध्र खिद्वः पुरुहूत पुरूवसो.असुरघ्नः ||
6.22.e: Tell thou us this, if at thy hand aforetime the earlier singers have obtained good fortune,  What is thy share and portion, Strong Subduer, Asura-slayer, rich, invoked of many?

6.22.d: तं पर्छन्ती वज्रहस्तं रथेष्ठामिन्द्रं वेपी वक्वरीयस्य नू गीः | तुविग्राभं तुविकूर्मिं रभोदां गातुमिषे नक्षते तुम्रमछ ||
6.22.e: He who for car-borne Indra, armed with thunder, hath a hymn, craving, deeply-piercing, fluent,  Who sends a song effectual, firmly-grasping, and strength-bestowing, he comes near the mighty.

6.22.d: अया ह तयं मायया वाव्र्धानं मनोजुवा सवतवः पर्वतेन | अच्युता चिद वीळिता सवोजो रुजो वि दर्ळ्हा धर्षता विरप्शिन ||
6.22.e: Strong of thyself, thou by this art hast shattered, with thought-swift Parvata, him who waxed against thee,  And, Mightiest! roaring! boldly rent in pieces things that were firmly fixed and never shaken.

6.22.d: तं वो धिया नव्यस्या शविष्ठं परत्नं परत्नवत परितंसयध्यै | स नो वक्षदनिमानः सुवह्मेन्द्रो विश्वान्यतिदुर्गहाणि ||
6.22.e: Him will we fit for you with new devotion, the strongest Ancient One, in ancient manner.  So may that Indra, boundless, faithful Leader, conduct us o’er all places hard to traverse.

6.22.d: आ जनाय दरुह्वणे पार्थिवानि दिव्यानि दीपयो.अन्तरिक्षा | तपा वर्षन विश्वतः शोचिषा तान बरह्मद्विषे शोचय कषामपश्च ||
6.22.e: Thou for the people who oppress hast kindled the earthly firmament and that of heaven.  With heat, O Bull, on every side consume them: heat earth and flood for him who hates devotion.

6.22.d: भुवो जनस्य दिव्यस्य राजा पार्थिवस्य जगतस्त्वेषसन्द्र्क | धिष्व वज्रं दक्षिण इन्द्र हस्ते विश्वा अजुर्य दयसे वि मायाः ||
6.22.e: Of all the Heavenly Folk, of earthly creatures thou art the King, O God of splendid aspect.  In thy right hand, O Indra, grasp die thunder: Eternal! thou destroyest all enchantments.

6.22.d: आ संयतमिन्द्र णः सवस्तिं शत्रुतूर्याय बर्हतीमम्र्ध्राम | यया दासान्यार्याणि वर्त्रा करो वज्रिन सुतुका नाहुषाणि ||
6.22.e: Give us confirmed prosperity, O Indra, vast and exhaustless for the foe's subduing.  Strengthen therewith the Ārya's hate and Dāsa's, and let the arms of Nahusas be mighty.

6.22.d: स नो नियुद्भिः पुरुहूत वेधो विश्ववाराभिरा गहि परयज्यो | न या अदेवो वरते न देव आभिर्याहि तूयमा मद्र्यद्रिक ||
6.22.e: Come with thy team which brings all blessings hither, Disposer, much-invoked, exceeding holy.  Thou whom no fiend, no God can stay or hinder, come swittly with these Steeds in my direction.

6.23.d: सुत इत तवं निमिश्ल इन्द्र सोमे सतोमे बरह्मणि शस्यमानौक्थे | यद वा युक्ताभ्यां मघवन हरिभ्यां बिभ्रद वज्रम्बाह्वोरिन्द्र यासि ||
6.23.e: THOU art attached to pressed-out Soma, Indra, at laud, at prayer, and when the hymn is chanted;  Or when with yoked Bays, Maghavan, thou comest, O Indra, bearing in thine arms the thunder.

6.23.d: यद वा दिवि पार्ये सुष्विमिन्द्र वर्त्रहत्ये.अवसि शूरसातौ | यद वा दक्षस्य बिभ्युषो अबिभ्यदरन्धयः शर्धत इन्द्र दस्यून ||
6.23.e: Or when on that decisive day thou holpest the presser of the juice at Vṛtra's slaughter;  Or when thou, while the strong one feared, undaunted, gavest to death, Indra, the daring Dasyus.

6.23.d: पाता सुतमिन्द्रो अस्तु सोमं परणेनीरुग्रो जरितारमूती | कर्ता वीराय सुष्वय उ लोकं दाता वसु सतुवते कीरये चित ||
6.23.e: Let Indra drink the pressed-out Soma, Helper and mighty Guide of him who sings his praises.  He gives the hero room who pours oblations, and treasure even to the lowly singer.

6.23.d: गन्तेयान्ति सवना हरिभ्यां बभ्रिर्वज्रं पपिः सोमं ददिर्गाः | कर्ता वीरं नर्यं सर्ववीरं शरोता हवंग्र्णत सतोमवाहाः ||
6.23.e: E’en humble rites with his Bay steeds he visits: he wields the bolt, drinks Soma, gives us cattle.  He makes the valiant rich in store of heroes, accepts our praise and hears the singer's calling.
