6.23.d: अस्मै वयं यद वावान तद विविष्म इन्द्राय यो नः परदिवो अपस कः | सुते सोमे सतुमसि शंसदुक्थेन्द्राय बरह्म वर्धनं यथासत ||
6.23.e: What he hath longed for we have brought to Indra, who from the days of old hath done us service.  While Soma flows we will sing hymn, and laud him, so that our prayer may streng. then Indra's vigour.

6.23.d: बरह्माणि हि चक्र्षे वर्धनानि तावत त इन्द्र मतिभिर्विविष्मः | सुते सोमे सुतपाः शन्तमानि रान्द्र्या करियास्म वक्षणानि यज्ञैः ||
6.23.e: Thou hast made prayer the means of thine exalting, therefore we wait on thee with hymns, O Indra.  May we, by the pressed Soma, Somadrinker! bring thee, with sacrifice, blissful sweet refreshment.

6.23.d: स नो बोधि पुरोळाशं रराणः पिबा तु सोमं गोर्जीकमिन्द्र | एदं बर्हिर्यजमानस्य सीदोरुं कर्धि तवायत उ लोकम ||
6.23.e: Mark well our sacrificial cake, delighted Indra, drink Soma and the milk commingled.  Here on the sacrificer's grass be seated: give ample room to thy devoted servant.

6.23.d: स मन्दस्वा हयनु जोषमुग्र पर तवा यज्ञास इमे अश्नुवन्तु | परेमे हवासः पुरुहूतमस्मे आ तवेयं धीरवस इन्द्र यम्याः ||
6.23.e: O Mighty One, be joyful as thou willest. Let these our sacrifices reach and find thee;  And may this hymn and these our invocations turn thee, whom many men invoke, to help us.

6.23.d: तं वः सखायः सं यथा सुतेषु सोमेभिरीं पर्णता भोजमिन्द्रम | कुवित तस्मा असति नो भराय न सुष्विमिन्द्रो.अवसे मर्धाति ||
6.23.e: Friends, when thejuices flow, replenish duly your own, your bounteous Indra with the Soma.  Will it not aid him to support us? Indra. spares him who sheds the juice to win his favour.

6.23.d: एवेदिन्द्रः सुते अस्तावि सोमे भरद्वाजेषु कषयदिन मघोनः | असद यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिन्द्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता ||
6.23.e: While Soma flowed, thus Indra hath been lauded, Ruler of nobles, mid the Bharadvājas,  That Indra may become the singer's patron and give him wealth in every kind of treasure.

6.24.d: वर्षा मद इन्द्रे शलोक उक्था सचा सोमेषु सुतपा रजीषी | अर्चत्र्यो मघवा नर्भ्य उक्थैर्द्युक्षो राजा गिरामक्षितोतिः ||
6.24.e: STRONG rapturous joy, praise, glory are with Indra: impetuous God, he quaffs the juice of Soma:  That Maghavan whom men must laud with singing, Heaven-dweller, King of songs, whose help is lasting.

6.24.d: ततुरिर्वीरो नर्यो विचेताः शरोता हवं गर्णत उर्व्यूतिः | वसुः शंसो नरां कारुधाया वाजी सतुतो विदथे दाति वाजम ||
6.24.e: He, Friend of man, most wise, victorious Hero, hears, with far-reaching aid, the singer call him.  Excellent, Praise of Men, the bard's Supporter, Strong, he gives strength, extolled in holy synod.

6.24.d: अक्षो न चक्र्योः शूर बर्हन पर ते मह्ना रिरिचे रोदस्योः | वर्क्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया वयूतयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ||
6.24.e: The lofty axle of thy wheels, O Hero, is not surpassed by heaven and earth in greatness.  Like branches of a tree, Invoked of many manifold aids spring forth from thee, O Indra.

6.24.d: शचीवतस्ते पुरुशाक शाका गवामिव सरुतयः संचरणीः | वत्सानां न तन्तयस्त इन्द्र दामन्वन्तो अदामानः सुदामन ||
6.24.e: Strong Lord, thine energies, endowed with vigour, are like the paths of kine converging homeward.  Like bonds of cord, Indra, that bind the younglings, no bonds are they, O thou of boundless bounty.

6.24.d: अन्यदद्य कर्वरमन्यदु शवो.असच्च सन मुहुराचक्रिरिन्द्रः | मित्रो नो अत्र वरुणश्च पूषार्यो वशस्य पर्येतास्ति ||
6.24.e: One act to-day, another act tomorrow oft Indra makes what is not yet existeni.  Here have we Mitra, Varuṇa, and Pūṣan to overcome the foeman's domination.

6.24.d: वि तवदापो न पर्वतस्य पर्ष्ठादुक्थेभिरिन्द्रानयन्त यज्ञैः | तं तवाभिः सुष्टुतिभिर्वाजयन्त आजिं न जग्मुर्गिर्वाहो अश्वाः ||
6.24.e: By song and sacrifice men brought the waters from thee, as from a mountain's ridge, O Indra.  Urging thy might, with these fair lauds they seek thee, O theme of song, as horses rush tobattle.

6.24.d: न यं जरन्ति शरदो न मासा न दयाव इन्द्रमवकर्शयन्ति | वर्द्धस्य चिद वर्धतामस्य तनू सतोमेभिरुक्थैश्चशस्यमाना ||
6.24.e: That Indra whom nor months nor autumn seasons wither with age, nor fleeting days enfeeble,—  Still may his body Wax, e’en now so mighty, glorified by the lauds and hymns that praise him.

6.24.d: न वीळवे नमते न सथिराय न शर्धते दस्युजूताय सतवान | अज्रा इन्द्रस्य गिरयश्चिद रष्वा गम्भीरे चिद भवतिगाधमस्मै ||
6.24.e: Extolled, he bends not to the strong, the steadfast, nor to the bold incited by the Dasyu.  High mountains are as level plains to Indra: even in the deep he finds firm ground to rest on.

6.24.d: गम्भीरेण न उरुणामत्रिन परेषो यन्धि सुतपावन वाजान | सथा ऊ षु ऊर्ध्व ऊती अरिषण्यन्नक्तोर्व्युष्टौ परितक्म्यायाम ||
6.24.e: Impetuous Speeder through all depth and distance, give strengthening food, thou drinker of the juices.  Stand up erect to help us, unreluctant, what time the gloom of night brightens to morning.

6.24.d: सचस्व नायमवसे अभीक इतो वा तमिन्द्र पाहि रिषः | अमा चैनमरण्ये पाहि रिषो मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ||
6.24.e: Hasting to help, come hither and protect him, keep him from harm when he is here, O Indra.  At home, abroad, from injury preserve him. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.25.d: या त ऊतिरवमा या परमा या मध्यमेन्द्र शुष्मिन्नस्ति | ताभिरू षु वर्त्रहत्ये.अवीर्न एभिश्च वाजैर्महान्न उग्र ||
6.25.e: WITH thine assistance, O thou Mighty Indra, be it the least, the midmost, or the highest,—  Great with those aids and by these powers support us, Strong God! in battle that subdues our foemen.

6.25.d: आभि सप्र्धो मिथतीररिषण्यन्नमित्रस्य वयथया मन्युमिन्द्र | आभिर्विश्वा अभियुजो विषूचीरार्याय विशो.अव तारीर्दासीः ||
6.25.e: With these discomfit hosts that fight against us, and check the opponent's wrath, thyself uninjured.  With these chase all our foes to every quarter: subdue the tribes of Dāsas to the Ārya.

6.25.d: इन्द्र जामय उत ये.अजामयो.अर्वाचीनासो वनुषो युयुज्रे | तवमेषां विथुरा शवांसि जहि वर्ष्ण्यानि कर्णुही पराचः ||
6.25.e: Those who array themselves as foes to smite us, O Indra, be they kin or be they strangers,—  Strike thou their manly strength that it be feeble, and drive in headlong flight our foemen backward.

6.25.d: शूरो वा शूरं वनते शरीरैस्तनूरुचा तरुषि यत कर्ण्वैते | तोके वा गोषु तनये यदप्सु वि करन्दसी उर्वरासु बरवैते ||
6.25.e: With strength of limb the hero slays the hero, when bright in arms they range them for the combat.  When two opposing hosts contend in battle for seed and offspring, waters, kine, or corn-lands.

6.25.d: नहि तवा शूरो न तुरो न धर्ष्णुर्न तवा योधो मन्यमानो युयोध | इन्द्र नकिष टवा परत्यस्त्येषां विश्वा जातान्यभ्यसि तानि ||
6.25.e: Yet no strong man hath conquered thee, no hero, no brave, no warrior trusting in his valour.  Not one of these is match for thee, O Indra. Thou far surpassest all these living creatures.

6.25.d: स पत्यत उभयोर्न्र्म्णमयोर्यदी वेधसः समिथे हवन्ते | वर्त्रे वा महो नर्वति कषये वा वयचस्वन्ता यदि वितन्तसैते ||
6.25.e: He is the Lord of both these armies' valour when the commanders call them to the conflict:  When with their ranks expanded they are fighting with a great foe or for a home with heroes.

6.25.d: अध समा ते चर्षणयो यदेजानिन्द्र तरातोत भवा वरूता | अस्माकासो ये नर्तमासो अर्य इन्द्र सूरयो दधिरे पुरोनः ||
6.25.e: And when the people stir themselves for battle, be thou their saviour, Indra, and protector,  And theirs, thy manliest of our friends, the pious, the chiefs who have installed us priests, O Indra.

6.25.d: अनु ते दायि मह इन्द्रियाय सत्रा ते विष्वमनु वर्त्रहत्ये | अनु कषत्रमनु सहो यजत्रेन्द्र देवेभिरनु ते नर्षह्ये ||
6.25.e: To thee for high dominion hath been for evermore, for slaughtering the Vṛtras,  All lordly power and might, O Holy Indra, given by Gods for victory in battle.

6.25.d: एवा न सप्र्धः समजा समत्स्विन्द्र रारन्धि मिथतीरदेवीः | विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गर्णन्तो भरद्वाजा उत त इन्द्र नूनम ||
6.25.e: So urge our hosts together in the combats: yield up the godless bands that fight against us.  Singing, at morn may we find thee with favour, yea, Indra, and e’en now, we Bharadvājas.

6.26.d: शरुधी न इन्द्र हवयामसि तवा महो वाजस्य सातौ वाव्र्षाणाः | सं यद विशो.अयन्त शूरसाता उग्रं नो.अवः पार्ये अहन दाः ||
6.26.e: O INDRA, hear us. Raining down the Soma, we call on thee to win us mighty valour.  Give us strong succour on the day of trial, when the tribes gather on the field of battle.

6.26.d: तवां वाजी हवते वाजिनेयो महो वाजस्य गध्यस्य सातौ | तवां वर्त्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं तरुत्रं तवां चष्टे मुष्टिहा गोषु युध्यन ||
6.26.e: The warrior, son of warrior sire, invokes thee, to gain great strength that may be won as booty:  To thee, the brave man's Lord, the fiends' subduer, he looks when fighting hand to hand for cattle.

6.26.d: तवं कविं चोदयो.अर्कसातौ तवं कुत्साय शुष्णं दाशुषे वर्क | तवं शिरो अमर्मणः पराहन्नतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन ||
6.26.e: Thou didst impel the sage to win the daylight, didst ruin Śuṣṇa for the pious Kutsa.  The invulnerable demon's head thou clavest when thou wouldst win the praise of Atithigva.

6.26.d: तवं रथं पर भरो योधं रष्वमावो युध्यन्तं वर्षभं दशद्युम | तवं तुग्रं वेतसवे सचाहन तवं तुजिं गर्णन्तमिन्द्र तूतोः ||
6.26.e: The lofty battle-car thou broughtest forward; thou holpest Dasadyu the strong when fighting.  Along with Vetasu thou slewest Tugra, and madest Tuji strong, who praised thee, Indra.

6.26.d: तवं तदुक्थमिन्द्र बर्हणा कः पर यच्छता सहस्राशूर दर्षि | अव गिरेर्दासं शम्बरं हन परावो दिवोदासं चित्राभिरूती ||
6.26.e: Thou madest good the laud, what time thou rentest a hundred thousand fighting foes, O Hero,  Slewest the Dāsa Śambara of the mountain, and with strange aids didst succour Divodāsa.

6.26.d: तवं शरद्धाभिर्मन्दसानः सोमैर्दभीतये चुमुरिमिन्द्रसिष्वप | तवं रजिं पिठीनसे दशस्यन षष्टिं सहस्राशच्या सचाहन ||
6.26.e: Made glad with Soma-draughts and faith, thou sentest Cumuri to his sleep, to please Dabhīti.  Thou, kindly giving Raji to Pithinas, slewest with might, at once, the sixty thousand.

6.26.d: अहं चन तत सूरिभिरानश्यां तव जयाय इन्द्र सुम्नमोजः | तवया यत सतवन्ते सधवीर वीरास्त्रिवरूथेन नहुषा शविष्ठ ||
6.26.e: May I too, with the liberal chiefs, O Indra, acquire thy blin supreme and domination,  When, Mightiest! Hero-girt! Nahuṣa heroes boast them in thee, the triply-strong Defender.

6.26.d: वयं ते अस्यामिन्द्र दयुम्नहूतौ सखायः सयाम महिन परेष्ठाः | परातर्दनिः कषत्रश्रीरस्तु शरेष्ठो घने वर्त्राणां सनये धनानाम ||
6.26.e: So may we he thy friends, thy best beloved, O Indra, at this holy invocation.  Best be Pratardani, illustrious ruler, in slaying foemen and in gaining riches.

6.27.d: किमस्य मदे किं वस्य पीताविन्द्रः किमस्य सख्ये चकार | रणा वा ये निषदि किं ते अस्य पुर विविद्रे किमु नूतनासः ||
6.27.e: WHAT deed hath Indra done in the wild transport, in quaffing or in friendship with, the Soma?  What joys have men of ancient times or recent obtained within the chamber of libation?

6.27.d: सदस्य मदे सद वस्य पितविन्द्रः सदस्य सख्ये चकार | रणा वा ये निषदि सत ते अस्य पुर विविद्रे सदु नूतनासः ||
6.27.e: In its wild joy Indra hath proved him faithful, faithful in quaffing, faithful in its friendship.  His truth is the delight that in this chamber the men of old and recent times have tasted.

6.27.d: नहि नु ते महिमनः समस्य न मघवन मघवत्त्वस्य विद्म | न राधसो-राधसो नूतनस्येन्द्र नकिर्दद्र्श इन्द्रियं ते ||
6.27.e: All thy vast power, O Maghavan, we know not, know not the riches of thy full abundance.  No one hath seen that might of thine, productive of bounty every day renewed, O Indra.

6.27.d: एतत तयत त इन्द्रियमचेति येनावधीर्वरशिखस्य शेषः | वज्रस्य यत ते निहतस्य शुष्मात सवनाच्चिदिन्द्र परमोददार ||
6.27.e: This one great power of thine our eyes have witnessed, wherewith thou slewest Varasikha's children,  When by the force of thy descending thunder, at the mere solund, their boldest was demolished.

6.27.d: वधीदिन्द्रो वरशिखस्य शेषो.अभ्यावर्तिने चायमानाय शिक्षन | वर्चीवतो यद धरियूपीयायां हन पूर्वे अर्धे भियसापरो दर्त ||
6.27.e: In aid of Abhyavartin Cayamana, Indra destroyed the seed of Varasikha.  At Hariyupiya he smote the vanguard of the Vrcivans, and the rear fled frighted.

6.27.d: तरिंशच्छतं वर्मिण इन्द्र साकं यव्यावत्यां पुरुहूत शरवस्या | वर्चीवन्तः शरवे पत्यमानाः पात्रा भिन्दानन्यर्थान्यायन ||
6.27.e: Three thousand, mailed, in quest of fame, together, on the Yavyavati, O much-sought Indra,  Vrcivan's sons, falling before the arrow, like bursting vessels went to their destruction.

6.27.d: यस्य गावावरुषा सूयवस्यू अन्तरू षु चरतो रेरिहाणा | स सर्ञ्जयाय तुर्वशं परादाद वर्चीवतो दैववातायशिक्षन ||
6.27.e: He, whose two red Steers, seeking goodly pasture, plying their tongues move on 'twixt earth and heaven,  Gave Turvaśa to Sṛñjaya, and, to aid him, gave the Vrcivans up to Daivavata.

6.27.d: दवयानग्ने रथिनो विंशतिं गा वधूमतो मघवा मह्यं सम्राट | अभ्यावर्ती चायमानो ददाति दूणाशेयं दक्षिणा पार्थवानाम ||
6.27.e: Two wagon-teams, with damsels, twenty oxen, O Agni, Abhydvartin Cayamdna,  The liberal Sovran, giveth me. This guerdon of Prthu's seed is hard to win from others.

6.28.d: आ गावो अग्मन्नुत भद्रमक्रन सीदन्तु गोष्ठे रणयन्त्वस्मे | परजावतीः पुरुरूपा इह सयुरिन्द्राय पूर्वीरुषसो दुहानाः ||
6.28.e: THE Kine have come and brought good fortune: let them rest in the cow-pen and be happy near us.  Here let them stay prolific, many-coloured, and yield through many morns their milk for Indra.

6.28.d: इन्द्रो यज्वने पर्णते च शिक्षत्युपेद ददाति न सवं मुषायति | भूयो-भूयो रयिमिदस्य वर्धयन्नभिन्ने खिल्ये निदधाति देवयुम ||
6.28.e: Indra aids him who offers sacrifice and gifts: he takes not what is his, and gives him more thereto.  Increasing ever more and ever more his wealth, he makes the pious dwell within unbroken bounds.

6.28.d: न ता नशन्ति न दभाति तस्करो नासामामित्रो वयथिरादधर्षति | देवांश्च याभिर्यजते ददाति च जयोगित ताभिः सचते गोपतिः सह ||
6.28.e: These are ne’er lost, no robber ever injures them: no evil-minded foe attempts to harass them.  The master of the Kine lives many a year with these, the Cows whereby he pours his gifts and serves the Gods.

6.28.d: न ता अर्वा रेणुककाटो अश्नुते न संस्क्र्तत्रमुप यन्ति ता अभि | उरुगायमभयं तस्य ता अनु गावो मर्तस्य विचरन्ति यज्वनः ||
6.28.e: The charger with his dusty brow o’ertakes them not, and never to the shambles do they take their way.  These Cows, the cattle of the pious worshipper, roam over widespread pasture where no danger is.

6.28.d: गावो भगो गाव इन्द्रो मे अछान गावः सोमस्य परथमस्य भक्षः | इमा या गावः स जनास इन्द्र इछामीद धर्दामनसा चिदिन्द्रम ||
6.28.e: To me the Cows seem Bhaga, they seem Indra, they seem a portion of the first-poured Soma.  These present Cows, they, O ye Indra. I long for Indra with my heart and spirit.

6.28.d: यूयं गावो मेदयथा कर्शं चिदश्रीरं चित कर्णुथा सुप्रतीकम | भद्रं गर्हं कर्णुथ भद्रवाचो बर्हद वो वय उच्यते सभासु ||
6.28.e: O Cows, ye fatten e’en the worn and wasted, and make the unlovely beautiful tolook on.  Prosper my house, ye with auspicious voices. Your power is glorified in our assemblies.

6.28.d: परजावतीः सूयवसं रिशन्तीः शुद्धा अपः सुप्रपाणेपिबन्तीः | मा व सतेन ईशत माघशंसः परि वो हेती रुद्रस्य वर्ज्याः ||
6.28.e: Crop goodly pasturage and be prolific drink pure sweet water at good drinking places.  Never be thief or sinful man your matter, and may the dart of Rudra still avoid you.

6.28.d: उपेदमुपपर्चनमासु गोषूप पर्च्यताम | उप रषभस्य रेतस्युपेन्द्र तव वीर्ये ||
6.28.e: Now let this close admixture be close intermigled with these Cows,  Mixt with the Steer's prolific flow, and, Indra, with thy hero might.

6.29.d: इन्द्रं वो नरः सख्याय सेपुर्महो यन्तः सुमतये चकानाः | महो हि दाता वज्रहस्तो अस्ति महामु रण्वमवसे यजध्वम ||
6.29.e: YOUR men have followed Indra for his friendship, and for his loving-kindness glorified him.  For he bestows great wealth, the Thunder-wielder: worship him, Great and Kind, to win his favour.

6.29.d: आ यस्मिन हस्ते नर्या मिमिक्षुरा रथे हिरण्यये रथेष्ठाः | आ रश्मयो गभस्त्यो सथूरयोराध्वन्नश्वासो वर्षणो युजानाः ||
6.29.e: Him to whose hand, men closely cling, and drivers stand on his golden chariot firmly stationed.  With his firm arms he holds the reins; his Horses, the Stallions, are yoked ready for the journey.

6.29.d: शरिये ते पादा दुव आ मिमिक्षुर्ध्र्ष्णुर्वज्री शवसा दक्षिणावान | वसानो अत्कं सुरभिं दर्शे कं सवर्ण नर्तविषिरो बभूथ ||
6.29.e: Thy devotees embrace thy feet for glory. Bold, thunder-armed, rich, through thy strength, in guerdon,  Robed in a garment fair as heaven to look on, thou hast displayed thee like an active dancer.

6.29.d: स सोम आमिश्लतमः सुतो भूद यस्मिन पक्तिः पच्यते सन्तिधानाः | इन्द्रं नर सतुवन्तो बरह्मकारा उक्था शंसन्तो देववाततमाः ||
6.29.e: That Soma when effused hath best consistence, for which the food is dressed and grain is mingled;  By which the men who pray, extolling Indra chief favourites of Gods, recite their praises.

6.29.d: न ते अन्तः शवसो धाय्यस्य वि तु बाबधे रोदसी महित्वा | आ ता सूरिः पर्णति तूतुजानो यूथेवाप्सु समीजमान ऊती ||
6.29.e: No limit of thy might hath been appointed, which by its greatness sundered earth and heaven.  These the Prince filleth full with strong endeavour, driving, as ’twere, with help his flocks to waters.

6.29.d: एवेदिन्द्रः सुहव रष्वो अस्तूती अनूती हिरिशिप्रः सत्वा | एवा हि जातो असमात्योजाः पुरू च वर्त्रा हनति नि दस्यून ||
6.29.e: So be the lofty Indra prompt to listen, Helper unaided, golden-visored Hero.  Yea, so may he, shown forth in might unequalled, smite down the many Vṛtras and the Dasyus.

6.30.d: भूय इद वाव्र्धे वीर्यायनेको अजुर्यो दयते वसूनि | पर रिरिचे दिव इन्द्रः पर्थिव्या अर्धमिदस्य परति रोदसी उभे ||
6.30.e: INDRA hath waxed yet more for hero prowess, alone, Eternal, he bestoweth treasures.  Indra transcendeth both the worlds in greatness: one half of him equalleth earth and heaven.

6.30.d: अधा मन्ये बर्हदसुर्यमस्य यानि दाधार नकिरा मिनाति | दिवे-दिवे सूर्यो दर्शतो भूद वि सद्मान्युर्विया सुक्रतुर्धात ||
6.30.e: Yea, mighty I esteem his Godlike nature: none hindereth what he hath once determined.  Near and afar he spread and set the regions, and every day the Sun became apparent.

6.30.d: अद्या चिन नू चित तदपो नदीनां यदाभ्यो अरदो गातुमिन्द्र | नि पर्वता अद्मसदो न सेदुस्त्वया दर्ळ्हानि सुक्रतो रजांसि ||
6.30.e: E’en now endures thine exploit of the Rivers, when, Indra, for their floods thou clavest passage.  Like men who sit at meat the mountains settled: by thee, Most Wise! the regions were made steadfast.

6.30.d: सत्यमित तन न तवावानन्यो अस्तीन्द्र देवो न मर्त्यो जयायान | अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्णो.अवास्र्जो अपो अछा समुद्रम ||
6.30.e: This is the truth, none else is like thee, Indra, no God superior to thee, no mortal.  Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and lettest loose the streams to hurry seaward.

6.30.d: तवमपो वि दुरो विषूचीरिन्द्र दर्ळ्हमरुजः पर्वतस्य | राजाभवो जगतश्चर्षणीनां साकं सूर्यं जनयन दयामुषासम ||
6.30.e: Indra, thou breakest up the floods and portals on all sides, and the firmness of the mountain.  Thou art the King of men, of all that liveth, engendering at once Sun, Heaven, and Morning.

6.31.d: अभूरेको रयिपते रयीणामा हस्तयोरधिथा इन्द्र कर्ष्टीः | वि तोके अप्सु तनये च सूरे.अवोचन्त चर्षणयो विवाचः ||
6.31.e: SOLE Lord of wealth art thou, O Lord of riches: thou in thine hands hast held the people, Indra!  Men have invoked thee with contending voices for seed and waters, progeny and sunlight.

6.31.d: तवद भियेन्द्र पार्थिवानि विश्वाच्युता चिच्च्यावयन्ते रजांसि | दयावाक्षामा पर्वतासो वनानि विश्वं दर्ळ्हं भयते अज्मन्ना ते ||
6.31.e: Through fear of thee, O Indra, all the regions of earth, though naught may move them, shake and tremble.  All that is firm is frightened at thy coming, -the earth, the heaven, the mountain, and the forest.

6.31.d: तवं कुत्सेनाभि शुष्णमिन्द्राशुषं युध्य कुयवं गविष्टौ | दश परपित्वे अध सूर्यस्य मुषायश्चक्रमविवेरपांसि ||
6.31.e: With Kutsa, Indra! thou didst conquer Śuṣṇa, voracious, bane of crops, in fight for cattle.  In the close fray thou rentest him: thou stolest the Sun's wheel and didst drive away misfortunes.

6.31.d: तवं शतान्यव शम्बरस्य पुरो जघन्थाप्रतीनि सस्योः | अशिक्षो यत्र शच्या शचीवो दिवोदासाय सुन्वते सुतक्रे भरद्वाजाय गर्णते वसूनि ||
6.31.e: Thou smotest to the ground the hundred castles, impregnable, of Śambara the Dasyu,  When, Strong, with might thou holpest Divodāsa who poured libations out, O Soma-buyer, and madest Bharadvāja rich who praised thee.

6.31.d: स सत्यसत्वन महते रणाय रथमा तिष्ठ तुविन्र्म्ण भीमम | याहि परपथिन्नवसोप मद्रिक पर च शरुत शरावय चर्षणिभ्यः ||
6.31.e: As such, true Hero, for great joy of battle mount thy terrific car, O Brave and Manly.  Come with thine help to me, thou distant Roamer, and, glorious God, spread among men my glory.

6.32.d: अपूर्व्या पुरुतमान्यस्मै महे वीराय तवसे तुराय | विरप्शिने वज्रिणे शन्तमानि वचांस्यासा सथविराय तक्षम ||
6.32.e: I WITH my lips have fashioned for this Hero words never matched, most plentiful and auspicious,  For him the Ancient, Great, Strong, Energetic, the very mighty Wielder of the Thunder.

6.32.d: स मातरा सूर्येणा कवीनामवासयद रुजदद्रिं गर्णानः | सवाधीभिर्र्क्वभिर्वावशान उदुस्रियाणामस्र्जन निदानम ||
6.32.e: Amid the sages, with the Sun he brightened the Parents: glorified, he burst the mountain;  And, roaring with the holy-thoughted singers, he loosed the bond that held the beams of Morning.

6.32.d: स वह्निभिर्र्क्वभिर्गोषु शश्वन मितज्ञुभिः पुरुक्र्त्वा जिगाय | पुरः पुरोहा सखिभिः सखीयन दर्ळ्हा रुरोज कविभिः कविः सन ||
6.32.e: Famed for great deeds, with priests who kneel and laud him, he still hath conquered in the frays for cattle,  And broken down the forts, the Fort-destroyer, a Friend with friends, a Sage among the sages.

6.32.d: स नीव्याभिर्जरितारमछा महो वाजेभिर्महद्भिश्च शुष्मैः | पुरुवीराभिर्व्र्षभ कषितीनामा गिर्वणः सुविताय पर याहि ||
6.32.e: Come with thy girthed mares, with abundant vigour and plenteous strength to him who sings thy praises.  Come hither, borne by mares with many heroes, Lover of song! Steer! for the people's welfare.

6.32.d: स सर्गेण शवसा तक्तो अत्यैरप इन्द्रो दक्षिणतस्तुराषाट | इत्था सर्जाना अनपाव्र्दर्थं दिवे-दिवे विविषुरप्रम्र्ष्यम ||
6.32.e: Indra with rush and might, sped by his Coursers, hath swiftly won the waters from the southward.  Thus set at liberty the rivers daily flow to their goal, incessant and exhaustless.

6.33.d: य ओजिष्ठ इन्द्र तं सु नो दा मदो वर्षन सवभिष्टिर्दास्वान | सौवश्व्यं यो वनवत सवश्वो वर्त्रा समत्सु सासहदमित्रान ||
6.33.e: GIVE us the rapture that is mightiest, Indra, prompt to bestow and swift to aid, O Hero,  That wins with brave steeds where brave steeds encounter, and quells the Vṛtras and the foes in battle.

6.33.d: तवां हीन्द्रावसे विवाचो हवन्ते चर्षणयः शूरसातौ | तवं विप्रेभिर्वि पणीन्रशायस्त्वोत इत सनिता वाजमर्वा ||
6.33.e: For with loud voice the tribes invoke thee, Indra, to aid them in the battlefield of heroes.  Thou, with the singers, hast pierced through the Paṇis: the charger whom thou aidest wins the booty.

6.33.d: तवं तानिन्द्रोभयानमित्रान दासा वर्त्राण्यार्या च शूर | वधीर्वनेव सुधितेभिरत्कैरा पर्त्सु दर्षि नर्णां नर्तम ||
6.33.e: Both races, Indra, of opposing foemen, O Hero, both the Ārya and the Dāsa,  Hast thou struck down like woods with well-shot lightnings: thou rentest them in fight, most manly Chieftain!

6.33.d: स तवं न इन्द्राकवाभिरूती सखा विश्वायुरविता वर्धे भूः | सवर्षाता यद धवयामसि तवा युध्यन्तो नेमधिताप्र्त्सु शूर ||
6.33.e: Indra, befriend us with no scanty succour, prosper and aid us, Loved of all that liveth,  When, fighting for the sunlight, we invoke thee, O Hero, in the fray, in war's division.

6.33.d: नूनं न इन्द्रापराय च सया भवा मर्ळीक उत नो अभिष्टौ | इत्था गर्णन्तो महिनस्य शर्मन दिवि षयाम पार्ये गोषतमाः ||
6.33.e: Be ours, O Indra, now and for the future, be graciously inclined and near to help us.  Thus may we, singing, sheltered by the Mighty, win many cattle on the day of trial.

6.34.d: सं च तवे जग्मुर्गिर इन्द्र पूर्वीर्वि च तवद यन्ति विभ्वोमनीषाः | पूरा नूनं च सतुतय रषीणां पस्प्र्ध्र इन्द्रे अध्युक्थार्का ||
6.34.e: FULL Many songs have met in thee, O Indra, and many a noble thought from thee proceedeth.  Now and of old the eulogies of sages, their holy hymns and lauds, have yearned for Indra.

6.34.d: पुरुहूतो यः पुरुगूर्त रभ्वानेकः पुरुप्रशस्तो अस्ति यज्ञैः | रथो न महे शवसे युजानो.अस्माभिरिन्द्रो अनुमाद्यो भूत ||
6.34.e: He, praised of many, bold, invoked of many, alone is glorified at sacrifices.  Like a car harnessed for some great achievement, Indra must be the cause of our rejoicing.

6.34.d: न यं हिंसन्ति धीतयो न वाणीरिन्द्रं नक्षन्तीदभि वर्धयन्तीः | यदि सतोतारः शतं यत सहस्रं गर्णन्ति गिर्वणसं शं तदस्मै ||
6.34.e: They make their way to Indra and exalt him, bim whom no prayers and no laudations trouble;  For when a hundred or a thousand singers. laud him who loves the song their praise delights him.

6.34.d: अस्मा एतद दिव्यर्चेव मासा मिमिक्ष इन्द्रे नययामि सोमः | जनं न धन्वन्नभि सं यदापः सत्रा वाव्र्धुर्हवनानि यज्ञैः ||
6.34.e: As brightness mingles with the Moon in heaven, the offered Soma yearns to mix with Indra.  Like water brought to men in desert places, our gifts at sacrifice have still refreshed him.

6.34.d: अस्मा एतन मह्याङगूषमस्मा इन्द्राय सतोत्रं मतिभिरवाचि | असद यथा महति वर्त्रतूर्य इन्द्रो विश्वायुरविता वर्धश्च ||
6.34.e: To him this mighty eulogy, to Indra hath this our laud been uttered by the poets,  That in the great encounter with the foemen, Loved of all life, Indra may guard and help us.

6.35.d: कदा भुवन रथक्षयाणि बरह्म कदा सतोत्रे सहस्रपोष्यन्दाः | कदा सतोमं वासयो.अस्य राया कदा धियः करसि वाजरत्नाः ||
6.35.e: WHEN shall our prayers rest in thy car beside thee? When dost thou give the singer food for thousands?  When wilt thou clothe this poet's laud with plenty, and when wilt thou enrich our hymns with booty?

6.35.d: कर्हि सवित तदिन्द्र यन नर्भिर्नॄन वीरैर्वीरान नीळयासे जयाजीन | तरिधातु गा अधि जयासि गोष्विन्द्र दयुम्नंस्वर्वद धेह्यस्मे ||
6.35.e: When wilt thou gatber men with men, O Indra, heroes with heroes, and prevail in combat?  Thou shalt win triply kine in frays for cattle, so, Indra, give thou us celestial glory.

6.35.d: कर्हि सवित तदिन्द्र यज्जरित्रे विष्वप्सु बरह्म कर्णवः शविष्ठ | कदा धियो न नियुतो युवासे कदा गोमघा हवनानि गछाः ||
6.35.e: Yea, when wilt thou, O Indra, thou Most Mighty, make the prayer all-sustaining for the singer?  When wilt thou yoke, as we yoke songs, thy Horses, and come to offerings that bring wealth in cattle?

6.35.d: स गोमघा जरित्रे अश्वश्चन्द्रा वाजश्रवसो अधि धेहि पर्क्षः | पीपिहीषः सुदुघामिन्द्र धेनुं भरद्वाजेषु सुरुचो रुरुच्याः ||
6.35.e: Grant to the Singer food with store of cattle, splendid with horses and the fame of riches.  Send food to swell the milch-cow good at milking: bright be its shine among the Bharadvājas.

6.35.d: तमा नूनं वर्जनमन्यथा चिच्छूरो यच्छक्र वि दुरोग्र्णीषे | मा निररं शुक्रदुघस्य धेनोराङगिरसान बरह्मणा विप्र जिन्व ||
6.35.e: Lead otherwise this present foeman, Śakra! Hence art thou praised as Hero, foe destroyer  Him who gives pure gifts may I praise unceasing. Sage, quicken the Aṅgirases by devotion.

6.36.d: सत्रा मदासस्तव विश्वजन्याः सत्रा रायो.अध ये पार्थिवासः | सत्रा वाजानामभवो विभक्ता यद देवेषु धारयथा असुर्यम ||
6.36.e: THY raptures ever were for all men's profit: so evermore have been thine earthly riches.  Thou still hast been the dealer-forth of vigour, since among Gods thou hast had power and Godhead.

6.36.d: अनु पर येजे जन ओजो अस्य सत्रा दधिरे अनु वीर्याय | सयूमग्र्भे दुधये.अर्वते च करतुं वर्ञ्जन्त्यपि वर्त्रहत्ये ||
6.36.e: Men have obtained his strength by sacrificing, and ever urged him, on to hero valour.  For the rein-seizing, the impetuous Charger they furnished power even for Vṛtra's slaughter.

6.36.d: तं सध्रीचीरूतयो वर्ष्ण्यानि पौंस्यानि नियुतः सश्चुरिन्द्रम | समुद्रं न सिन्धव उक्थशुष्मा उरुव्यचसं गिरा विशन्ति ||
6.36.e: Associate with him, as teams of horses, help, manly might, and vigour follow Indra.  As rivers reach the sea, so, strong with praises, our holy songs reach him the Comprehensive.

6.36.d: स रायस खामुप सर्जा गर्णानः पुरुश्चन्द्रस्य तवमिन्द्रवस्वः | पतिर्बभूथासमो जनानामेको विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा ||
6.36.e: Lauded by us, let flow the spring, O Indra, of excellent and brightly-shining riches.  For thou art Lord of men, without an equal: of all the world thou art the only Sovran.

6.36.d: स तु शरुधि शरुत्या यो दुवोयुर्द्यौर्न भूमाभि रायोर्यः | असो यथा नः शवसा चकानो युगे-युगे वयसा चेकितानः ||
6.36.e: Hear what thou mayst hear, thou who, fain for worship, as heaven girds earth, guardest thy servant's treasure;  Tlat thou mayst be our own, joying in power, famed through thy might in every generation.

6.37.d: अर्वाग रथं विश्ववारं त उग्रेन्द्र युक्तासो हरयो वहन्तु | कीरिश्चिद धि तवा हवते सवर्वान रधीमहि सधमादस्तेद्य ||
6.37.e: LET thy Bay Horses, yoked, O mighty Indra, bring thy car hither fraught with every blessing.  For thee, the Heavenly, e’en the poor invoketh: may we this day, thy feast-companions, prosper.

6.37.d: परो दरोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन पुनानास रज्यन्तो अभूवन | इन्द्रो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पपीयाद दयुक्षो मदस्य सोम्यस्य राजा ||
6.37.e: Forth to the vat the brown drops flow for service, and purified proceed directly forward.  May Indra drink of this, our guest aforetime, Celestial King of the strong draught of Soma.

6.37.d: आसस्राणासः शवसानमछेन्द्रं सुचक्रे रथ्यासो अश्वाः | अभि शरव रज्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन नु वायोरम्र्तं विदस्येत ||
6.37.e: Bringing us hitherward all-potent Indra on well-wheeled chariot, may the Steeds who bear him  Convey him on the road direct to glory, and ne’er may Vāyu's Amṛta cease and fail him.

6.37.d: वरिष्ठो अस्य दक्षिणामियर्तीन्द्रो मघोनां तुविकूर्मितमः | यया वज्रिवः परियास्यंहो मघा च धर्ष्णो दयसे वि सूरीन ||
6.37.e: Supreme, he stirs this man to give the guerdon,—Indra, most efficacious of the princes,—  Wherewith, O Thunderer, thou removest sorrow, and, Bold One! partest wealth among the nobles.

6.37.d: इन्द्रो वाजस्य सथविरस्य दातेन्द्रो गीर्भिर्वर्धतां वर्द्धमहाः | इन्द्रो वर्त्रं हनिष्ठो अस्तु सत्वा ता सूरिः पर्णति तूतुजानः ||
6.37.e: Indra is hewho gives enduring vigour: may our songs magnify the God Most Mighty.  Best Vṛtra-slayer be the Hero Indra these things he gives as Prince, with strong endeavour.

6.38.d: अपादित उदु नश्चित्रतमो महीं भर्षद दयुमतीमिन्द्रहूतिम | पन्यसीं धीतिं दैव्यस्य यामञ जनस्य रातिं वनते सुदानुः ||
6.38.e: HE hath drunk hence, Most Marvellous, and carried away our great and splendid call on Indra.  The Bounteous, when we serve the Gods, accepteth song yet more famous and the gifts we bring him.

6.38.d: दूराच्चिदा वसतो अस्य कर्णा घोषादिन्द्रस्य तन्यति बरुवाणः | एयमेनं देवहूतिर्वव्र्त्यान मद्र्यगिन्द्रमियं रच्यमाना ||
6.38.e: The speaker filleth with a cry to Indra his ears who cometh nigh e’en from a distance.  May this my call bring Indra to my presence, this call to Gods composed in sacred verses.

6.38.d: तं वो धिया परमया पुराजामजरमिन्द्रमभ्यनूष्यर्कैः | बरह्मा च गिरो दधिरे समस्मिन महांश्च सतोमो अधि वर्धदिन्द्रे ||
6.38.e: Him have I sung with my best song and praises, Indra of ancient birth and Everlasting.  For prayer and songs in him are concentrated: let laud wax mighty when addressed to Indra:

6.38.d: वर्धाद यं यज्ञ उत सोम इन्द्रं वर्धाद बरह्म गिर उक्था च मन्म | वर्धाहैनमुषसो यामन्नक्तोर्वर्धान मासाः शरदो दयाव इन्द्रम ||
6.38.e: Indra, whom sacrifice shall strengthen, Soma, and song and hymn, and praises and devotion,  Whom Dawns shall strengthen when the night departeth, Indra whom days shall strengthen, months, and autumns.

6.38.d: एवा जज्ञानं सहसे असामि वाव्र्धानं राधसे च शरुताय | महामुग्रमवसे विप्र नूनमा विवासेम वर्त्रतूर्येषु ||
6.38.e: Him, born for conquering might in full perfection, and waxen strongfor bounty and for glory,  Great, Powerful, will we to-day, O singer, invite to aid. us and to quell our foemen.

6.39.d: मन्द्रस्य कवेर्दिव्यस्य वह्नेर्विप्रमन्मनो वचनस्य मध्वः | अपा नस्तस्य सचनस्य देवेषो युवस्व गर्णते गोग्राः ||
6.39.e: OF this our charming, our celestial Soma, eloquent, wise, Priest, with inspired devotion,  Of this thy close attendant, hast thou drunken. God, send the singer food with milk to grace it.

6.39.d: अयमुशानः पर्यद्रिमुस्र रतधीतिभिर्र्तयुग युजानः | रुजदरुग्णं वि वलस्य सानुं पणीन्र्वचोभिरभि योधदिन्द्रः ||
6.39.e: Craving the kine, rushing against the mountain led on by Law, with holyminded comrades,  He broke the never-broken ridge of Vala. With words of might Indra subdued the Paṇis.

6.39.d: अयं दयोतयदद्युतो वयक्तून दोषा वस्तोः शरद इन्दुरिन्द्र | इमं केतुमदधुर्नू चिदह्नां शुचिजन्मन उषसश्चकार ||
6.39.e: This Indu lighted darksome nights, O Indra, throughout the years, at morning and at evening.  Him have they stablished as the days' bright ensign. He made the Mornings to be born in splendour.

6.39.d: अयं रोचयदरुचो रुचानो.अयं वासयद वय रतेन पूर्वीः | अयमीयत रतयुग्भिरश्वैः सवर्विदा नाभिना चर्षणिप्राः ||
6.39.e: He shone and caused to shme the worlds that shone not. By Law he lighted up the host of Mornings.  He moves with Steeds yoked by eternal Order, contenting men with nave that finds the sunlight.

6.39.d: नू गर्णानो गर्णते परत्न राजन्निषः पिन्व वसुदेयाय पूर्वीः | अप ओषधीरविषा वनानि गा अर्वतो नॄन रचसे रिरीहि ||
6.39.e: Now, praised, O Ancient King! fill thou the singer with plenteous food that he may deal forth treasures.  Give waters, herbs that have no poison, forests, and kine, and steeds, and men, to him who lauds thee.

6.40.d: इन्द्र पिब तुभ्यं सुतो मदायाव सय हरी वि मुचा सखाया | उत पर गाय गण आ निषद्याथा यज्ञाय गर्णते वयो धाः ||
6.40.e: DRINK, Indra; juice is shed to make thee joyful: loose thy Bay Steeds and give thy friends their freedom.  Begin the song, seated in our assembly. Give strength for sacrifice to him who singeth.

6.40.d: अस्य पिब यस्य जज्ञान इन्द्र मदाय करत्वे अपिबो विरप्शिन | तमु ते गावो नर आपो अद्रिरिन्दुं समह्यन पीतये समस्मै ||
6.40.e: Drink thou of this whereof at birth, O Indra, thou drankest, Mighty One for power and rapture.  The men, the pressing-stones, the cows, the waters have made this Soma ready for thy drinking.

6.40.d: समिद्धे अग्नौ सुत इन्द्र सोम आ तवा वहन्तु हरयो वहिष्ठाः | तवायता मनसा जोहवीमीन्द्रा याहि सुविताय महे नः ||
6.40.e: The fire is kindled, Soma pressed, O Indra: let thy Bays, best to draw, convey thee hither.  With mind devoted, Indra, I invoke thee. Come, for our great prosperity approach us.

6.40.d: आ याहि शश्वदुशता ययाथेन्द्र महा मनसा सोमपेयम | उप बरह्माणि शर्णव इमा नो.अथा ते यज्ञस्तन्वे वयो धात ||
6.40.e: Indra, come hither: evermore thou camest through our great strong desire to drink the Soma.  Listen and hear the prayers which now we offer, and let this sacrifice increase thy vigour.

6.40.d: यदिन्द्र दिवि पार्ये यद रधग यद वा सवे सदने यत्र वासि | अतो नो यज्ञमवसे नियुत्वान सजोषाः पाहि गिर्वणो मरुद्भिः ||
6.40.e: Mayst thou, O Indra, on the day of trial, present or absent, wheresoe’er thou dwellest,  Thence, with thy team, accordant with the Maruts, Song-lover! guard our sacrifice, to help us.

6.41.d: अहेळमान उप याहि यज्ञं तुभ्यं पवन्त इन्दवः सुतासः | गावो न वज्रिन सवमोको अछेन्द्रा गहि परथमो यज्ञियानाम ||
6.41.e: COME gracious to our sacrifice, O Indra: pressed Soma-drops are purified to please thee.  As cattle seek their home, so Thunderwielder, come, Indra, first of those who claim our worship.

6.41.d: या ते काकुत सुक्र्ता या वरिष्ठा यया शश्वत पिबसि मध्व ऊर्मिम | तया पाहि पर ते अध्वर्युरस्थात सं ते वज्रोवर्ततामिन्द्र गव्युः ||
6.41.e: With that well-formed most wide-extending palate, wherewith thou ever drinkest streams of sweetness,  Drink thou; the Adhvaryu standeth up before thee: let thy spoil-winning thunderbolt attend thee.

6.41.d: एष दरप्सो वर्षभो विश्वरूप इन्द्राय वर्ष्णे समकारि सोमः | एतं पिब हरिव सथातरुग्र यस्येशिषे परदिवि यस्तेन्नम ||
6.41.e: This drop, steer-strong and omniform, the Soma, hath been made ready for the Bull, for India.  Drink this, Lord of the Bays, thou Strong Supporter, this that is thine of old, thy food for ever.

6.41.d: सुतः सोमो असुतादिन्द्र वस्यानयं शरेयाञ्चिकितुषे रणाय | एतं तितिर्व उप याहि यज्ञं तेन विश्वास्तविषीरा पर्णस्व ||
6.41.e: Soma when pressed excels the unpressed Soma, better, for one who knows, to give him pleasure.  Come to this sacrifice of ours, O Victor replenish all thy powers with this libation.

6.41.d: हवयामसि तवेन्द्र याह्यर्वां अरं ते सोमस्तन्वे भवाति | शतक्रतो मादयस्वा सुतेषु परास्मानव पर्तनासु पर विक्षु ||
6.41.e: We call on thee, O Indra: come thou hither: sufficient be the Soma for thy body.  Rejoice thee, Śatakratu! in the juices guard us in wars, guard us among our people.

6.42.d: परत्यस्मै पिपीषते विश्वानि विदुषे भर | अरंगमाय जग्मये.अपश्चाद्दघ्वने नरे ||
6.42.e: BRING sacrificial gifts to him, Omniscient, for he longs to drink,  The Wanderer who comes with speed, the Hero ever in the van.

6.42.d: एमेनं परत्येतन सोमेभिः सोमपातमम | अमत्रेभिर्र्जीषिणमिन्द्रं सुतेभिरिन्दुभिः ||
6.42.e: With Soma go ye nigh to him chief drinker of the Soma's juice:  With beakers to the Impetuous God, to Indra with the drops effused.

6.42.d: यदी सुतेभिरिन्दुभिः सोमेभिः परतिभूषथ | वेदा विश्वस्य मेधिरो धर्षत तं-तमिदेषते ||
6.42.e: What time, with Soma, with the juice effused, ye come before the God,  Full wise he knows the hope of each, and, Bold One, strikes this foe and that.

6.42.d: अस्मा-अस्मा इदन्धसो.अध्वर्यो पर भरा सुतम | कुवित समस्य जेन्यस्य शर्धतो.अभिशस्तेरवस्परत ||
6.42.e: To him, Adhvaryu! yea, to him give offerings of the juice expressed.  Will he not keep us safely from the spiteful curse of each presumptuous high-born foe?

6.43.d: यस्य तयच्छम्बरं मदे दिवोदासाय रन्धयः | अयं स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब ||
6.43.e: IN whose wild joy thou madest once Śambara Divodāsa's prey,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!

6.43.d: यस्य तीव्रसुतं मदं मध्यमन्तं च रक्षसे | अयं स... ||
6.43.e: Whose gladdening draught, shed from the points, thou guardest in the midst and end,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!

6.43.d: यस्य गा अन्तरश्मनो मदे दर्ळ्हा अवास्र्जः | अयं स .. . ||
6.43.e: In whose wild joy thou settest free the kine held fast within the rock,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!

6.43.d: यस्य मन्दानो अन्धसो माघोनं दधिषे शवः | अयं स... ||
6.43.e: This, in whose juice delighting thou gainest the might of Maghavan,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!

6.44.d: यो रयिवो रयिन्तमो यो दयुम्नैर्द्युम्नवत्तमः | सोमः सुतः स इन्द्र ते.अस्ति सवधापते मदः ||
6.44.e: THAT which is wealthiest, Wealthy God in splendoursmost illustrious,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: यः शग्मस्तुविशग्म ते रायो दामा मतीनाम | सोमः सुतः ... ||
6.44.e: Effectual, Most Effectual One! thine, as bestowing wealth of hymns,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: येन वर्द्धो न शवसा तुरो न सवाभिरूतिभिः | सोमः सुतः ... ||
6.44.e: Wherewith thou art increased in strength, and conquerest with thy proper aids,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: तयमु वो अप्रहणं गर्णीषे शवसस पतिम | इन्द्रं विश्वासाहं नरं मंहिष्ठं विश्वचर्षणिम ||
6.44.e: Him for your sake I glorify as Lord of Strength who wrongeth none,  The Hero Indra, conquering all, Most Bounteous, God of all the tribes.

6.44.d: यं वर्धयन्तीद गिरः पतिं तुरस्य राधसः | तमिन्न्वस्य रोदसी देवी शुष्मं सपर्यतः ||
6.44.e: Those Goddesses, both Heaven and Earth, revere the power and might of him,  Him whom our songs increase in strength, the Lord of bounty swift to come.

6.44.d: तद व उक्थस्य बर्हणेन्द्रायोपस्त्र्णीषणि | विपो न यस्योतयो वि यद रोहन्ति सक्षितः ||
6.44.e: To seat your Indra, I will spread abroad with power this song of praise.  The saving succours that abide in him, like songs, extend and grow.

6.44.d: अविदद दक्षं मित्रो नवीयान पपानो देवेभ्यो वस्यो अचैत | ससवान सतौलाभिर्धौतरीभिरुरुष्या पायुरभवत सखिभ्यः ||
6.44.e: A recent Friend, he found the skilful priest: he drank, and showed forth treasure from the Gods.  He conquered, borne by strong all-shaking mares, and was with far-spread power his friends' Protector.

6.44.d: रतस्य पथि वेधा अपायि शरिये मनांसि देवासो अक्रन | दधानो नाम महो वचोभिर्वपुर्द्र्शये वेन्यो वयावः ||
6.44.e: In course of Law the sapient juice was quaffed: the Deities to glory turned their mind.  Winning through hymns a lofty title, he, the Lovely, made his beauteous form apparent.

6.44.d: दयुमत्तमं दक्षं धेह्यस्मे सेधा जनानां पूर्वीररातीः | वर्षीयो वयः कर्णुहि शचीभिर्धनस्य सातावस्मानविड्ढि ||
6.44.e: Bestow on us the most illustrious strength ward off men's manifold malignities.  Give with thy might abundant vital force, and aid us graciously in gaining riches.

6.44.d: इन्द्र तुभ्यमिन मघवन्नभूम वयं दात्रे हरिवो मा विवेनः | नकिरापिर्दद्र्शे मर्त्यत्रा किमङग रध्रचोदनन्त्वाहुः ||
6.44.e: We turn to thee as Giver, liberal Indra. Lord of the Bay Steeds, be not thou ungracious.  No friend among mankind have we to lookto: why have men called thee him who spurs the niggard?

6.44.d: मा जस्वने वर्षभ नो ररीथा मा ते रेवतः सख्ये रिषाम | पूर्वीष ट इन्द्र निष्षिधो जनेषु जह्यसुष्वीन पर वर्हाप्र्णतः ||
6.44.e: Give us not up, Strong Hero! to the hungry: unharmed be we whom thou, so rich, befriendest.  Full many a boon hast thou for men demolish those who present no gifts nor pour oblations.

6.44.d: उदभ्राणीव सतनयन्नियर्तीन्द्रो राधांस्यश्व्यानि गव्या | तवमसि परदिवः कारुधाया मा तवादामान आ दभन्मघोनः ||
6.44.e: As Indra thundering impels the rain-clouds, so doth he send us store of kine and horses.  Thou art of old the Cherisher of singers let not the rich who bring no gifts deceive thee.

6.44.d: अध्वर्यो वीर पर महे सुतानामिन्द्राय भर स हयस्य राजा | यः पूर्व्याभिरुत नूतनाभिर्गीर्भिर्वाव्र्धे गर्णतां रषीणाम ||
6.44.e: Adbyaryu, hero, bring to mighty Indrafor he is King thereof-the pressed-out juices;  To him exalted by the hymns and praises, ancient and modern, of the singing Ṛṣis.

6.44.d: अस्य मदे पुरु वर्पांसि विद्वानिन्द्रो वर्त्राण्यप्रती जघान | तमु पर होषि मधुमन्तमस्मै सोमं वीराय शिप्रिणे पिबध्यै ||
6.44.e: In the wild joy of this hath Indra, knowing full many a form, struck down resistless Vṛtras.  Proclaim aloud to him the savoury Soma so that the Hero, strong of jaw, may drink it.

6.44.d: पाता सुतमिन्द्रो अस्तु सोमं हन्ता वर्त्रं वज्रेण मन्दसानः | गन्ता यज्ञं परावतश्चिदछा वसुर्धीनामविता कारुधायाः ||
6.44.e: May Indra drink this Soma poured to please him, and cheered therewith slay Vṛtra with his thunder.  Come to our sacrifice even from a distance, good lover of our songs, the bard's Supporter.

6.44.d: इदं तयत पात्रमिन्द्रपानमिन्द्रस्य परियमम्र्तमपायि | मत्सद यथा सौमनसाय देवं वयस्मद दवेषो युयवद वयंहः ||
6.44.e: The cup whence Indra drinks the draught is present: the Amṛta dear to Indra hath been drunken,  That it may cheer the God to gracious favour, and keep far from us hatred and affliction.

6.44.d: एना मन्दानो जहि शूर शत्रूञ जामिमजामिं मघवन्नमित्रान | अभिषेणानभ्यादेदिशानान पराच इन्द्र पर मर्णाजही च ||
6.44.e: Therewith enraptured, Hero, slay our foemen, the unfriendly, Maghavan be they kin or strangers,  Those who still aim their hostile darts to smite us, turn them to flight, O Indra, crush and kill them.

6.44.d: आसु षमा णो मघवन्निन्द्र पर्त्स्वस्मभ्यं महि वरिवः सुगं कः | अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेष इन्द्र सूरीन कर्णुहिस्मा नो अर्धम ||
6.44.e: O Indra Maghavan, in these our battles win easy paths for us and ample freedom.  That we may gain waters and seed and offspring, set thou our princes on thy side, O Indra.

6.44.d: आ तवा हरयो वर्षणो युजाना वर्षरथासो वर्षरश्मयो.अत्याः | अस्मत्राञ्चो वर्षणो वज्रवाहो वर्ष्णे मदाय सुयुजोवहन्तु ||
6.44.e: Let thy Bay Stallions, harnessed, bring thee hither, Steeds with strong chariot and strong reins to hold them,  Strong Horses, speeding hither, bearing thunder, well-harnessed, for the strong exciting potion.

6.44.d: आ ते वर्षन वर्षणो दरोणमस्थुर्घ्र्तप्रुषो नोर्मयो मदन्तः | इन्द्र पर तुभ्यं वर्षभिः सुतानां वर्ष्णे भरन्तिव्र्षभाय सोमम ||
6.44.e: Beside the vat, Strong God! stand thy strong Horses, shining with holy oil, like waves exulting.  Indra, they bring to thee, the Strong and Mighty, Soma of juices shed by mighty press-stones.

6.44.d: वर्षासि दिवो वर्षभः पर्थिव्या वर्षा सिन्धूनां वर्षभस्तियानाम | वर्ष्णे त इन्दुर्व्र्षभ पीपाय सवादू रसो मधुपेयो वराय ||
6.44.e: Thou art the Bull of earth, the Bull of heaven, Bull of the rivers, Bull of standing waters.  For thee, the Strong, O Bull, hath Indu swollen. juice pleasant, sweet to drink, for thine election.

6.44.d: अयं देवः सहसा जायमान इन्द्रेण युजा पणिमस्तभायत | अयं सवस्य पितुरायुधानीन्दुरमुष्णादशिवस्य मायाः ||
6.44.e: This God, with might, when first he had his being, with Indra for ally, held fast the Paṇi.  This Indu stole away the warlike weapons, and foiled the arts of his malignant father.

6.44.d: अयमक्र्णोदुषसः सुपत्नीरयं सूर्ये अदधाज्ज्योतिरन्तः | अयं तरिधातु दिवि रोचनेषु तरितेषु विन्ददम्र्तं निगूळ्हम ||
6.44.e: The Dawns he wedded to a glorious Consort, and set within the Sun the light that lights him.  He found in heaven, in the third lucid regions, the threefold Amṛta in its close concealment.

6.44.d: अयं दयावाप्र्थिवी वि षकभायदयं रथमयुनक सप्तरश्मिम | अयं गोषु शच्या पक्वमन्तः सोमो दाधार दशयन्त्रमुत्सम ||
6.44.e: He stayed and held the heaven and earth asunder: the chariot with the sevenfold reins he harnessed.  This Soma Set with power within the milch-kine a spring whose ripe contents ten fingers empty.

6.45.d: य आनयत परावतः सुनीती तुर्वशं यदुम | इन्द्रः सनो युवा सखा ||
6.45.e: THAT Indra is our youthful Friend, who with his trusty guidance led  Turvaśa, Yadu from afar.

6.45.d: अविप्रे चिद वयो दधदनाशुना चिदर्वता | इन्द्रो जेता हितं धनम ||
6.45.e: Even to the dull and uninspired Indra, gives vital power, and wins  Even with slow steed the offered prize.

6.45.d: महीरस्य परणीतयः पूर्वीरुत परशस्तयः | नास्य कषीयन्त ऊतयः ||
6.45.e: Great are his ways of guiding us, andṅanilbld are Ins eulogies:  His kind protections never fail.

6.45.d: सखायो बरह्मवाहसे.अर्चत पर च गायत | स हि नः परमतिर्मही ||
6.45.e: Friends, sing your psalm and offer praise to him to whom the prayer is brought:  For our great Providence is he.

6.45.d: तवमेकस्य वर्त्रहन्नविता दवयोरसि | उतेद्र्शे यथा वयम ||
6.45.e: Thou, Slaughterer of Vṛtra, art Guardian and Friend of one and two,  Yea, of a man like one of us.

6.45.d: नयसीद वति दविषः कर्णोष्युक्थशंसिनः | नर्भिः सुवीर उच्यसे ||
6.45.e: Beyond men's hate thou leadest us, and givest cause to sing thy praise:  Good hero art thou called by men.

6.45.d: बरह्माणं बरह्मवाहसं गीर्भिः सखायं रग्मियम | गांन दोहसे हुवे ||
6.45.e: I call with hymns, as ’twere a cow to milk, the Friend who merits praise,  The Brahman who accepts the prayer.

6.45.d: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोरूचुर्वसूनि नि दविता | वीरस्य पर्तनाषहः ||
6.45.e: Him in whose hands they say are stored all treasures from the days of old,  The Hero, conquering in the fight.

6.45.d: वि दर्ळ्हानि चिदद्रिवो जनानां शचीपते | वर्ह माया अनानत ||
6.45.e: Lord of Strength, Caster of the Stone, destroy the firm forts built by men,  And foil their arts, unbending God!

6.45.d: तमु तवा सत्य सोमपा इन्द्र वाजानां पते | अहूमहि शरवस्यवः ||
6.45.e: Thee, thee as such, O Lord of Power, O Indra, Soma-drinker, true,  We, fain for glory, have invoked.

6.45.d: तमु तवा यः पुरासिथ यो वा नूनं हिते धने | हव्यःस शरुधी हवम ||
6.45.e: Such as thou wast of old, and art now to be called on when the prize  lies ready, listen to our call.

6.45.d: धीभिरर्वद्भिरर्वतो वाजानिन्द्र शरवाय्यान | तवया जेष्म हितं धनम ||
6.45.e: With hymns and coursers we will gain, Indra, through thee, both steeds and spoil  Most glorious, and the proffered prize.

6.45.d: अभूरु वीर गिर्वणो महानिन्द्र धने हिते | भरे वितन्तसाय्यः ||
6.45.e: Thou, Indra, Lover of the Song, whom men must stir to help, hast been  Great in the contest for the prize.

6.45.d: या त ऊतिरमित्रहन मक्षूजवस्तमासति | तया नो हिनुही रथम ||
6.45.e: Slayer of foes, whatever aid of thine imparts the swiftest course,  With that impel our car to speed.

6.45.d: स रथेन रथीतमो.अस्माकेनाभियुग्वना | जेषि जिष्णो हितं धनम ||
6.45.e: As skilfullest of those who drive the chariot, with our art and aim,  O Conqueror, win the proffered prize.

6.45.d: य एक इत तमु षटुहि कर्ष्टीनां विचर्षणिः | पतिर्जज्ञे वर्षक्रतुः ||
6.45.e: Praise him who, Matchless and Alone, was born the Lord of living men,  Most active, with heroic soul.

6.45.d: यो गर्णतामिदासिथापिरूती शिवः सखा | स तवंन इन्द्र मर्ळय ||
6.45.e: Thou who hast been the singers' Friend, a Friend auspicious with thine aid,  As such, O Indra, favour us.

6.45.d: धिष्व वज्रं गभस्त्यो रक्षोहत्याय वज्रिवः | सासहीष्ठा अभि सप्र्धः ||
6.45.e: Grasp in thine arms the thunderbolt, O Thunder-armed, to slay the fiends:  Mayst thou subdue the foemen's host.

6.45.d: परत्नं रयीणां युजं सखायं कीरिचोदनम | बरह्मवाहस्तमं हुवे ||
6.45.e: I call the ancient Friend, allied with wealth, who speeds the lowly man,  Him to whom chiefly prayer is brought.

6.45.d: स हि विश्वानि पार्थिवानेको वसूनि पत्यते | गिर्वणस्तमो अध्रिगुः ||
6.45.e: For he alone is Lord of all the treasures of the earth: he speeds  Hither, chief Lover of the Song.

6.45.d: स नो नियुद्भिरा पर्ण कामं वाजेभिरश्विभिः | गोमद्भिर्गोपते धर्षत ||
6.45.e: So with thy yoked teams satisfy our wish with power and wealth in steeds  And cattle, boldly, Lord of kine!

6.45.d: तद वो गाय सुते सचा पुरुहूताय सत्वने | शं यद गवे ||
6.45.e: Sing this, what time the ' juice is pressed, to him your Hero, Much-invoked,  To please him as a mighty Steer.

6.45.d: न शाकिने ||
6.45.e: He, Excellent, withholdeth not his gift of power and wealth in kine,  When he hath listened to our songs.

6.45.d: न घा वसुर्नि यमते दानं वाजस्य गोमतः | यत सीमुप शरवद गिरः ||
6.45.e: May he with might unclose for us the cow's stall, whosesoe’er it be,  To which the Dasyu-slayer goes.

6.45.d: कुवित्सस्य पर हि वरजं गोमन्तं दस्युहा गमत | शचीभिरप नो वरत ||
6.45.e: O Indra Śatakratu, these our songs have called aloud to thee,  Like mother cows to meet their calves.

6.45.d: इमा उ तवा शतक्रतो.अभि पर णोनुवुर्गिरः | इन्द्र वत्संन मातरः ||
6.45.e: Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers:  Be to one craving steeds a Steed.

6.45.d: दूणाशं सख्यं तव गौरसि वीर गव्यते | अश्वो अश्वायते भव ||
6.45.e: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence:  Yield not thy singer to reproach.

6.45.d: स मन्दस्वा हयन्धसो ... ||
6.45.e: These songs with every draught we pour come, Lover of the Song, to thee,  As milch-kine hasten to their young

6.45.d: इमा उ तवा सुते-सुते नक्षन्ते गिर्वणो गिरः | वत्सं गावोन धेनवः ||
6.45.e: To thee most oft invoked, amid the many singers' rivalry  Who beg with all their might for wealth.

6.45.d: पुरूतमं पुरूणां सतोतॄणां विवाचि | वाजेभिर्वाजयताम ||
6.45.e: Nearest and most attractive may our laud, O Indra come to thee.  Urge thou us on to ample wealth.

6.45.d: अस्माकमिन्द्र भूतु ते सतोमो वाहिष्ठो अन्तमः | अस्मान राये महे हिनु ||
6.45.e: Brbu hath set himself above the Paṇis, o’er their highest head,  Like the wide bush on Gan!gā's bank.

6.45.d: अधि बर्बुः पणीनां वर्षिष्ठे मूर्धन्नस्थात | उरुः कक्षो न गाङगयः ||
6.45.e: He whose good bounty, thousandfold, swift as the rushing of the wind,  Suddenly offers as a gift.

6.45.d: यस्य वायोरिव दरवद भद्रा रातिः सहस्रिणी | सद्यो दानाय मंहते ||
6.45.e: So all our singers ever praise the pious Brbu's noble deed,  Chief, best to give his thousands, best to give a thousand liberal gifts.

6.45.d: तत सु नो विश्वे अर्य आ सदा गर्णन्ति कारवः | बर्बुं सहस्रदातमं सूरिं सहस्रसातमम ||
6.45.e: Missing line from Griffith.

6.46.d: तवामिद धि हवामहे साता वाजस्य कारवः | तवां वर्त्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ||
6.46.e: THAT we may win us wealth and power we poets, verily, call on thee:  In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's race-course call on thee.

6.46.d: स तवं नश्चित्र वज्रहस्त धर्ष्णुया मह सतवानो अद्रिवः | गामश्वं रथ्यमिन्द्र सं किर सत्रा वाजं न जिग्युषे ||
6.46.e: As such, O Wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone!  Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariotsteeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength.

6.46.d: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिन्द्रं तं हूमहे वयम | सहस्रमुष्क तुविन्र्म्ण सत्पते भवा समत्सु नो वर्धे ||
6.46.e: We call upon that Indra, who, most active, ever slays the foe:  Lord of the brave, Most Manly, with a thousand powers, help thou and prosper us in fight.

6.46.d: बाधसे जनान वर्षभेव मन्युना घर्षौ मीळ्ह रचीषम | अस्माकं बोध्यविता महाधने तनूष्वप्सु सूर्ये ||
6.46.e: Rcisama, thou forcest men as with a bull, with anger, in the furious fray.  Be thou our Helper in the mighty battle fought for sunlight, water, and for life.

6.46.d: इन्द्र जयेष्ठं न आ भरनोजिष्ठं पपुरि शरवः | येनेमे चित्र वज्रहस्त रोदसी ओभे सुशिप्र पराः ||
6.46.e: O Indra, bring us name and fame, enriching, mightiest, excellent,  Wherewith, O Wondrous God, fair-visored, thunder-armed, thou hast filled full this earth and heaven.

6.46.d: तवामुग्रमवसे चर्षणीसहं राजन देवेषु हूमहे | विश्वा सु नो विथुरा पिब्दना वसो.अमित्रान सुषहान कर्धि ||
6.46.e: We call on thee, O King, Mighty amid the Gods, Ruler of men, to succour us.  All that is weak in us, Excellent God, make firm: make our foes easy to subdue.

6.46.d: यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वानोजो नर्म्णं च कर्ष्टिषु | यद वापञ्च कषितीनां दयुम्नमा भर सत्रा विश्वानि पौंस्या ||
6.46.e: All strength and valour that is found, Indra, in tribes of Nahusas, and all the splendid fame that the Five Tribes enjoy  Bring, yea, all manly powers at once.

6.46.d: यद वा तर्क्षौ मघवन दरुह्यावा जने यत पूरौ कच्च वर्ष्ण्यम | अस्मभ्यं तद रिरीहि सं नर्षाह्ये.अमित्रान पर्त्सुतुर्वणे ||
6.46.e: Or, Maghavan, what vigorous strength in Trksi lay, in Druhyus or in Paru's folk,  Fully bestow on us, that, in the conquering fray, we may subdue our foes in fight.

6.46.d: इन्द्र तरिधातु शरणं तरिवरूथं सवस्तिमत | छर्दिर्यछ मघवद्भ्यश्च मह्यं च यावया दिद्युमेभ्यः ||
6.46.e: O Indra, grant a happy home, a triple refuge triply strong.  Bestow a dwelling-place on the rich lords and me, and keep thy dart afar from these.

6.46.d: ये गव्यता मनसा शत्रुमादभुरभिप्रघ्नन्ति धर्ष्णुया | अध समा नो मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणस्तनूपा अन्तमो भव ||
6.46.e: They who with minds intent on spoil subdue the foe, boldly attack and smite him down,—  From these, O Indra Maghavan who lovest song, be closest guardian of our lives.

6.46.d: अध समा नो वर्धे भवेन्द्र नायमवा युधि | यदन्तरिक्षेपतयन्ति पर्णिनो दिद्यवस्तिग्ममूर्धानः ||
6.46.e: And now, O Indra, strengthen us: come near and aid us in the fight,  What time the feathered shafts are flying in the air, the arrows with their sharpened points.

6.46.d: यत्र शूरासस्तन्वो वितन्वते परिया शर्म पितॄणाम | अध समा यछ तन्वे तने च छर्दिरचित्तं यावय दवेषः ||
6.46.e: Give us, where heroes strain their bodies in the fight, the shelter that our fathers loved.  To us and to our sons give refuge: keep afar all unobserved hostility.

6.46.d: यदिन्द्र सर्गे अर्वतश्चोदयासे महाधने | असमने अध्वनिव्र्जिने पथि शयेनानिव शरवस्यतह ||
6.46.e: When, Indra, in the mighty fray thou urgest chargers to their speed,  On the uneven road and on a toilsome path, like falcons, eager for renown,

6.46.d: सिन्धून्रिव परवण आशुया यतो यदि कलोशमनु षवणि | आ ये वयो न वर्व्र्तत्यामिषि गर्भीता बाह्वोर्गवि ||
6.46.e: Speeding like rivers rushing down a steep descent, responsive to the urging call,  That come like birds attracted to the bait, held in by reins in both the driver's hands.

6.47.d: सवादुष किलायं मधुमानुतायं तीव्रः किलायं रसवानुतायम | उतो नवस्य पपिवांसमिन्द्रं न कश्चनसहत आहवेषु ||
6.47.e: YEA, this is good to taste and full of. sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour.  No one may conquer Indra in the battle when he hath drunken of the draught we offer.

6.47.d: अयं सवादुरिह मदिष्ठ आस यस्येन्द्रो वर्त्रहत्ये ममाद | पुरूणि यश्च्यौत्ना शम्बरस्य वि नवतिं नव च देह्यो हन ||
6.47.e: This sweet juice here had mightiest power to gladden: it boldened Indra when he siaughtered Vṛtra,  When he defeated Śambara's many onslaughts, and battered down his nineand ninety ramparts.

6.47.d: अयं मे पीत उदियर्ति वचमयं मनीषामुशतीमजीगः | अयं षळ उर्वीरमिमीत धीरो न याभ्यो भुवनं कच्चनारे ||
6.47.e: This stirreth up my voice when I have drunk it: this hath aroused from sleep my yearning spirit.  This Sage hath measured out the six expanses from which no single creature is excluded.

6.47.d: अयं स यो वरिमाणं पर्थिव्या वर्ष्माणं दिवो अक्र्णोदयं सः | अयं पीयूषं तिस्र्षु परवत्सु सोमो दाधारोर्वन्तरिक्षम ||
6.47.e: This, even this, is he who hath created the breadth of earth, the lofty height of heaven.  He formed the nectar in three headlong rivers. Soma supports the wide mid-air above us.

6.47.d: अयं विदच्चित्रद्र्शीकमर्णः शुक्रसद्मनामुषसामनीके | अयं महान महता सकम्भनेनोद दयामस्तभ्नाद वर्षभोमरुत्वान ||
6.47.e: He found the wavy sea of brilliant colours in forefront of the Dawns who dwell in brightness.  This Mighty One, the Steer begirt by Maruts, hath propped the heavens up with a mighty pillar.

6.47.d: धर्षत पिब कलशे सोममिन्द्र वर्त्रहा शूर समरे वसूनाम | माध्यन्दिने सवन आ वर्षस्व रयिस्थानो रयिमस्मासु धेहि ||
6.47.e: Drink Soma boldly from the beaker, Indra, in war for treasures, Hero, Vṛtra-slayer!  Fill thyself full at the mid-day libation, and give us wealth, thou Treasury of riches.

6.47.d: इन्द्र पर णः पुरेतेव पश्य पर नो नय परतरं वस्यो अछ | भवा सुपारो अतिपारयो नो भवा सुनीतिरुत वामनीतिः ||
6.47.e: Look out for us, O Indra, as our Leader, and guide us on to gain yet goodlier treasure.  Excellent Guardian, bear us well through peril, and lead us on to wealth with careful guidance.

6.47.d: उरुं नो लोकमनु नेषि विद्वान सवर्वज्ज्योतिरभयं सवस्ति | रष्वा त इन्द्र सथविरस्य बाहू उप सथेयाम शरणा बर्हन्ता ||
6.47.e: Lead us to ample room, O thou who knowest, to happiness, security, and sunlight.  High, Indra, are the arms of thee the Mighty: may we betake. us to their lofty shelter.

6.47.d: वरिष्ठे न इन्द्र वन्धुरे धा वहिष्ठयोः शतावन्नश्वयोरा | इषमा वक्षीषां वर्षिष्ठां मा नस्तारीन मघवन रायो अर्यः ||
6.47.e: Set us on widest chariot-seat, O Indra, with two steeds best to draw, O Lord of Hundreds!  Bring us the best among all sorts of viands: let not the foe's wealth, Maghavan, subdue us.

6.47.d: इन्द्र मर्ळ मह्यं जीवातुमिछ चोदय धियमयसो न धाराम | यत किं चाहं तवायुरिदं वदामि तज्जुषस्व कर्धि मा देववन्तम ||
6.47.e: Be gracious, Indra, let my days be lengthened: sharpen my thought as ’twere a blade of iron  Approve whatever words I speak, dependent on thee, and grant me thy divine protection.

6.47.d: तरातारमिन्द्रमवितारमिन्द्रं हवे-हवे सुहवं शूरमिन्द्रम | हवयामि शक्रं पुरुहूतमिन्द्रं सवस्ति नो मघवाधात्विन्द्रः ||
6.47.e: Indra the Rescuer, Indra the Helper, Hero who listens at each invocation,  Śakra I call, Indra invoked of many. May Indra Maghavan prosper and bless us.

6.47.d: इन्द्रः सुत्रामा सववानवोभिः सुम्र्ळीको भवतु विश्ववेदाः | बाधतां दवेषो अभयं कर्णोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः सयाम ||
6.47.e: May helpful Indra as our good Protector, Lord of all treasures, favour us with succour,  Baffle our foes, and give us rest and safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour.

6.47.d: तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे सयाम | स सुत्रामा सववानिन्द्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद दवेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ||
6.47.e: May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, may we dwell in his auspicious favour.  May helpful Indra as our good Preserver drive from us, even from afar, our foemen.

6.47.d: अव तवे इन्द्र परवतो नोर्मिर्गिरो बरह्माणि नियुतो धवन्ते | उरू न राधः सवना पुरूण्यपो गा वज्रिन युवसे समिन्दून ||
6.47.e: Like rivers rushing down a slope, O Indra, to thee haste songs and prayers and linked verses.  Thou gatherest, Thunderer! like widespread bounty, kine, water, drops, and manifold libations.

6.47.d: क ईं सतवत कः पर्णात को यजाते यदुग्रमिन मघवा विश्वहावेत | पादाविव परहरन्नन्यम-अन्यं कर्णोति पूर्वमपरं शचीभिः ||
6.47.e: Who lauds him, satisfies him, pays him worship? E’en the rich noble still hath found him mighty.  With power, as when one moves his feet alternate, he makes the last precede, the foremost follow.

6.47.d: शर्ण्वे वीर उग्रम-उग्रं दमायन्नन्यम अन्यमतिनेनीयमानः | एधमानद्विळ उभयस्य राजा चोष्कूयते विश इन्द्रो मनुष्यान ||
6.47.e: Famed is the Hero as each strong man's tamer, ever advancing one and then another.  King of both worlds, hating the high and haughty, Indra protects the men who are his people.

6.47.d: परा पूर्वेषां सख्या वर्णक्ति वितर्तुराणो अपरेभिरेति | अनानुभूतीरवधून्वानः पूर्वीरिन्द्रः शरदस्तर्तरीति ||
6.47.e: He loves no more the men he loved aforetime: he turns and moves away allied with others.  Rejecting those who disregard his worship, Indra victorious lives through many autumns.

6.47.d: रूपं-रूपं परतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं परतिचक्षणाय | इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता हयस्य हरयःशता दश ||
6.47.e: In every figure he hath been the mode: this is his only form for us to look on.  Indra moves multiform by his illusions; for his Bay Steeds are yoked, ten times a hundred.

6.47.d: युजानो हरिता रथे भूरि तवष्टेह राजति | को विश्वाहा दविषतः पक्ष आसत उतासीनेषु सूरिषु ||
6.47.e: Here Tvaṣṭar, yoking to the car the Bay Steeds, hath extended sway.  Who will for ever stand upon the foeman's side, even when our princes sit at ease?

6.47.d: अगव्यूति कषेत्रमागम्न देवा उर्वी सती भूमिरंहूरणाभूत | बर्हस्पते पर चिकित्सा गविष्टावित्था सते जरित्रैन्द्र पन्थाम ||
6.47.e: Gods, we have reached a country void of pasture the land, though spacious, was too small to hold us.  Bṛhaspati, provide in war for cattle; find a path, Indra, for this faithful singer.

6.47.d: दिवे-दिवे सद्र्शीरन्यमर्धं कर्ष्णा असेधतप सद्मनोजाः | अहन दासा वर्षभो वस्नयन्तोदव्रजे वर्चिनं शम्बरं च ||
6.47.e: Day after day far from their seat he drove them, alike, from place to place, those darksome creatures.  The Hero slew the meanly-huckstering Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, where the waters gather.

6.47.d: परस्तोक इन नु राधसस्त इन्द्र दश कोशयीर्दश वाजिनो.अदात | दिवोदासादतिथिग्वस्य राधः शाम्बरं वसु परत्यग्रभीष्म ||
6.47.e: Out of thy bounty, Indra, hath Prastoka bestowed ten coffers and ten mettled horses.  We have received in turn from Divodāsa Śambara's wealth, the gift of Atithigva.

6.47.d: दशाश्वान दश कोशान दश वस्त्राधिभोजना | दशो हिरण्यपिण्डान दिवोदासादसानिषम ||
6.47.e: Ten horses and ten treasure-chests, ten garments as an added gift,  These and ten lumps of gold have I received from Divodāsa's hand.

6.47.d: दश रथान परष्टिमतः शतं गा अथर्वभ्यः | अश्वथः पायवे.अदात ||
6.47.e: Ten cars with extra steed to each, for the Atharvans hundred cows,  Hath Asvatha to Payu given.

6.47.d: महि राधो विश्वजन्यं दधानान भरद्वाजान सार्ञ्जयो अभ्ययष्ट ||
6.47.e: Thus Sṛñjaya's son honoured the Bharadvājas, recipients of all noble gifts and bounty.

6.47.d: वनस्पते वीड्वङगो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा परतरणः सुवीरः | गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ||
6.47.e: Lord of the wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious hero  Show forth thy strength, compact with straps of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle.

6.47.d: दिवस पर्थिव्याः पर्योज उद्भ्र्तं वनस्पतिभ्यः पर्याभ्र्तं सहः | अपामोज्मानं परि गोभिराव्र्तमिन्द्रस्य वज्रं हविषा रथं यज ||
6.47.e: Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood.  Honour with holy gifts the Car like Indra's bolt, the Car bound round with straps, the vigour of the floods.

6.47.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो मरुतामनीकं मित्रस्य गर्भो वरुणस्य नाभिः | सेमां नो हव्यदातिं जुषाणो देव रथ परति हव्या गर्भाय ||
6.47.e: Thou Bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuṇa and Child of Mitra,—  As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O Godlike Chariot, these oblations.

6.47.d: उप शवासय पर्थिवीमुत दयां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत | स दुन्दुभे सजूरिन्द्रेण देवैर्दूराद दवीयोप सेध शत्रून ||
6.47.e: Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee;  O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.

6.47.d: आ करन्दय बलमोजो न आ धा नि षटनिहि दुरिता बाधमानः | अप परोथ दुन्दुभे दुछुना इत इन्द्रस्य मुष्टिरसि वीळयस्व ||
6.47.e: Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers.  Drive hence, O War-drum, drive away misfortune: thou art the Fist of Indra: show thy firmness.

6.47.d: आमूरज परत्यावर्तयेमाः केतुमद दुन्दुभिर्वावदीति | समश्वपर्णाश्चरन्ति नो नरो.अस्माकमिन्द्र रथिनो जयन्तु ||
6.47.e: Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle's signal.  Our heroes, winged with horses, come together. Let our car-warriors, Indra, be triumphant.

6.48.d: यज्ञा-यज्ञा वो अग्नये गिरा-गिरा च दक्षसे | पर-पर वयमम्र्तं जातवेदसं परियं मित्रं न शंसिषम ||
6.48.e: SING to your Agni with each song, at every sacrifice, for strength.  Come, let us praise the Wise and Everlasting God, even as a well-beloved Friend,

6.48.d: ऊर्जो नपातं स हिनायमस्मयुर्दाशेम हव्यदातये | भुवद वाजेष्वविता भुवद वर्ध उत तराता तनूनाम ||
6.48.e: The Son of Strength; for is he not our gracious Lord? Let us serve him who bears our gifts.  In battle may he be our help and strengthener, yea, be the saviour of our lives.

6.48.d: वर्षा हयग्ने अजरो महान विभास्यर्चिषा | अजस्रेण शोचिषा शोशुचच्छुचे सुदीतिभिः सु दीदिहि ||
6.48.e: Agni, thou beamest forth with light, great Hero, never changed by time.  Shining, pure Agni! with a light that never fades, beam with thy fair beams brilliantly.

6.48.d: महो देवान यजसि यक्ष्यानुषक तव करत्वोत दंसना | अर्वाचः सीं कर्णुह्यग्ने.अवसे रास्व वाजोत वंस्व ||
6.48.e: Thou worshippest great Gods: bring them without delay by wisdom and thy wondrous power.  O Agni, make them turn hither to succour us. Give strength, and win it for thyself.

6.48.d: यमापो अद्रयो वना गर्भं रतस्य पिप्रति | सहसा यो मथितो जायते नर्भिः पर्थिव्या अधि सानवि ||
6.48.e: He whom floods, stones, and trees support, the offspring of eternal Law;  He who when rubbed with force is brought to life by men upon the lofty height of earth;

6.48.d: आ यः पप्रौ भानुना रोदसी उभे धूमेन धावते दिवि | तिरस्तमो दद्र्श ऊर्म्यास्वा शयावास्वरुषो वर्षा शयावा अरुषो वर्षा ||
6.48.e: He who hath filled both worlds fult with his brilliant shine, who hastens with his smoke to heaven;  He made himself apparent through the gloom by night, the Red Bull in the darksome nights, the Red Bull in the darksome nights.

6.48.d: बर्हद्भिरग्ने अर्चिभिः शुक्रेण देव शोचिषा | भरद्वाजे समिधानो यविष्ठ्य रेवन नः शुक्र दीदिहि दयुमत पावक दीदिहि ||
6.48.e: O Agni, with thy lofty beams, with thy pure brilliancy, O God,  Kindled, Most Youthful One! by Bharadvāja's hand, shine on us, O pure God, with wealth, shine, Purifier! splendidly.

6.48.d: विश्वासां गर्हपतिर्विशामसि तवमग्ने मानुषीणाम | शतं पूर्भिर्यविष्ठ पाह्यंहसः समेद्धारं शतं हिमा सतोत्र्भ्यो ये च ददति ||
6.48.e: Thou art the Lord of house and home of all the tribes, O Agni, of all tribes of men.  Guard with a hundred forts thy kindler from distress, through hundred winters, Youngest God! and those who make thy singers rich.

6.48.d: तवं नश्चित्र ऊत्या वसो राधांसि चोदय | अस्य रायस्त्वमग्ने रथीरसि विदा गाधं तुचे तु नः ||
6.48.e: Wonderful, with thy favouring help, send us thy bounties, gracious Lord.  Thou art the Charioteer, Agni, of earthly wealth: find rest and safety for our seed.

6.48.d: पर्षि तोकं तनयं पर्त्र्भिष टवमदब्धैरप्रयुत्वभिः | अग्ने हेळांसि दैव्या युयोधि नो.अदेवानि हवरांसि च ||
6.48.e: With guards unfailing never negligent speed thou our children and our progeny.  Keep far from us, O Agni, all celestial wrath and wickedness of godless men.

6.48.d: आ सखायः सबर्दुघां धेनुमजध्वमुप नव्यसा वचः | सर्जध्वमनपस्फुराम ||
6.48.e: Hither, O friends, with newest song drive her who freely pours her milk;  Loose her who never turns away;

6.48.d: या शर्धाय मारुताय सवभानवे शरवो.अम्र्त्यु धुक्षत | या मर्ळीके मरुतां तुराणां या सुम्नैरेवयावरी ||
6.48.e: Who, for the host of Maruts bright with native sheen, hath shed immortal fame like milk;  Whom the impetuous Maruts look upon with love, who moves in splendour on their ways.

6.48.d: भरद्वाजायाव धुक्षत दविता | धेनुं च विश्वदोहसमिषं च विश्वभोजसम ||
6.48.e: For Bharadvāja she poured down in days of old  The milch-cow yielding milk for all, and food that gives all nourishment.

6.48.d: तं व इन्द्रं न सुक्रतुं वरुणमिव मायिनम | अर्यमणं न मन्द्रं सर्प्रभोजसं विष्णुं न सतुष आदिशे ||
6.48.e: Your friend like Indra passing wise, with magic power like Varuṇa.  Like Aryaman joy-giving, bringing plenteous food like ViSnxu for my wish, I praise,

6.48.d: तवेषं शर्धो न मारुतं तुविष्वण्यनर्वाणं पूषणं सं यथा शता | सं सहस्रा कारिषच्चर्षणिभ्य आनाविर्गूळ्हा वसू करत सुवेदा नो वसू करत ||
6.48.e: Bright as the host of Maruts mighty in their roar. May they bring Pūṣan free from foes;  May they bring hither hundreds, thousands for our men: may they bring hidden stores to light, and make wealth easy to be found.

6.48.d: आ मा पूषन्नुप दरव शंसिषं नु ते अपिकर्ण आघ्र्णे | अघा अर्यो अरातयः ||
6.48.e: Haste to me, Pūṣan, in thine car, bright Deity: I fain would speak:  Most sinful is our foeman's hate.

6.48.d: मा काकम्बीरमुद वर्हो वनस्पतिमशस्तीर्वि हि नीनशः | मोत सूरो अह एवा चन गरीवा आदधते वेः ||
6.48.e: Tear not up by the roots the Kakambira tree: destroy thou all malignity.  Let them not snare by day the neck of that Celestial Bird the Sun.

6.48.d: दर्तेरिव ते.अव्र्कमस्तु सख्यम | अछिद्रस्य दधन्वतः सुपूर्णस्य दधन्वतः ||
6.48.e: Uninjured let thy friendship be, like the smooth surface of a skin,  A flawless skin, containing curds, full to the mouth, containing curds.

6.48.d: परो हि मर्त्यैरसि समो देवैरुत शरिया | अभि खयः पूषन पर्तनासु नस्त्वमवा नूनं यथा पुरा ||
6.48.e: For thou art high above mankind, in glory equal to the Gods.  Therefore, O Pūṣan, look upon us in the fight: now help us as in days of old.

6.48.d: वामी वामस्य धूतयः परणीतिरस्तु सून्र्ता | देवस्य वामरुतो मर्त्यस्य वेजानस्य परयज्यवः ||
6.48.e: May the kind excellence of him the Kind, loud Roarers! be our guide,  Be it the God's, O Maruts, or a mortal man's who worships, ye impetuous Ones!

6.48.d: सद्यश्चिद यस्य चर्क्र्तिः परि दयां देवो नैति सूर्यः | तवेषं शवो दधिरे नाम यज्ञियं मरुतो वर्त्रहं शवो जयेष्ठं वर्त्रहं शवः ||
6.48.e: They whose high glory in a moment like the God, the Sun, goes round the space of heaven,  The Maruts have obtained bright strength, a sacred name, strength that destroys the Vṛtras, strength Vṛtra-destroying excellent.

6.48.d: सक्र्द ध दयौरजायत सक्र्द भूमिरजायत | पर्श्न्या दुग्धं सक्र्त पयस्तदन्यो नानु जायते ||
6.48.e: Once, only once, the heaven was made, once only once, the earth was formed-  Once, only Pṛśni's milk was shed: no second, after this, is born.

6.49.d: सतुषे जनं सुव्रतं नव्यसीभिर्गीर्भिर्मित्रावरुणा सुम्नयन्ता | त आ गमन्तु त इह शरुवन्तु सुक्षत्रासो वरुणोमित्रो अग्निः ||
6.49.e: I LAUD with newest songs the Righteous People, Mitra and Varuṇa who make us happy.  Let them approach, here let them listen,Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Lords of fair dominion.

6.49.d: विशो-विश ईड्यमध्वरेष्वद्र्प्तक्रतुमरतिं युवत्योः | दिवः शिशुं सहसः सूनुमग्निं यज्ञस्य केतुमरुषं यजध्यै ||
6.49.e: Him, to be praised at each tribe's sacrifices, the Two young Matrons' sober-minded Herald,  The Son of Strength, the Child of Heaven, the signal of sacrifice, red Agni will I worship.

6.49.d: अरुषस्य दुहितरा विरूपे सत्र्भिरन्या पिपिशे सूरो अन्या | मिथस्तुरा विचरन्ती पावके मन्म शरुतं नक्षत रच्यमाने ||
6.49.e: Unlike in form are the Red God's two Daughters: one is the Sun's, and stars bedeck the other.  Apart, the Sanctifiers, in succession, come to the famed hymn, praised in holy verses.

6.49.d: पर वायुमछा बर्हती मनीषा बर्हद्रयिं विश्ववारं रथप्राम | दयुतद्यामा नियुतः पत्यमानः कविः कविमियक्षसि परयज्यो ||
6.49.e: I with a lofty song call hither Vāyu, all-bounteous, filler of his car, most wealthy.  Thou, Sage, with bright path, Lord of harnessed horses, impetuous, promptly honourest the prudent.

6.49.d: स मे वपुश्छदयदश्विनोर्यो रथो विरुक्मान मनसा युजानः | येन नरा नासत्येषयध्यै वर्तिर्याथस्तनयाय तमने च ||
6.49.e: That chariot of the Aśvins, fair to look on, pleaseth me well, yoked with a thought, refulgent,  Wherewith, Nāsatyas, Chiefs, ye seek our dwelling, to give new strength to us and to our children.

6.49.d: पर्जन्यवाता वर्षभा पर्थिव्याः पुरीषाणि जिन्वतमप्यानि | सत्यश्रुतः कवयो यस्य गीर्भिर्जगत सथातर्जगदाक्र्णुध्वम ||
6.49.e: Bulls of the Earth, O Vāta and Parjanya, stir up for us the regions of the water.  Hearers of truth, ye, Sages, World-Supporters, increase his living wealth whose songs delight you.

6.49.d: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः सरस्वती वीरपत्नी धियं धात | गनाभिरछिद्रं शरणं सजोषा दुराधर्षं गर्णते शर्म यंसत ||
6.49.e: So may Sarasvatī, the Hero's Consort, brisk with rare life, the lightning's Child, inspire us,  And, with the Dames accordant, give the singer a refuge unassailable and flawless.

6.49.d: पथस-पथः परिपतिं वचस्या कामेन कर्तो अभ्यानळ अर्कम | स नो रासच्छुरुधश्चन्द्राग्रा धियं-धियं सीषधाति पर पूषा ||
6.49.e: I praise with eloquence him who guards all pathways. He, when his love impelled him, went to Arka.  May he vouchsafe us gear with gold to grace it: may Pūṣan make each prayer of ours efective.

6.49.d: परथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सुपाणिं देवं सुगभस्तिं रभ्वम | होता यक्षद यजतं पस्त्यानामग्निस्त्वष्टारं सुहवं विभावा ||
6.49.e: May Herald Agni, fulgent, bring for worship Tvaṣṭar adored, in homes and swift to listen,  Glorious, first to share, the life-bestower, the ever active God, fair-armed, fair-handed.

6.49.d: भुवनस्य पितरं गीर्भिराभी रुद्रं दिवा वर्धया रुद्रमक्तौ | बर्हन्तं रष्वमजरं सुषुम्नं रधग घुवेम कविनेषितासः ||
6.49.e: Rudra by day, Rudra at night we honour with these our songs, the Universe's Father.  Him great and lofty, blissful, undecaying let us call specially as the Sage impels us.

6.49.d: आ युवानः कवयो यज्ञियासो मरुतो गन्त गर्णतो वरस्याम | अचित्रं चिद धि जिन्वथा वर्धन्त इत्था नक्षन्तो नरो अङगिरस्वत ||
6.49.e: Ye who are youthful, wise, and meet for worship, come, Martits, to the longing of the singer.  Coming, as erst to Aṅgiras, O Heroes, ye animate and quicken e’en the desert.

6.49.d: पर वीराय पर तवसे तुरायाजा यूथेव पशुरक्षिरस्तम | स पिस्प्र्शति तन्वि शरुतस्य सत्र्भिर्न नाकं वचनस्यविपः ||
6.49.e: Even as the herdsman driveth home his cattle, I urge my songs to him the strong swift Hero  May he, the glorious, lay upon his body the singer's hymns, as stars bedeck the heaven.

6.49.d: यो रजांसि विममे पार्थिवानि तरिश्चिद विष्णुर्मनवे बाधिताय | तस्य ते शर्मन्नुपदद्यमाने राया मदेम तन्वा तना च ||
6.49.e: He who for man's behoof in his afiliction thrice measured out the earthly regions, Viṣṇu-  When one so great as thou affordeth shelter, may we with wealth and with ourselves be happy.

6.49.d: तन नो.अहिर्बुध्न्यो अब्धिरर्कैस्तत पर्वतस्तत सविता चनो धात | तदोषधीभिरभि रातिषाचो भगः पुरन्धिर्जिन्वतु पर राये ||
6.49.e: Sweet be this song of mine to Ahibudhnya, Parvata, Savitar, with Floods and Lightnings;  Sweet, with the Plants, to Gods who seek oblations. May liberal Bhaga speed us on to riches.

6.49.d: नु नो रयिं रथ्यं चर्षणिप्रां पुरुवीरं मह रतस्य गोपाम | कषयं दाताजरं येन जनान सप्र्धो अदेवीरभि चक्रमाम विश आदेवीरभ्यश्नवाम ||
6.49.e: Give riches borne on cars, with many heroes, contenting men, the guard of mighty Order.  Give us a lasting home that we may battle with godless bands of men who fight against us, and meet with tribes to whom the Gods are gracious.

6.50.d: हुवे वो देवीमदितिं नमोभिर्म्र्ळीकाय वरुणं मित्रमग्निम | अभिक्षदामर्यमणं सुशेवं तरातॄन देवान सवितारं भगं च ||
6.50.e: I CALL with prayers on Aditi your Goddess, on Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa for favour,  On Aryaman who gives unasked, the gracious, on Gods who save, on Savitar and Bhaga.

6.50.d: सुज्योतिषः सूर्य दक्षपितॄननागास्त्वे सुमहो वीहि देवान | दविजन्मानो य रतसापः सत्याः सवर्वन्तो यजता अग्निजिह्वाः ||
6.50.e: Visit, to prove us free from sin, O Sūrya Lord of great might, the bright Gods sprung from Dakṣa,  Twice-born and true, observing sacred duties, Holy and full of light, whose tongue is Agni.

6.50.d: उत दयावाप्र्थिवी कषत्रमुरु बर्हद रोदसी शरणं सुषुम्ने | महस करथो वरिवो यथा नो.अस्मे कषयाय धिषणे अनेहः ||
6.50.e: And, O ye Heaven and Earth, a wide dominion, O ye most blissful Worlds, our lofty shelter,  Give ample room and freedom for our dwelling, a home, ye Hemispheres, which none may rival.

6.50.d: आ नो रुद्रस्य सूनवो नमन्तामद्या हूतासो वसवो.अध्र्ष्टाः | यदीमर्भे महति वा हितासो बाधे मरुतो अह्वाम देवान ||
6.50.e: This day invited may the Sons of Rudra, resistless, excellent, stoop down to meet us;  For, when beset with slight or sore affliction, we ever call upon the Gods, the Maruts;

6.50.d: मिम्यक्ष येषु रोदसी नु देवी सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्धयज्वा | शरुत्वा हवं मरुतो यद ध याथ भूमा रेजन्ते अध्वनि परविक्ते ||
6.50.e: To whom the Goddess Rodasī clings closely, whom Pūṣan follows bringing ample bounty.  What time ye hear our call and come, O Maruts, upon your separate path all creatures tremble.

6.50.d: अभि तयं वीरं गिर्वणसमर्चेन्द्रं बरह्मणा जरितर्नवेन | शरवदिद धवमुप च सतवानो रासद वाजानुप महो गर्णानः ||
6.50.e: With a new hymn extol, O thou who singest, the Lover of the Song, the Hero Indra.  May he, exalted, hear our invocation, and grant us mighty wealth and strength when lauded.

6.50.d: ओमानमापो मानुषीरम्र्क्तं धात तोकाय तनयाय शंयोः | यूयं हि षठा भिषजो मात्र्तमा विश्वस्य सथातुर्जगतो जनित्रीः ||
6.50.e: Give full protection, Friends of man, ye Waters, in peace and trouble, to our sons and grandsons.  For ye are our most motherly physicians, parents of all that standeth, all that moveth.

6.50.d: आ नो देवः सविता तरायमाणो हिरण्यपाणिर्यजतो जगम्यात | यो दत्रवानुषसो न परतीकं वयूर्णुते दाशुषे वार्याणि ||
6.50.e: May Savitar come hither and approach us, the God who rescues, Holy, goldenhanded,  The God who, bounteous as the face of Morning, discloses precious gifts for him who worships.

6.50.d: उत तवं सूनो सहसो नो अद्या देवानस्मिन्नध्वरे वव्र्त्याः | सयामहं ते सदमिद रातौ तव सयामग्ने.अवसा सुवीरः ||
6.50.e: And thou, O Son of Strength, do thou turn hither the Gods to-day to this our holy service.  May I for evermore enjoy thy bounty and, Agni, by thy grace be rich in heroes.

6.50.d: उत तया मे हवमा जग्म्यातं नासत्या धीभिर्युवमङग विप्रा | अत्रिं न महस्तमसो.अमुमुक्तं तूर्वतं नरा दुरितादभीके ||
6.50.e: Come also to my call, O ye Nāsatyas, yea, verily, through my prayers, ye Holy Sages.  As from great darkness ye delivered Atri, protect us, Chiefs, from danger in the conflict.

6.50.d: ते नो रायो दयुमतो वाजवतो दातारो भूत नर्वतः पुरुक्षोः | दशस्यन्तो दिव्याः पार्थिवासो गोजाता अप्या मर्लता चदेवाः ||
6.50.e: O Gods, bestow upon us riches, splendid with strength and heroes, bringing food in plenty.  Be gracious, helpful Gods of earth, of heaven, born of the Cow, and dwellers in the waters.

6.50.d: ते नो रुद्रः सरस्वती सजोषा मीळ्हुष्मन्तो विष्णुर्म्र्ळन्तु वायुः | रभुक्षा वाजो दैव्यो विधाता पर्जन्यावाता पिप्यतामिषं नः ||
6.50.e: May Rudra and Sarasvatī, accordant, Viṣṇu and Vāyu, pour down gifts and bless us;  Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and divine Vidhatar, Parjanya, Vāta make our food abundant.

6.50.d: उत सय देवः सविता भगो नो.अपां नपादवतु दानु पप्रिः | तवष्टा देवेभिर्जनिभिः सजोषा दयौर्देवेभिः पर्थिवी समुद्रैः ||
6.50.e: May this God Savitar, the Lord, the Offspring of Waters, pouring down his dew be gracious,  And, with the Gods and Dames accordant, Tvaṣṭar; Dyaus with the Gods and Prthivi with oceans.

6.50.d: उत नो.अहिर्बुध्न्यः शर्णोत्वज एकपात पर्थिवी समुद्रः | विश्वे देवा रताव्र्धो हुवाना सतुता मन्त्राः कविशस्ता अवन्तु ||
6.50.e: May Aja-Ekapād and Ahibudhnya, and Earth and Ocean hear our invocation;  All Gods who strengthen Law, invoked and lauded, and holy texts uttered by sages, help us.

6.50.d: एवा नपातो मम तस्य धीभिर्भरद्वाजा अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः | गना हुतासो वसवो.अध्र्ष्टा विश्वे सतुतासो भूता यजत्राः ||
6.50.e: So with my thoughts and hymns of praise the children of Bharadvāja sing aloud to please you.  The Dames invoked, and the resistless Vasus, and all ye Holy Ones have been exalted.

6.51.d: उदु तयच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरानेति परियं वरुणयोरदब्धम | रतस्य शुचि दर्शतमनीकं रुक्मो न दिव उदिताव्यद्यौत ||
6.51.e: THAT mighty eye of Varuṇa and Mitra, infallible and dear, is moving upward.  The pure and lovely face of holy Order hath shone like gold of heaven in its arising.

6.51.d: वेद यस्त्रीणि विदथान्येषां देवानां जन्म सनुतरा च विप्रः | रजु मर्तेषु वर्जिना च पश्यन्नभि चष्टे सूरो अर्य एवान ||
6.51.e: The Sage who knows these Gods’ three ranks and orders, and all their generations near and distant,  Beholding good and evil acts of mortals, Sūra marks well the doing of the pious.
