6.51.d: सतुष उ वो मह रतस्य गोपानदितिं मित्रं वरुणं सुजातान | अर्यमणं भगमदब्धधीतीनछा वोचे सधन्यः पावकान ||
6.51.e: I praise you Guards of mighty Law eternal, Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, the noble,  Aryaman, Bhaga, all whose thoughts are faithful: hither I call the Bright who share in common.

6.51.d: रिशादसः सत्पतीन्रदब्धान महो राज्ञः सुवसनस्य दातॄन | यूनः सुक्षत्रान कषयतो दिवो नॄनादित्यान याम्यदितिं दुवोयु ||
6.51.e: Lords of the brave, infallible, foe-destroyers, great Kings, bestowers of fair homes to dwell in,  Young, Heroes, ruling heaven with strong dominion, Ādityas, Aditi I seek with worship.

6.51.d: दयौष पितः पर्थिवि मातरध्रुगग्ने भरातर्वसवो मर्ळता नः | विश्व आदित्या अदिते सजोषा अस्मभ्यं शर्म बहुलं वि यन्त ||
6.51.e: O Heaven our Father, Earth our guileless Mother, O Brother Agni, and ye Vasus, bless us.  Grant us, O Aditi and ye Ādityas, all of one mind, your manifold protection.

6.51.d: मा नो वर्काय वर्क्ये समस्मा अघायते रीरधता यजत्राः | यूयं हि षठा रथ्यो नस्तनूनां यूयं दक्षस्य वचसो बभूव ||
6.51.e: Give us not up to any evil creature, as spoil to wolf or she-wolf, O ye Holy.  For ye are they who guide aright our bodies, ye are the rulers of our speech and vigour.

6.51.d: मा व एनो अन्यक्र्तं भुजेम मा तत कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे | विश्वस्य हि कषयथ विश्वदेवाः सवयं रिपुस्तन्वं रीरिषीष्ट ||
6.51.e: Let us not suffer for the sin of others, nor do the deed which ye, O Vasus, punish.  Ye, Universal Gods! are all-controllers: may he do harm unto himself who hates Me.

6.51.d: नम इदुग्रं नम आ विवासे नमो दाधार पर्थिवीमुत दयाम | नमो देवेभ्यो नम ईश एषां कर्तं चिदेनो नमसाविवासे ||
6.51.e: Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven.  Homage to Gods! Homage commands and rules them. I banish even committed sin by homage

6.51.d: रतस्य वो रथ्यः पूतदक्षान रतस्य पस्त्यसदो अदब्धान | ताना नमोभिरुरुचक्षसो नॄन विश्वान व आ नमे महो यजत्राः ||
6.51.e: You Furtherers of Law, pure in your spirit, infallible, dwellers in the home of Order,  To you all Heroes mighty and far-seeing I bow me down, O Holy Ones, with homage.

6.51.d: ते हि शरेष्ठवर्चसस्त उ नस्तिरो विश्वानि दुरिता नयन्ति | सुक्षत्रासो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निरतधीतयो वक्मराजसत्याः ||
6.51.e: For these are they who shine with noblest splendour; through all our troubles these conduct us safely-  Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, mighty Rulers, trueminded, faithful to the hymn's controllers.

6.51.d: ते न इन्द्रः पर्थिवी कषाम वर्धन पूषा भगो अदितिः पञ्च जनाः | सुशर्माणः सववसः सुनीथा भवन्तु नःसुत्रात्रासः सुगोपाः ||
6.51.e: May they, Earth, Aditi, Indra, Bhaga, Pūṣan increase our laud, increase the Fivefold people.  Giving good help, good refuge, goodly guidance, be they our good deliverers, good protectors.

6.51.d: नू सद्मानं दिव्यं नंशि देवा भारद्वाजः सुमतिं याति होता | आसानेभिर्यजमानो मियेधैर्देवानां जन्म वसूयुर्ववन्द ||
6.51.e: Come now, O Gods, to your celestial station: the Bharadvājas' priest entreats your favour.  He, sacrificing, fain for wealth, hath honoured the Gods vath those who sit and share oblations.

6.51.d: अप तयं वर्जिनं रिपुं सतेनमग्ने दुराध्यम | दविष्ठमस्य सत्पते कर्धी सुगम ||
6.51.e: Agni, drive thou the wicked foe, the evil-hearted thief away,  Far, far, Lord of the brave I and give us easy paths.

6.51.d: गरावाणः सोम नो हि कं सखित्वनाय वावशुः | जही नयत्रिणं पणिं वर्को हि षः ||
6.51.e: Soma, these pressing-stones have called aloud to win thee for our Friend.  Destroy the greedy Paṇi, for a wolf is he.

6.51.d: यूयं हि षठा सुदानव इन्द्रज्येष्ठा अभिद्यवः | कर्ता नो अध्वन्ना सुगं गोपा अमा ||
6.51.e: Ye, O most bountiful, are they who, led by Indra, seek the sky.  Give us good paths for travel: guard us ivell at home.

6.51.d: अपि पन्थामगन्महि सवस्तिगामनेहसम | येन विश्वाः परिद्विषो वर्णक्ति विन्दते वसु ||
6.51.e: Now have we entered on the road that leads to bliss, without a foe,  The road whereon a man escapes all enemies and gathers wealth.

6.52.d: न तद दिवा न पर्थिव्यानु मन्ये न यज्ञेन नोत शमीभिराभिः | उब्जन्तु तं सुभ्वः पर्वतासो नि हीयतामतियाजस्य यष्टा ||
6.52.e: THIS I allow not in the earth or heaven, at sacrifice or in these holy duties.  May the huge mountains crush him down: degraded be Atiyaja's sacrificing patron.

6.52.d: अति वा यो मरुतो मन्यते नो बरह्म वा यः करियमाणं निनित्सात | तपूंषि तस्मै वर्जिनानि सन्तु बरह्मद्विषमभि तं शोचतु दयौः ||
6.52.e: Or he who holds us in contempt, O Maruts, or seeks to blame the prayer that we are making,  May agonies of burning be his portion. May the sky scorch the man who hates devotion.

6.52.d: किमङग तवा बरह्मणः सोम गोपां किमङग तवाहुरभिशस्तिपां नः | किमङग नः पश्यसि निद्यमानान बरह्मद्विषे तपुषिं हेतिमस्य ||
6.52.e: Why then, O Soma, do they call thee keeper of prayer? Why then our guardian from reproaches?  Why then beholdest thou how men revile us? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion.

6.52.d: अवन्तु मामुषसो जायमाना अवन्तु मा सिन्धवः पिन्वमानाः | अवन्तु मा पर्वतासो धरुवासो.अवन्तु मा पितरो देवहूतौ ||
6.52.e: May Mornings as they spring to life, protect me, and may the Rivers as they swell preserve me.  My guardians be the firmly-seated mountains: the Fathers, when I call on Gods, defend me!

6.52.d: विश्वदानीं सुमनसः सयाम पश्येम नु सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम | तथा करद वसुपतिर्वसूनां देवानोहानो.अवसागमिष्ठः ||
6.52.e: Through all our days may we be healthy. minded, and look upon the Sun when he arises.  Grant this the Treasure-Lord of treasures, coming, observant, oftenest of Gods, with succour!

6.52.d: इन्द्रो नेदिष्ठमवसागमिष्ठः सरस्वती सिन्धुभिः पिन्वमाना | पर्जन्यो न ओषधीभिर्मयोभुरग्निः सुशंसः सुहवः पितेव ||
6.52.e: Most near, most oft comes Indra with protection, and she Sarasvatī, who swells with rivers -  Parjanya, bringing health with herbs, and Agni, well lauded swift to listen, like a father.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवास आ गत शर्णुता म इमं हवम | एदं बर्हिर्नि षीदत ||
6.52.e: Hear this mine invocation; come hither, O Universal Gods,  Be seated on this holy grass.

6.52.d: यो वो देवा घर्तस्नुना हव्येन परतिभूषति | तं विश्व उप गछथ ||
6.52.e: To him who comes to meet you, Gods, with offerings bathed in holy oil-  Approach ye, one and all, to him.

6.52.d: उप नः सूनवो गिरः शर्ण्वन्त्वम्र्तस्य ये | सुम्र्ळीका भवन्तु नः ||
6.52.e: All Sons of Immortality shall listen to the songs we sing,  And be exceeding good to us.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवा रताव्र्ध रतुभिर्हवनश्रुतः | जुषन्तां युज्यं पयः ||
6.52.e: May all the Gods who strengthen Law, with Ṛtus, listening to our call,  Be pleased with theit appropriate draught.

6.52.d: सतोत्रमिन्द्रो मरुद्गणस्त्वष्ट्र्मान मित्रो अर्यमा | इमा हव्या जुषन्त नः ||
6.52.e: May Indra, with the Marut host, with Tvaṣṭar, Mitra, Aryaman,  Accept the laud and these our gifts.

6.52.d: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं होतर्वयुनशो यज | चिकित्वान दैव्यं जनम ||
6.52.e: O Agni, Priest, as rules ordain, offer this sacrifice of ours,  Remembering the Heavenly Folk.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवाः शर्णुतेमं हवं मे ये अन्तरिक्षे य उप दयवि षठ | ये अग्निजिह्वा उत वा यजत्रा आसद्यास्मिन बर्हिषि मादयध्वम ||
6.52.e: Listen, All-Gods, to this mine invocation, Ye who inhabit heaven, and air's midregions,  All ye, O Holy Ones, whose tongue is Agni, seated upon this sacred grass, be joyful.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवा मम शर्ण्वन्तु यज्ञिया उभे रोदसी अपां नपाच्च मन्म | मा वो वचांसि परिचक्ष्याणि वोचं सुम्नेष्विद वो अन्तमा मदेम ||
6.52.e: May the All-Gods who claim our worship hear my thought; may the two World-halves hear it, and the Waters’ Child.  Let me not utter words that ye may disregard. Closely allied with you may we rejoice in bliss.

6.52.d: ये के च जमा महिनो अहिमाया दिवो जज्ञिरे अपां सधस्थे | ते अस्मभ्यमिषये विश्वमायुः कषप उस्रा वरिवस्यन्तुदेवाः ||
6.52.e: And those who, Mighty, with the wiles of serpents, were born on earth, in heaven, where waters gather-  May they vouchsafe us life of full duration. May the Gods kindly give us nights and mornings.

6.52.d: अग्नीपर्जन्याववतं धियं मे.अस्मिन हवे सुहवा सुष्टुतिंनः | इळामन्यो जनयद गर्भमन्यः परजावतीरिष आ धत्तमस्मे ||
6.52.e: At this my call, O Agni and Parjanya, help, swift to hear, my thought and our laudation.  One generates holy food, the other offspring, so grant us food enough with store of children.

6.52.d: सतीर्णे बर्हिषि समिधाने अग्नौ सूक्तेन महा नमसा विवासे | अस्मिन नो अद्य विदथे यजत्रा विश्वे देवा हविषि मादयध्वम ||
6.52.e: When holy grass is strewn and fire enkindled, with hymn and lowly homage I invite you.  All-Gods, to day in this our great assembly rejoice, ye Holy, in the gifts we offer.

6.53.d: वयमु तवा पथस पते रथं न वाजसातये | धिये पूषन्नयुज्महि ||
6.53.e: LORD of the path, O Pūṣan, we have yoked and bound thee to our hymn,  Even as a car, to win the prize.

6.53.d: अभि नो नर्यं वसु वीरं परयतदक्षिणम | वामं गर्हपतिं नय ||
6.53.e: Bring us the wealth that men require, a manly master of a house,  Free-handed with the liberal meed.

6.53.d: अदित्सन्तं चिदाघ्र्णे पूषन दानाय चोदय | पणेश्चिद विम्रदा मनः ||
6.53.e: Even him who would not give, do thou,  O glowing Pūṣan, urge to give,  And make the niggard's soul grow soft.

6.53.d: वि पथो वाजसातये चिनुहि वि मर्धो जहि | साधन्तामुग्र नो धियः ||
6.53.e: Clear paths that we may win the prize; scatter our enemies afar.  Strong God, be all our thoughts fulfilled.

6.53.d: परि तर्न्धि पणीनामारया हर्दया कवे | अथेमस्मभ्यं रन्धय ||
6.53.e: Penetrate with an awl, O Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,  And make them subject to our will.

6.53.d: वि पूषन्नारया तुद पणेरिछ हर्दि परियम | अथें ... ||
6.53.e: Thrust with thine awl, O Pūṣan: seek that which the niggard's heart holds dear,  And make him subject to our will.

6.53.d: आ रिख किकिरा कर्णु पणीनां हर्दया कवे | अथें ... ||
6.53.e: Tear up and read in pieces, Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,  And make them subject to our will.

6.53.d: यां पूषन बरह्मचोदनीमारां बिभर्ष्याघ्र्णे | तया समस्य हर्दयमा रिख किकिरा कर्णु ||
6.53.e: Thou, glowing Pūṣan, carriest an awl that urges men to prayer;  Therewith do thou tear up and rend to shreds the heart of every one.

6.53.d: या ते अष्ट्रा गोोपशाघ्र्णे पशुसाधनी | तस्यास्ते सुम्नमीमहे ||
6.53.e: Thou bearest, glowing Lord! a goad with horny point that guides the cows  Thence do we seek thy gift of bliss.

6.53.d: उत नो गोषणिं धियमश्वसां वाजसामुत | नर्वत कर्णुहि वीतये ||
6.53.e: And make this hymn of ours produce kine, horses, and a store of wealth  For our delight and use as men.

6.54.d: सं पूषन विदुषा नय यो अञ्जसानुशासति | य एवेदमिति बरवत ||
6.54.e: O PUSAN, bring us to the man who knows, who shall direct us straight,  And say unto us, It is here.

6.54.d: समु पूष्णा गमेमहि यो गर्हानभिशासति | इम एवेति चब्रवत ||
6.54.e: May we go forth with Pūṣan who shall point the houses out to us,  And say to us, These same are they.

6.54.d: पूष्णश्चक्रं न रिष्यति न कोशो.अव पद्यते | नो अस्य वयथते पविः ||
6.54.e: Unharmed is Pūṣan's chariot wheel; the box ne’er falleth to the ground,  Nor doth the loosened felIy shake.

6.54.d: यो अस्मै हविषाविधन न तं पूषापि मर्ष्यते | परथमो विदते वसु ||
6.54.e: Pūṣan forgetteth not the man who serveth him with offered gift:  That man is first to gather wealth.

6.54.d: पूषा गा अन्वेतु नः पुषा रक्षत्वर्वतः | पूषा वाजं सनोतु नः ||
6.54.e: May Pūṣan follow near our kine; may Pūṣan keep our horses safe:  May Pūṣan gather gear for us.

6.54.d: पूषन्ननु पर गा इहि यजमानस्य सुन्वतः | अस्माकं सतुवतामुत ||
6.54.e: Follow the kine of him who pours libations out and worships thee;  And ours who sing thee songs of praise.

6.54.d: माकिर्नेशन माकीं रिषन माकीं सं शारि केवटे | अथारिष्टाभिरा गहि ||
6.54.e: Let none be lost, none injured, none sink in a pit and break a limb.  Return with these all safe and sound.
Pūṣan who listens to our prayers, the Strong whose wealth is never lost,  The Lord of riches, we implore.

6.54.d: पूषन तव वरते वयं न रिष्येम कदा चन | सतोतारस्त इह समसि ||
6.54.e: Secure in thy protecting care, O Pūṣan, never may we fail.  We here are they who sing thy praise.

6.54.d: परि पूषा परस्ताद धस्तं दधातु दक्षिणम | पुनर्नो नष्टमाजतु ||
6.54.e: From out the distance, far and wide, may Pūṣan stretch his right hand forth,  And drive our lost again to us.

6.55.d: एहि वां विमुचो नपादाघ्र्णे सं सचावहै | रथीरतस्य नो भव ||
6.55.e: SON of Deliverance, come, bright God!  Let us twain go together: be our charioteer of sacrifice.

6.55.d: रथीतमं कपर्दिनमीशानं राधसो महः | रायः सखायमीमहे ||
6.55.e: We pray for wealth to thee most skilled of charioteers, with braided hair,  Lord of great riches, and our Friend.

6.55.d: रायो धारास्याघ्र्णे वसो राशिरजाश्व | धीवतो-धीवतः सखा ||
6.55.e: Bright God whose steeds are goats, thou art a stream of wealth, a treasure-heap,  The Friend of every pious man.

6.55.d: पूषणं नवजाश्वमुप सतोषाम वाजिनम | सवसुर्यो जार उच्यते ||
6.55.e: Pūṣan, who driveth goats for steeds, the strong and Mighty, who is called  His Sister's lover, will we laud.

6.55.d: मातुर्दिधिषुमब्रवं सवसुर्जारः शर्णोतु नः | भरातेन्द्रस्य सखा मम ||
6.55.e: His Mother's suitor I address. May he who loves his Sister hear,  Brother of Indra, and my Friend.

6.55.d: आजासः पूषणं रथे निश्र्म्भास्ते जनश्रियम | देवं वहन्तु बिभ्रतः ||
6.55.e: May the sure-footed goats come nigh, conveying Pūṣan on his car,  The God who visiteth mankind.

6.56.d: य एनमादिदेशति करम्भादिति पूषणम | न तेन देव आदिशे ||
6.56.e: WHOSO remembers Pūṣan as cater of mingled curd and meal  Need think no more upon the God.

6.56.d: उत घा स रथीतमः सख्या सत्पतिर्युजा | इन्द्रो वर्त्राणि जिघ्नते ||
6.56.e: And he is best of charioteers. Indra, the hero's Lord, allied  With him as Friend, destroys the foes.

6.56.d: उतादः परुषे गवि सूरश्चक्रं हिरण्ययम | नयैरयद्रथीतमः ||
6.56.e: And there the best of charioteers hath guided through the speckled cloud  The golden wheel of Sūra's car.

6.56.d: यदद्य तवा पुरुष्टुत बरवाम दस्र मन्तुमः | तत सु नो मन्म साधय ||
6.56.e: Whate’er we speak this day to thee, Wise, Wondrous God whom many praise,  Give thou fulfilment of our thought.

6.56.d: इमं च नो गवेषणं सातये सीषधो गणम | आरात पूषन्नसि शरुतः ||
6.56.e: Lead on this company of ours, that longs for kine, to win the spoil:  Thou, Pūṣan, art renowned afar.

6.56.d: आ ते सवस्तिमीमह आरेघामुपावसुम | अद्या च सर्वतातये शवश्च सर्वतातये ||
6.56.e: Prosperity we crave from thee, afar from sin and near to wealth,  Tending to perfect happiness both for to. morrow and to-day.

6.57.d: इन्द्रा नु पूषणा वयं सख्याय सवस्तये | हुवेम वाजसातये ||
6.57.e: INDRA and Pūṣan will we call for friend ship and prosperity  And for the winning of the spoil.

6.57.d: सोममन्य उपासदत पातवे चम्वोः सुतम | करम्भमन्य इछति ||
6.57.e: One by the Soma sits to drink juice which the mortar hath expressed:  The other longs for curd and meal.

6.57.d: अजा अन्यस्य वह्नयो हरी अन्यस्य सम्भ्र्ता | ताभ्यां वर्त्राणि जिघ्नते ||
6.57.e: Goats are the team that draws the one: the other hath Bay Steeds at hand;  With both of these he slays the fiends.

6.57.d: यदिन्द्रो अनयद रितो महीरपो वर्षन्तमः | तत्र पूषाभवत सचा ||
6.57.e: When Indra, wondrous strong, brought down the streams, the mighty waterfloods,  Pūṣan was standing by his side.

6.57.d: तां पूष्णः सुमतिं वयं वर्क्षस्य पर वयामिव | इन्द्रस्य चा रभामहे ||
6.57.e: To this, to Pūṣan's favouring love, and Indra's, may we closely cling,  As to a tree's extended bough.

6.57.d: उत पूषणं युवामहे.अभीशून्रिव सारथिः | मह्या इन्द्रं सवस्तये ||
6.57.e: As one who drives a car draws in his reins, may we draw Pūṣan near,  And Indra, for our great success.

6.58.d: शुक्रं ते अन्यद यजतं ते अन्यद विषुरूपे अहनी दयौरिवासि | विश्वा हि माया अवसि सवधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निहरातिरस्तु ||
6.58.e: LIKE heaven art thou: one form is bright, one holy, like Day and Night dissimilar in colour.  All magic powers thou aidest, self-depen. dent! Auspicious be thy bounty here, O Pūṣan.

6.58.d: अजाश्वः पशुपा वाजपस्त्यो धियंजिन्वो भुवने विश्वे अर्पितः | अष्ट्रां पूषा शिथिरामुद्वरीव्र्जत संचक्षाणोभुवना देव ईयते ||
6.58.e: Goat-borne, the guard of cattle, he whose home is strength, inspirer of the hymn, set over all the world;  Brandishing here and there his lightly. moving goad, beholding every creature, Pūṣan, God, goes forth.

6.58.d: यास्ते पूषन नावो अन्तः समुद्रे हिरण्ययीरन्तरिक्षे चरन्ति | ताभिर्यासि दूत्यां सूर्यस्य कामेन कर्त शरव इछमानः ||
6.58.e: O Pūṣan, with thy golden ships that travel across the ocean, in the air's mid-region,  Thou goest on an embassy to Sūrya, subdued by love, desirous of the glory.

6.58.d: पूषा सुबन्धुर्दिव आ पर्थिव्या इळस पतिर्मघवा दस्मवर्चाः | यं देवासो अददुः सूर्यायै कामेन कर्तं तवसं सवञ्चम ||
6.58.e: Near kinsman of the heaven and earth is Pūṣan, liberal, Lord of food, of wondrous iustre,  Whom strong and vigorous and swiftlymoving, subdued by love, the Deities gave to Sūrya.

6.59.d: पर नु वोचा सुतेषु वां वीर्या यानि चक्रथुः | हतासो वां पितरो देवशत्रव इन्द्राग्नी जीवथो युवम ||
6.59.e: I WILL declare, while juices flow, the manly deeds that ye have done:  Your Fathers, enemies of Gods, were smitten down, and, Indra-Agni, ye survive.

6.59.d: बळ इत्था महिमा वामिन्द्राग्नी पनिष्ठ आ | समानो वां जनिता भरातरा युवं यमाविहेहमातरा ||
6.59.e: Thus, Indra-Agnip verily your greatness merits loftiest praise,  Sprung from one common Father, brothers, twins are ye; your Mother is in every place.

6.59.d: ओकिवांसा सुते सचानश्वा सप्ती इवादने | इन्द्रा नवग्नी अवसेह वज्रिणा वयं देवा हवामहे ||
6.59.e: These who delight in flowing juice, like fellow horses at their food,  Indra and Agni, Gods armed with the thunderbolt, we call this day to come with help.

6.59.d: य इन्द्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सतवत तेष्व रताव्र्धा | जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ||
6.59.e: Indra and Agni, Friends of Law, served with rich gifts, your speech is kind  To him who praises you while these libations flow: that man, O Gods, ye ne’er consume.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी को अस्य वां देवौ मर्तश्चिकेतति | विषूचो अश्वान युयुजान ईयत एकः समान आ रथे ||
6.59.e: What mortal understands, O Gods, Indra and Agni, this your way?  One of you, yoking Steeds that move to every side, advances in your common car.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी अपादियं पूर्वागात पद्वतीभ्यः | हित्वी शिरो जिह्वया वावदच्चरत तरिंशत पदा नयक्रमीत ||
6.59.e: First, Indra-Agni, hath this Maid come footless unto those with feet.  Stretching her head and speaking loudly with her tongue, she hath gone downward thirty steps.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी आ हि तन्वते नरो धन्वानि बाह्वोः | मा नो अस्मिन महाधने परा वर्क्तं गविष्टिषु ||
6.59.e: E’en now, O Indra-Agni, men hold in their arms and stretch their bows.  Desert us not in this great fray, in battles for the sake of kine.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी तपन्ति माघा अर्यो अरातयः | अप दवेषांस्या कर्तं युयुतं सूर्यादधि ||
6.59.e: The foeman's sinful enmities, Indra and Agni, vex me sore.  Drive those who hate me far away, and keep them distant from the Sun.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी युवोरपि वसु दिव्यानि पार्थिवा | आ न इह परयछतं रयिं विश्वायुपोषसम ||
6.59.e: Indra and Agni, yours are all the treasures of the heavens and earth.  Here give ye us the opulence that prospers every living man.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी उक्थवाहसा सतोमेभिर्हवनश्रुता | विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरा गतमस्य सोमस्य पीतये ||
6.59.e: O Indra-Agni, who accept the laud, and hear us for our praise,  Come near us, drawn by all our songs, to drink of this our Soma juice.

6.60.d: शनथद वर्त्रमुत सनोति वाजमिन्द्रा यो अग्नी सहुरी सपर्यात | इरज्यन्ता वसव्यस्य भूरेः सहस्तमा सहसा वाजयन्ता ||
6.60.e: HE slays the foe and wins the spoil who worships Indra and Agni, strong and mighty Heroes,  Who rule as Sovrans over ample riches, victorious, showing forth their power in conquest.

6.60.d: ता योधिष्टमभि गा इन्द्र नूनमपः सवरुषसो अग्न ऊळ्हः | दिशः सवरुषस इन्द्र चित्रा अपो गा अग्ने युवसे नियुत्वान ||
6.60.e: So battle now, O Indra and thou, Agni, for cows and waters, sunlight, stolen Mornings.  Team-borne, thou makest kine thine own, O Agni: thou, Indra, light, Dawns, regions, wondrous waters.

6.60.d: आ वर्त्रहणा वर्त्रहभिः शुष्मैरिन्द्र यातं नमोभिरग्ने अर्वाक | युवं राधोभिरकवेभिरिन्द्राग्ने अस्मे भवतमुत्तमेभिः ||
6.60.e: With Vṛtra-slaying might, Indra and Agni, come, drawn by homage, O ye Vṛtra-slayers.  Indra and Agni, show yourselves among us with your supreme and unrestricted bounties.

6.60.d: ता हुवे ययोरिदं पप्ने विश्वं पुरा कर्तम | इन्द्राग्नी नमर्धतः ||
6.60.e: I call the Twain whose deeds of old have all been famed in ancient days  O Indra-Agni, harm us not.

6.60.d: उग्रा विघनिना मर्ध इन्द्राग्नी हवामहे | ता नो मर्ळात ईद्र्शे ||
6.60.e: The Strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni, we invoke;  May they be kind to one like me.

6.60.d: हतो वर्त्राण्यार्या हतो दासानि सत्पती | हतो विश्वा अप दविषः ||
6.60.e: They slay our Ārya foes, these Lords of heroes, slay our Dasyu foes  And drive our enemies away.

6.60.d: इन्द्राग्नी युवामिमे.अभि सतोमा अनूषत | पिबतं शम्भुवा सुतम ||
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, these our songs of praise have sounded forth to you:  Ye who bring blessings! drink the juice.

6.60.d: या वां सन्ति पुरुस्प्र्हो नियुतो दाशुषे नरा | इन्द्राग्नी ताभिरा गतम ||
6.60.e: Come, Indra-Agni, with those teams, desired of many, which ye have,  O Heroes, for the worshipper.

6.60.d: ताभिरा गछतं नरोपेदं सवनं सुतम | इन्द्राग्नी सोमपीतये ||
6.60.e: With those to this libation poured, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, come:  Come ye to drink the Soma juice.

6.60.d: तमीळिष्व यो अर्चिषा वना विश्वा परिष्वजत | कर्ष्णाक्र्णोति जिह्वया ||
6.60.e: Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing flame,  And leaves them blackened with his tongue.

6.60.d: य इद्ध आविवासति सुम्नमिन्द्रस्य मर्त्यः | दयुम्नाय सुतरा अपः ||
6.60.e: He who gains Indra's bliss with fire enkindled finds an easy way  Over the floods to happiness.

6.60.d: ता नो वाजवतीरिष आशून पिप्र्तमर्वतः | इन्द्रमग्निं च वोळ्हवे ||
6.60.e: Give us fleet coursers to convey Indra and Agni, and bestow  Abundant strengthening food on us.

6.60.d: उभा वामिन्द्राग्नी आहुवध्या उभा राधसः सह मादयध्यै | उभा दाताराविषां रयीणामुभा वाजस्य सातये हुवे वाम ||
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, I will call you hither and make you joyful with the gifts I offer.  Ye Twain are givers both of food and riches: to win me strength and vigour I invoke you.

6.60.d: आ नो गव्येभिरश्व्यैर्वसव्यैरुप गछतम | सखायौ देवौ सख्याय शम्भुवेन्द्राग्नी ता हवामहे ||
6.60.e: Come unto us with riches, come with wealth in horses and in kine.  Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, the Gods, as Friends for friendship, bringing bliss.

6.60.d: इन्द्राग्नी शर्णुतं हवं यजमानस्य सुन्वतः | वीतं हव्यान्या गतं पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ||
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, hear his call who worships. with libations poured.  Come and enjoy the offerings, drink the sweetly-flavoured Soma juice.

6.61.d: इयमददाद रभसं रणच्युतं दिवोदासं वध्र्यश्वाय दाशुषे | या शश्वन्तमाचखादावसं पणिं ता ते दात्राणि तविषा सरस्वति ||
6.61.e: To Vadhryasva when. be worshipped her with gifts she gave fierce Divodāsa, canceller of debts.  Consumer of the churlish niggard, one and all, thine, O Sarasvatī, are these effectual boons.

6.61.d: इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः | पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुव्र्क्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ||
6.61.e: She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.  Let us invite with songs and holy hymns for help Sarasvatī who slayeth the Paravatas.

6.61.d: सरस्वति देवनिदो नि बर्हय परजां विश्वस्य बर्सयस्य मायिनः | उत कषितिभ्यो.अवनीरविन्दो विषमेभ्यो अस्रवो वाजिनीवति ||
6.61.e: Thou castest down, Sarasvatī, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Bṛsaya skilled in magic arts.  Thou hast discovered rivers for the tribes of men, and, rich in wealth! made poison flow away from them.

6.61.d: पर णो देवी सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती | धीनामवित्र्यवतु ||
6.61.e: May the divine Sarasvatī, rich in her wealth, protect us well,  Furthering all our thoughts with might

6.61.d: यस्त्वा देवि सरस्वत्युपब्रूते धने हिते | इन्द्रं न वर्त्रतूर्ये ||
6.61.e: Whoso, divine Sarasvatī, invokes thee where the prize is set,  Like Indra when he smites the foe.

6.61.d: तवं देवि सरस्वत्यवा वाजेषु वाजिनि | रदा पूषेव नःसनिम ||
6.61.e: Aid us, divine Sarasvad, thou who art strong in wealth and power  Like Pūṣan, give us opulence.

6.61.d: उत सया नः सरस्वती घोरा हिरण्यवर्तनिः | वर्त्रघ्नी वष्टि सुष्टुतिम ||
6.61.e: Yea, this divine Sarasvatī, terrible with her golden path,  Foe-slayer, claims our eulogy.
Whose limitless unbroken flood, swift-moving with a rapid rush,  Comes onward with tempestuous roar.

6.61.d: सा नो विश्वा अति दविषः सवसॄरन्या रतावरी | अतन्नहेव सूर्यः ||
6.61.e: She hath spread us beyond all foes, beyond her Sisters, Holy One,  As Sūrya spreadeth out the days.

6.61.d: उत नः परिया परियासु सप्तस्वसा सुजुष्टा | सरस्वती सतोम्या भूत ||
6.61.e: Yea, she most dear amid dear stream, Seven-sistered, graciously inclined,  Sarasvatī hath earned our praise.

6.61.d: आपप्रुषी पार्थिवान्युरु रजो अन्तरिक्षम | सरस्वती निदस पातु ||
6.61.e: Guard us from hate Sarasvatī, she who hath filled the realms of earth,  And that wide tract, the firmament!

6.61.d: तरिषधस्था सप्तधातुः पञ्च जाता वर्धयन्ती | वाजे-वाजे हव्या भूत ||
6.61.e: Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must be  Invoked in every deed of might.

6.61.d: पर या महिम्ना महिनासु चेकिते दयुम्नेभिरन्या अपसामपस्तमा | रथ इव बर्हती विभ्वने कर्तोपस्तुत्या चिकितुषा सरस्वती ||
6.61.e: Marked out by majesty among the Mighty Ones, in glory swifter than the other rapid Streams,  Created vast for victory like a chariot, Sarasvatī must be extolled by every sage.

6.61.d: सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यो माप सफरीः पयसा मा न आधक | जुषस्व नः सख्या वेश्या च मा तवत कषेत्राण्यरणानि गन्म ||
6.61.e: Guide us, Sarasvatī, to glorious treasure: refuse us not thy milk, nor spurn us from thee.  Gladly accept our friendship and obedience: let us not go from thee to distant countries.

6.62.d: सतुषे नरा दिवो अस्य परसन्ताश्विना हुवे जरमाणो अर्कैः | या सद्य उस्रा वयुषि जमो अन्तान युयूषतः पर्युरूवरांसि ||
6.62.e: I LAUD the Heroes Twain, this heaven's Controllers: singing with songs of praise I call the Aśvins,  Fain in a moment, when the morns are breaking, to part the earth's ends and the spacious regions.

6.62.d: ता यज्ञमा शुचिभिश्चक्रमाणा रथस्य भानुं रुरुचूरजोभिः | पुरू वरांस्यमिता मिमानापो धन्वान्यति याथो अज्रान ||
6.62.e: Moving to sacrifice through realms of lustre they light the radiance of the car that bears them.  Traversing many wide unmeasured spaces, over the wastes ye pass, and fields, and waters.

6.62.d: ता ह तयद वर्तिर्यदरध्रमुग्रेत्था धिय ऊहथुः शश्वदश्वैः | मनोजवेभिरिषिरैः शयध्यै परि वयथिर्दाशुषो मर्त्यस्य ||
6.62.e: Ye to that bounteous path of yours, ye mighty, have ever borne away our thoughts with horses,  Mind-swift and full of vigour, that the trouble of man who offers gifts might cease and slumber.

6.62.d: ता नव्यसो जरमाणस्य मन्मोप भूषतो युयुजानसप्ती | शुभं पर्क्षमिषमूर्जं वहन्ता होता यक्षत परत्नो अध्रुग युवाना ||
6.62.e: So ye, when ye have yoked your chariothorses, come to the hymn of the most recent singer.  Our true and ancient Herald Priest shall bring you, the Youthful, bearing splendour, food, and vigour.

6.62.d: ता वल्गू दस्रा पुरुशाकतमा परत्ना नव्यसा वचसा विवासे | या शंसते सतुवते शम्भविष्ठा बभूवतुर्ग्र्णते चित्रराती ||
6.62.e: With newest hymn I call those Wonder-Workers, ancient and brilliant, and exceeding mighty,  Bringers of bliss to him who lauds and praises, bestowing varied bounties on the singer.

6.62.d: ता भुज्युं विभिरद्भ्यः समुद्रात तुग्रस्य सूनुमूहथूरजोभिः | अरेणुभिर्योजनेभिर्भुजन्ता पतत्रिभिरर्णसोनिरुपस्थात ||
6.62.e: So ye, with birds, out of the sea and waters bore Bhujyu, son of Tugra, through the regions.  Speeding with winged steeds through dustless spaces, out of the bosom of the flood they bore him.

6.62.d: वि जयुषा रथ्या यातमद्रिं शरुतं हवं वर्षणा वध्रिमत्याः | दशस्यन्ता शयवे पिप्यथुर्गामिति चयवाना सुमतिं भुरण्यू ||
6.62.e: Victors, car-borne, ye rent the rock asunder: Bulls, heard the calling of the eunuch's consort.  Bounteous, ye filled the cow with milk for Śayu: thus, swift and zealous Ones, ye showed your favour.

6.62.d: यद रोदसी परदिवो अस्ति भूमा हेळो देवानामुत मर्त्यत्रा | तदादित्या वसवो रुद्रियासो रक्षोयुजे तपुरघं दधात ||
6.62.e: Whate’er from olden time, Heaven, Earth! existeth great object of the wrath of Gods and mortals,  Make that, Ādityas, Vasus, sons of Rudra, an evil brand to one allied with demons.

6.62.d: य ईं राजानाव रतुथा विदधद रजसो मित्रो वरुणश्चिकेतत | गम्भीराय रक्षसे हेतिमस्य दरोघाय चिद वचस आनवाय ||
6.62.e: May he who knows, as Varuṇa and Mitra, air's realm, appointing both the Kings in season,  Against the secret fiend cast forth his weapon, against the lying words that strangers utter.

6.62.d: अन्तरैश्चक्रैस्तनयाय वर्तिर्द्युमता यातं नर्वता रथेन | सनुत्येन तयजसा मर्त्यस्य वनुष्यतामपि शीर्षावव्र्क्तम ||
6.62.e: Come to our home with friendly wheels, for offipring; come on your radiant chariot rich in heroes.  Strike off, ye Twain, the heads of our assailants who with man's treacherous attack approach us.

6.62.d: आ परमाभिरुत मध्यमाभिर्नियुद्भिर्यातमवमाभिरर्वाक | दर्ळ्हस्य चिद गोमतो वि वरजस्य दुरो वर्तं गर्णते चित्रराती ||
6.62.e: Come hitherward to us with teams of horses, the highest and the midmost and the lowest.  Bountiful Lords, throw open to the singer doors e’en of the firm-closed stall of cattle.

6.63.d: कव तया वल्गू पुरुहूताद्य दूतो न सतोमो.अविदन नमस्वान | आ यो अर्वां नासत्या ववर्त परेष्ठा हयसथो अस्य मन्मन ||
6.63.e: WHERE hath the hymn with reverence, like an envoy, found both fair Gods to-day, invoked of many-  Hymn that hath brought the two Nāsatyas hither? To this man's thought be ye, both Gods, most friendly.

6.63.d: अरं मे गन्तं हवनायास्मै गर्णाना यथा पिबाथो अन्धः | परि ह तयद वर्तिर्याथो रिषो न यत परो नान्तरस्तुतुर्यात ||
6.63.e: Come readily to this mine invocation, lauded with songs, that ye may drink the juices.  Compass this house to keep it from the foeman, that none may force it, either near or distant.

6.63.d: अकारि वामन्धसो वरीमन्नस्तारि बर्हिः सुप्रायणतमम | उत्तानहस्तो युवयुर्ववन्दा वां नक्षन्तो अद्रय आञ्जन ||
6.63.e: Juice in wide room hath been prepared to feast you: for you the grass is strewn, most soft to tread on.  With lifted hands your servant hath adored you. Yearningfor you the press-stones shed the liquid.

6.63.d: ऊर्ध्वो वामग्निरध्वरेष्वस्थात पर रातिरेति जूर्णिनीघ्र्ताची | पर होता गूर्तमना उराणो.अयुक्त यो नासत्या हवीमन ||
6.63.e: Agni uplifts him at your sacrifices: forth goes the oblation dropping oil and glowing.  Up stands the grateful-minded priest, elected, appointed to invoke the two Nāsatyas.

6.63.d: अधि शरिये दुहिता सूर्यस्य रथं तस्थौ पुरुभुजा शतोतिम | पर मायाभिर्मायिना भूतमत्र नरा नर्तू जनिमन यज्ञियानाम ||
6.63.e: Lords of great wealth! for glory, Sūrya's Daughter mounted your car that brings a hundred succours.  Famed for your magic arts were ye, magicians! amid the race of Gods, ye dancing Heroes!

6.63.d: युवं शरीभिर्दर्शताभिराभिः शुभे पुष्टिमूहथुःसूर्यायाः | पर वां वयो वपुषे.अनु पप्तन नक्षद वाणी सुष्टुता धिष्ण्या वाम ||
6.63.e: Ye Twain, with these your glories fair to look on, brought, to win victory, rich gifts for Sūrya.  After you flew your birds, marvels of beauty: dear to our hearts! the song, well lauded, reached you.

6.63.d: आ वां वयो.अश्वासो वहिष्ठा अभि परयो नासत्या वहन्तु | पर वां रथो मनोजवा असर्जीषः पर्क्ष इषिधो अनु पूर्वीः ||
6.63.e: May your winged coursers, best to draw. Nāsatyas! convey you to the object of your wishes.  Swift as the thought, your car hath been sent onward to food of many a sort and dainty viands.

6.63.d: पुरु हि वां पुरुभुजा देष्णं धेनुं न इषं पिन्वतमसक्राम | सतुतश्च वां माध्वी सुष्टुतिश्च रसाश्च ये वामनु रातिमग्मन ||
6.63.e: Lords of great wealth, manifold is your bounty: ye filled our cow with food that never faileth.  Lovers of sweetness! yours are praise and singers, and poured libations which have sought your favour.

6.63.d: उत म रज्रे पुरयस्य रघ्वी सुमीळ्हे शतं पेरुके च पक्वा | शाण्डो दाद धिरणिनः समद्दिष्टीन दश वशासो अभिषाच रष्वान ||
6.63.e: Mine were two mares of Puraya, brown, swift-footed; a hundred with Sumidha, food with Peruk  Sanda gave ten gold-decked and well-trained horses, tame and obedient and of lofty stature.

6.63.d: सं वां शता नासत्या सहस्राश्वानां पुरुपन्था गिरे दात | भरद्वाजाय वीर नू गिरे दाद धता रक्षांसि पुरुदंससा सयुः ||
6.63.e: Nāsatyas! Purupanthas offered hundreds, thousands of steeds to him who sang your praises,  Gave, Heroes! to the singer Bharadvāja. Ye-Wonder-Workers, let the fiends be slaughtered.

6.63.d: आ वां सुम्ने वरिमन सूरिभिः षयाम ||
6.63.e: May I with princes share your bliss in freedom.

6.64.d: उदु शरिय उषसो रोचमाना अस्थुरपां नोर्मयो रुशन्तः | कर्णोति विश्वा सुपथा सुगान्यभूदु वस्वी दक्षिणामघोनी ||
6.64.e: THE radiant Dawns have risen up for glory, in their white splendour like the waves of waters.  She maketh paths all easy, fair to travel, and, rich, hath shown herself benign and friendly.

6.64.d: भद्रा दद्र्क्ष उर्विया वि भास्युत ते शोचिर्भानवो दयामपप्तन | आविर्वक्षः कर्णुषे शुम्भमानोषो देवि रोचमानामहोभिः ||
6.64.e: We see that thou art good: far shines thy lustre; thy beams, thy splendours have flown up to heaven.  Decking thyself, thou makest bare thy bosom, shining in majesty, thou Goddess Morning.

6.64.d: वहन्ति सीमरुणासो रुशन्तो गावः सुभगामुर्विया परथानाम | अपेजते शूरो अस्तेव शत्रून बाधते तमो अजिरो नवोळ्हा ||
6.64.e: Red are the kine and luminous that bear her the Blessed One who spreadeth through the distance.  The foes she chaseth like a valiant archer, like a swift warrior she repelleth darkness.

6.64.d: सुगोत ते सुपथा पर्वतेष्ववाते अपस्तरसि सवभानो | सा न आ वह पर्थुयामन्न्र्ष्वे रयिं दिवो दुहितरिषयध्यै ||
6.64.e: Thy ways are easy on the hills: thou passest Invincible! Se1f-luminous! through waters.  So lofty Goddess with thine ample pathway, Daughter of Heaven, bring wealth to give us comfort.

6.64.d: सा वह योक्षभिरवातोषो वरं वहसि जोषमनु | तवं दिवो दुहितर्या ह देवी पूर्वहूतौ मंहना दर्शता भूः ||
6.64.e: Dawn, bring me wealth: untroubled, with thine oxen thou bearest riches at thy will and pleasure;  Thou who, a Goddess, Child of Heaven, hast shown thee lovely through bounty when we called thee early.
As the birds fly forth from their restingplaces, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning.  Yea, to the liberal mortal who rernaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest.

6.65.d: एषा सया नो दुहिता दिवोजाः कषितीरुछन्ती मानुषीरजीगः | या भानुना रुशता राम्यास्वज्ञायि तिरस्तमसश्चिदक्तून ||
6.65.e: SHEDDING her light on human habitations this Child of Heaven hath called us from our slumber;  She who at night-time with her argent lustre hath shown herself e’en through the shades of darkness.

6.65.d: वि तद ययुररुणयुग्भिरश्वैश्चित्रं भान्त्युषसश्चन्द्ररथाः | अग्रं यज्ञस्य बर्हतो नयन्तीर्वि ता बाधन्तेतम ऊर्म्यायाः ||
6.65.e: All this with red-rayed steeds have they divided: the Dawns on bright cars shine in wondrous fashion.  They, bringing near the stately rite's commencement, drive far away the night's surrounding shadows.

6.65.d: शरवो वाजमिषमूर्जं वहन्तीर्नि दाशुष उषसो मर्त्याय | मघोनीर्वीरवत पत्यमाना अवो धात विधते रत्नमद्य ||
6.65.e: Dawns, bringing hither, to the man who worships, glory and power and might and food and vigour,  Opulent, with imperial sway like heroes, favour your servant and this day enrich him.

6.65.d: इदा हि वो विधते रत्नमस्तीदा वीराय दाशुष उषासः | इदा विप्राय जरते यदुक्था नि षम मावते वहथ पुर चित ||
6.65.e: Now is there treasure for the man who serves you, now for the hero, Dawns! who brings oblation;  Now for the singer when he sings the praise-song. Even to one like me ye brought aforetime.

6.65.d: इदा हि त उषो अद्रिसानो गोत्रा गवामन्गिरसो गर्णन्ति | वयर्केण बिभिदुर्ब्रह्मणा च सत्या नर्णामभवद देवहूतिः ||
6.65.e: O Dawn who standest on the mountain ridges, Aṅgirases now praise thy stalls of cattle.  With prayer and holy hymn they burst them open: the heroes' calling on the Gods was fruitful.

6.65.d: उछा दिवो दुहितः परत्नवन नो भरद्वाजवद विधते मघोनि | सुवीरं रयिं गर्णते रिरीह्युरुगायमधि धेहि शरवो नः ||
6.65.e: Shine on us as of old, thou Child of Heaven,on him, rich Maid! who serves like Bharadvāja.  Give to the singer wealth with noble heroes, and upon us bestow wide-spreading glory.

6.66.d: वपुर्नु तच्चिकितुषे चिदस्तु समानं नाम धेनु पत्यमानम | मर्तेष्वन्यद दोहसे पीपाय सक्र्च्छुक्रं दुदुहे पर्श्निरूधः ||
6.66.e: E'EN to the wise let that be still a wonder to which the general name of Cow is given.  The one hath swelled among mankind for milking: Pṛśni hath drained but once her fair bright udder.

6.66.d: ये अग्नयो न शोशुचन्निधाना दविर्यत तरिर्मरुतो वाव्र्धन्त | अरेञवो हिरण्ययास एषां साकं नर्म्णैः पौंस्येभिश्च भूवन ||
6.66.e: They who like kindled flames of fire are glowing,. the Maruts, twice and thrice have waxen mighty.  Golden and dustless were their cars, invested with their great strength and their heroic vigour.

6.66.d: रुद्रस्य ये मीळ्हुषः सन्ति पुत्रा यांश्चो नु दाध्र्विर्भरध्यै | विदे हि माता महो मही षा सेत पर्श्निः सुभ्वे गर्भमाधात ||
6.66.e: They who are Sons of the rain-pouring Rudra, whom the long-lasting One had power to foster:  The Mighty Ones whose germ great Mother Pṛśni is known to have received for man's advantage.

6.66.d: न य इषन्ते जनुषो.अया नवन्तः सन्तो.अवद्यानि पुनानाः | निर्यद दुह्रे शुचयो.अनु जोषमनु शरिया तन्वमुक्षमाणाः ||
6.66.e: They shrink not from the birth; in this same manner still resting there they purge away reproaches.  When they have streamed forth, brilliant, at their pleasure, with their own splendour they bedew their bodies.

6.66.d: मक्षू न येषु दोहसे चिदया आ नाम धर्ष्णु मारुतन्दधानाः | न ये सतौना अयासो मह्ना नू चित सुदानुरव वासदुग्रान ||
6.66.e: Even those who bear the brave bold name of Maruts, whom not the active quickly wins for milking.  Even the liberal wards not off those fierce ones, those who are light and agile in their greatness.

6.66.d: त इदुग्राः शवसा धर्ष्णुषेणा उभे युजन्त रोदसी सुमेके | अध समैषु रोदसी सवशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ||
6.66.e: When, strong in strength and armed with potent weapons, they had united wellformed earth and heaven,  Rodasl stood among these furious Heroes like splendour shining with her native brightness.

6.66.d: अनेनो वो मरुतो यामो अस्त्वनश्वश्चिद यमजत्यरथीः | अनवसो अनभीशू रजस्तूर्वि रोदसी पथ्या याति साधन ||
6.66.e: No team of goats shall draw your car, O Maruts, no horse no charioteer be he who drives it.  Halting not, reinless, through the air it travels, speeding alone its paths through earth and heaven.

6.66.d: नास्य वर्ता न तरुता नवस्ति मरुतो यमवथ वजसातौ | तोके वा गोषु तनये यमप्सु स वरजं दर्ता पार्ये अध दयोः ||
6.66.e: None may obstruct, none overtake, O Maruts, him whom ye succour in the strife of battle  For sons and progeny, for kine and waters: he bursts the cow-stall on the day of trial.

6.66.d: पर चित्रमर्कं गर्णते तुराय मारुताय सवतवसे भरध्वम | ये सहांसि सहसा सहन्ते रेजते अग्ने पर्थिवी मखेभ्यः ||
6.66.e: Bring a bright hymn to praise the band of Maruts, the Singers, rapid, strong in native vigour,  Who conquer mighty strength with strength more mighty: earth shakes in terror at their wars, O Agni.

6.66.d: तविषीमन्तो अध्वरस्येव दिद्युत तर्षुच्यवसो जुह्वो नाग्नेः | अर्चत्रयो धुनयो न वीरा भराजज्जन्मानो मरुतो अध्र्ष्टाः ||
6.66.e: Bright like the flashing flames of sacrifices, like tongues of fire impetuous in their onset,  Chanting their psalm, singing aloud, like heroes, splendid from birth, invincible, the Maruts.

6.66.d: तं वर्धन्तं मारुतं भराजद्र्ष्टिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा विवासे | दिवः शर्धाय शुचयो मनीषा गिरयो नाप उग्रा अस्प्र्ध्रन ||
6.66.e: That swelling band I call with invocation, the brood of Rudra, armed with glittering lances.  Pure hymns are meet for that celestial army: like floods and mountains have the Strong Ones battled.

6.67.d: विश्वेषां वः सतां जयेष्ठतमा गीर्भिर्मित्रावरुणावाव्र्धध्यै | सं या रश्मेव यमतुर्यमिष्ठा दवा जनानसमा बाहुभिः सवैः ||
6.67.e: NOW Mitra-Varuṇa shall be exalted high by your songs, noblest of all existing;  They who, as ’twere with reins are best Controllers, unequalled with their arms to check the people.

6.67.d: इयं मद वां पर सत्र्णीते मनीषोप परिया नमसा बर्हिरछ | यन्तं नो मित्रावरुणावध्र्ष्टं छर्दिर्यद वां वरूथ्यं सुदानू ||
6.67.e: To you Two Gods is this my thought extended, turned to the sacred grass with loving homage.  Give us, O Mitra-Varuṇa, a dwelling safe from attack, which ye shall guard, Boon-Givers!

6.67.d: आ यातं मित्रावरुणा सुशस्त्युप परिया नमसा हूयमाना | सं यावप्नः सथो अपसेव जनाञ्छ्रुधीयतश्चिद यतथो महित्वा ||
6.67.e: Come hither, Mitra-Varuṇa, invited with eulogies and loving adoration,  Ye who with your might, as Work-Controllers, urge even men who quickly hear to labour.

6.67.d: अश्वा न या वाजिना पूतबन्धू रता यद गर्भमदितिर्भरध्यै | पर या महि महान्ता जायमाना घोरा मर्तायरिपवे नि दीधः ||
6.67.e: Whom, of pure origin, like two strong horses, Aditi bore as babes in proper season,  Whom, Mighty at your birth, the Mighty Goddess brought forth as terrors to the mortal foeman.

6.67.d: विश्वे यद वां मंहना मन्दमानाः कषत्रं देवासो अदधुः सजोषाः | परि यद भूथो रोदसी चिदुर्वी सन्ति सपशो अदब्धासो अमूराः ||
6.67.e: As all the Gods in their great joy and gladness gave you with one accord your high dominion,  As ye surround both worlds, though wide and spacious your spies are ever true and never bewildered.

6.67.d: ता हि कषत्रं धारयेथे अनु दयून दरंहेथे सानुमुपमादिव दयोः | दर्ळ्हो नक्षत्र उत विश्वदेवो भूमिमातान दयां धासिनायोः ||
6.67.e: So, through the days maintaining princely power. ye prop the height as ’twere from loftiest heaven.  The Star of all the Gods, established, filleth the heaven and earth with food of man who liveth.

6.67.d: ता विग्रं धैथे जठरं पर्णध्या आ यत सद्म सभ्र्तयः पर्णन्ति | न मर्ष्यन्ते युवतयो.अवाता वि यत पयो विश्वजिन्वा भरन्ते ||
6.67.e: Take the strong drink, to quaff till ye are sated, when he and his attendants fill the chamber.  The young Maids brook not that none seeks to win them, when, Quickeners of all! they scatter moisture.

6.67.d: ता जिह्वया सदमेदं सुमेधा आ यद वां सत्यो अरतिरते भूत | तद वां महित्वं घर्तान्नावस्तु युवं दाशुषेवि चयिष्टमंहः ||
6.67.e: So with your tongue come ever, when your envoy, faithful and very wise, attends our worship.  Nourished by holy oil! he this yGur glory: annihilate the sacrificer's trouble.

6.67.d: पर यद वां मित्रावरुणा सपूर्धन परिया धाम युवधिता मिनन्ति | न ये देवास ओहसा न मर्ता अयज्ञसाचो अप्यो नपुत्राः ||
6.67.e: When, Mitra-Varuṇa, they strive against you and break tlie friendly laws ye have established,  They, neither Gods nor men in estimation, like Api's sons have godless sacrifices.

6.67.d: वि यद वाचं कीस्तासो भरन्ते शंसन्ति के चिन निविदो मनानाः | आद वां बरवाम सत्यान्युक्था नकिर्देवेभिर्यतथो महित्वा ||
6.67.e: When singers in their song uplift their voices, some chant the Nivid texts with steady purpose.  Then may we sing you lauds that shall be fruitful: dp ye not rival all the Gods in greatness?

6.67.d: अवोरित्था वां छर्दिषो अभिष्टौ युवोर्मित्रावरुणावस्क्र्धोयु | अनु यद गाव सफुरान रजिप्यं धर्ष्णुं यद रणेव्र्षणं युनजन ||
6.67.e: O Mitra-Varuṇa, may your large bounty come to us hither, near to this our dwelling,  When the kine haste to us, and when they harness the fleet-foot mettled stallion for the battle.

6.68.d: शरुष्टी वां यज्ञ उद्यतः सजोषा मनुष्वद वर्क्तबर्हिषो यजध्यै | आ य इन्द्रावरुणाविषे अद्य महे सुम्नाय मह आववर्तत ||
6.68.e: HIS honouring rite whose grass is trimmed is offered swiftly to you, in Manu's wise, accordant,  The rite which Indra-Varuṇa shall carry this day to high success and glorious issue.

6.68.d: ता हि शरेष्ठा देवताता तुजा शूराणां शविष्ठाता हि भूतम | मघोनां मंहिष्ठा तुविशुष्म रतेन वर्त्रतुरा सर्वसेना ||
6.68.e: For at Gods’ worship they are best through vigour; they have become the strongest of the Heroes;  With mighty strength, most liberal of the Princes, Chiefs of the host, by Law made Vṛtra's slayers.

6.68.d: ता गर्णीहि नमस्येभिः शूषैः सुम्नेभिरिन्द्रावरुणा चकाना | वज्रेणान्यः शवसा हन्ति वर्त्रं सिषक्त्यन्यो वर्जनेषु विप्रः ||
6.68.e: Praise those Twain Gods for powers that merit worship, Indra and Varuṇa, for bliss, the joyous.  One with his might and thunderbolt slays Vṛtra; the other as a Sage stands near in troubles.

6.68.d: गनाश्च यन नरश्च वाव्र्धन्त विश्वे देवासो नरां सवगूर्ताः | परैभ्य इन्द्रावरुणा महित्वा दयौश्च पर्थिवि भूतमुर्वी ||
6.68.e: Though dames and men have waxen strong and mighty, and all the Gods selfpraised among the Heroes,  Ye, Indra-Varuṇa, have in might surpassed them, and thus were ye spread wide, O Earth and Heaven.

6.68.d: स इत सुदानुः सववान रतावेन्द्रा यो वां वरुण दाशतित्मन | इषा स दविषस्तरेद दास्वान वंसद रयिं रयिवतश्च जनान ||
6.68.e: Righteous is he, and liberal and helpful who, Indra-Varuṇa, brings you gifts with gladness.  That bounteous man through food shall conquer faemen, and win him opulence and wealthy people.

6.68.d: यं युवं दाश्वध्वराय देवा रयिं धत्थो वसुमन्तं पुरुक्षुम | अस्मे स इन्द्रावरुणावपि षयात पर यो भनक्ति वनुषामशस्तीः ||
6.68.e: May wealth which ye bestow in food and treasure on him who brings you gifts and sacrifices,  Wealth, Gods! which breaks the curse of those who vex us, be, Indra-Varuṇa, e’en our own possession.

6.68.d: उत नः सुत्रात्रो देवगोपाः सूरिभ्य इन्द्रावरुणा रयिः षयात | येषां शुष्मः पर्तनासु साह्वान पर सद्यो दयुम्नातिरते ततुरिः ||
6.68.e: So also, Indra-Varuṇa, may our princes have riches swift to save, with Gods to guard them-  They whose great might gives victory in battles, and their triumphant glory spreads with swiftness.

6.68.d: नू न इन्द्रावरुणा गर्णाना पर्ङकतं रयिं सौश्रवसाय देवा | इत्था गर्णन्तो महिनस्य शर्धो.अपो न नावा दुरितातरेम ||
6.68.e: Indra. and Varuṇa, Gods whom we are lauding, mingle ye wealth with our heroic glory.  May we, who praise the strength of what is mighty, pass dangers, as with boats we cross the waters.

6.68.d: पर सम्राजे बर्हते मन्म नु परियमर्च देवाय वरुणाय सप्रथः | अयं य उर्वी महिना महिव्रतः करत्वा विभात्यजरो न शोचिषा ||
6.68.e: Now will I sing a dear and far-extending hymn to Varuṇa the God, sublime, imperial Lord,  Who, mighty Governor, Eternal, as with flame, illumines both wide worlds with majesty and power.

6.68.d: इन्द्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं सोमं पिबतं मद्यं धर्तव्रता | युवो रथो अध्वरं देववीतये परति सवसरमुप याति पीतये ||
6.68.e: True to Law, Indra-Varuṇa, drinkers of the juice, drink this pressed Soma which shall give you rapturous joy.  Your chariot cometh to the banquet of the Gods, to sacrifice, as it were home, that ye may drink.

6.68.d: इन्द्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्य वर्ष्णः सोमस्य वर्षणा वर्षेथाम | इदं वामन्धः परिषिक्तमस्मे आसद्यास्मिन बर्हिषि मादयेथाम ||
6.68.e: Indra and Varuṇa, drink your fill, ye Heroes, of this invigorating sweetest Soma.  This juice is shed by us that ye may quaff it: on this trimmed grass be seated, and rejoice you

6.69.d: सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमीन्द्राविष्णू अपसस परेस्य | जुषेथां यज्ञं दरविणं च धत्तमरिष्टैर्नः पथिभिः पारयन्ता ||
6.69.e: INDRA and Viṣṇu, at my task's completion I urge you on with food and sacred service.  Accept the sacrifice and grant us riches, leading us on by unobstructed pathways.

6.69.d: या विश्वासां जनितरा मतीनामिन्द्राविष्णू कलशा सोमधाना | पर वां गिरः शस्यमाना अवन्तु पर सतोमासो गीयमानासो अर्कैः ||
6.69.e: Ye who inspire all hymns, Indra and Viṣṇu, ye vessels who contain the Soma juices,  May hymns of praise that now are sung address you, the lauds that are recited by the singers.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू मदपती मदानामा सोमं यातं दरविणो दधाना | सं वामञ्जन्त्वक्तुभिर्मतीनां सं सतोमासः शस्यमानास उक्थैः ||
6.69.e: Lords of joy-giving draughts, Indra and Viṣṇu, come, giving gifts of treasure, to the Soma.  With brilliant rays of hymns let chanted praises, repeated with the lauds, adorn and deck you.

6.69.d: आ वामश्वासो अभिमातिषाह इन्द्राविष्णू सधमादो वहन्तु | जुषेथां विश्वा हवना मतीनामुप बरह्माणि शर्णुतं गिरो मे ||
6.69.e: May your foe-conquering horses bring you hither, Indra and Viṣṇu, sharers of the banquet.  Of all our hymns accept the invocations list to my prayers and hear the songs I sing you.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू तत पनयाय्यं वां सोमस्य मद उरु चक्रमाथे | अक्र्णुतमन्तरिक्षं वरीयो.अप्रथतं जीवसे नो रजांसि ||
6.69.e: This your deed, Indra-Viṣṇu, must be lauded: widely ye strode in the wild joy of Soma.  Ye made the firmament of larger compass, and made the regions broad for our existence.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू हविषा वाव्र्धानाग्राद्वाना नमसा रातहव्या | घर्तासुती दरविणं धत्तमस्मे समुद्रः सथः कलशः सोमधानः ||
6.69.e: Strengthened with sacred offerings, IndraViṣṇu, first eaters, served with worship ana oblation,  Fed with the holy oil, vouchsafe us riches ye are the lake, the vat that holds the Soma.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्य सोमस्य दस्रा जठरं पर्णेथाम | आ वामन्धांसि मदिराण्यग्मन्नुप बरह्माणि शर्णुतं हवं मे ||
6.69.e: Drink of this meath, O Indra, thou, and Viṣṇu; drink ye your fill of Soma, Wonder-Workers.  The sweet exhilarating juice hath reached you. Hear ye my prayers, give ear unto my calling.

6.69.d: उभा जिग्यथुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्ये कतरश्चनैनोः | इन्द्रश्च विष्णो यदपस्प्र्धेथां तरेधा सहस्रं वि तदैरयेथाम ||
6.69.e: Ye Twain have conquered, ne’er have yc been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished.  Ye, Indra-Viṣṇu, when ye fought the battle, produced this infinite with three divisions.

6.70.d: घर्तवती भुवनानामभिश्रियोर्वी पर्थ्वी मधुदुघे सुपेशसा | दयावाप्र्थिवी वरुणस्य धर्मणा विष्कभिते अजरेभूरिरेतसा ||
6.70.e: FILLED full of fatness, compassing all things that be, wide, spacious, dropping meath, beautiful in their form,  The Heaven and the Earth by Varuṇa's decree, unwasting, rich in germs, stand parted each from each.

6.70.d: असश्चन्ती भूरिधारे पयस्वती घर्तं दुहाते सुक्र्ते शुचिव्रते | राजन्ती अस्य भुवनस्य रोदसी अस्मे रेतः सिञ्चतंयन मनुर्हितम ||
6.70.e: The Everlasting Pair, with full streams, rich in milk, in their pure rule pour fatness for the pious man.  Ye who are Regents of this world, O Earth and Heaven, pour into us the genial flow that prospers meit.

6.70.d: यो वां रजवे करमणाय रोदसी मर्तो ददाश धिषणे स साधति | पर परजाभिर्जायते धर्मणस परि युवोः सिक्ता विषुरूपाणि सव्रता ||
6.70.e: Whoso, for righteous life, pours offerings to you, O Heaven and Earth, ye Hemispheres, that man succeeds.  He in his seed is born again and spreads by Law: from you flow things diverse in form, but ruled alike.

6.70.d: घर्तेन दयावाप्र्थिवी अभीव्र्ते घर्तश्रिया घर्तप्र्चा घर्ताव्र्धा | उर्वी पर्थ्वी होत्र्वूर्ये पुरोहिते ते इद विप्रा ईळते सुम्नमिष्टये ||
6.70.e: Enclosed in fatness, Heaven and Earth are bright therewith: they mingle with the fatness which they still increase.  Wide, broad, set foremost at election of the priest, to them the singers pray for bliss to further them.

6.70.d: मधु नो दयावाप्र्थिवी मिमिक्षतां मधुश्चुता मधुदुघे मधुव्रते | दधाने यज्ञं दरविणं च देवता महि शरवो वाजमस्मे सुवीर्यम ||
6.70.e: May Heaven and Earth pour down the balmy rain for us, balm-dropping, yielding balm, with balm upon your path,  Bestowing by your Godhead sacrifice and wealth, great fame and strength for us and good heroic might.

6.70.d: ऊर्जं नो दयौश्च पर्थिवी च पिन्वतां पिता माता विश्वविदा सुदंससा | संरराणे रोदसी विश्वशम्भुवा सनिं वाजं रयिमस्मे समिन्वताम ||
6.70.e: May Heaven and Earth make food swell plenteously for us, all-knowing Father, jother, wondrous in their works.  Pouring out bounties, may, in union, both the Worlds, all beneficial, send us gain, and power, and wealth.

6.71.d: उदु षय देवः सविता हिरण्यया बाहू अयंस्त सवनायसुक्रतुः | घर्तेन पाणी अभि परुष्णुते मखो युवा सुदक्षो रजसो विधर्मणि ||
6.71.e: FULL of effectual wisdom Savitar the God hath stretched out golden arms that he may bring forth life.  Young and most skilful, while he holds the region up, the Warrior sprinkles fatness over both his hands.

6.71.d: देवस्य वयं सवितुः सवीमनि शरेष्ठे सयाम वसुनश्चदावने | यो विश्वस्य दविपदो यश्चतुष्पदो निवेशने परसवे चासि भूमनः ||
6.71.e: May we enjoy the noblest vivifying force of Savitar the God, that he may give us wealth:  For thou art mighty to produce and lull to rest the world of life that moves on two feet and on four.

6.71.d: अदब्धेभिः सवितः पायुभिष टवं शिवेभिरद्य परि पाहि नो गयम | हिरण्यजिह्वः सुविताय नव्यसे रक्षा माकिर्नोघशंस ईशत ||
6.71.e: Protect our habitation, Savitar, this day, with guardian aids around, auspicious, firm and true.  God of the golden tongue, keep us for newest bliss: let not the evil-wisher have us in his power.

6.71.d: उदु षय देवः सविता दमूना हिरण्यपाणिः परतिदोषमस्थात | अयोहनुर्यजतो मन्द्रजिह्व आ दाशुषे सुवति भूरिवामम ||
6.71.e: This Savitar the God, the golden-handed, Friend of the home, hath risen to meet the twilight.  With cheeks of brass, with pleasant tongue, the Holy, he sends the worshipper rich gifts in plenty.

6.71.d: उदू अयानुपवक्तेव बाहू हिरण्यया सविता सुप्रतीका | दिवो रोहांस्यरुहत पर्थिव्या अरीरमत पतयत कच्चिदभ्वम ||
6.71.e: Like a Director, Savitar hath extended his golden arms, exceeding fair to look on.  He hath gone up the heights of earth and heaven, and made each monster fall and cease from troubling.

6.71.d: वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु शवो दिवे-दिवे वाममस्मभ्यं सावीः | वामस्य हि कषयस्य देव भूरेरया धिया वामभाजः सयाम ||
6.71.e: Fair wealth, O Savitar, to-day, to-morrow, fair wealth produce for us each day that passes.  May we through this our song be happy gainers, God, of a fair and spacious habitation.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा महि तद वां महित्वं युवं महानि परथमानि चक्रथुः | युवं सूर्यं विविदथुर्युवं सवर्विश्वा तमांस्यहतं निदश्च ||
6.72.e: GREAT is this might of yours, Indra and Soma: the first high exploits were your own achievements.  Ye found the Sun ye found the light of heaven: ye killed all darkness and the Gods’ blasphemers.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा वासयथ उषासमुत सूर्यं नयथो जयोतिषा सह | उप दयां सकम्भथुः सकम्भनेनाप्रथतं पर्थिवीं मातरं वि ||
6.72.e: Ye, Indra-Soma, gave her light to Morning, and led the Sun on high with all his splendour.  Ye stayed the heaven with a supporting pillar, and spread abroad apart, the Earth, the Mother.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमावहिमपः परिष्ठां हथो वर्त्रमनु वां दयौरमन्यत | परार्णांस्यैरयतं नदीनामा समुद्राणिपप्रथुः पुरूणि ||
6.72.e: Ye slew the flood -obstructing serpent Vṛtra, Indra and Soma: Heaven approved your exploit.  Ye urged to speed the currents of the rivers, and many seas have ye filled full with waters.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा पक्वमामास्वन्तर्नि गवामिद दधथुर्वक्षणासु | जग्र्भथुरनपिनद्धमासु रुशच्चित्रासु जगतीष्वन्तः ||
6.72.e: Ye in the unripe udders of the milch-kine have set the ripe milk, Indra, thou, and Soma.  Ye have held fast the unimpeded whiteness within these many-coloured moving creatures.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा युवमङग तरुत्रमपत्यसाचं शरुत्यं रराथे | युवं शुष्मं नर्यं चर्षणिभ्यः सं विव्यथुः पर्तनाषाहमुग्रा ||
6.72.e: Verily ye bestow, Indra and Soma, wealth, famed, victorious, passing to our children.  Ye have invested men, ye Mighty Beings, with manly strength that conquers in the battle.

6.73.d: यो अद्रिभित परथमजा रतावा बर्हस्पतिराङगिरसो हविष्मान | दविबर्हज्मा पराघर्मसत पिता न आ रोदसी वर्षभो रोरवीति ||
6.73.e: SERVED with oblations, first-born, mountain-render, Aṅgiras' son, Bṛhaspati, the Holy,  With twice-firm path, dwelling in light, our Father, roars loudly, as a bull, to Earth and Heaven.

6.73.d: जनाय चिद य ईवत उ लोकं बर्हस्पतिर्देवहूतौ चकार | घनन वर्त्राणि वि पुरो दर्दरीति जयञ्छत्रून्रमित्रान पर्त्सु साहन ||
6.73.e: Bṛhaspati, who made for such a people wide room and verge when Gods were invocated,  Slaying his enemies, breaks down their castles, quelling his foes and conquering those who hate him.

6.73.d: बर्हस्पतिः समजयद वसूनि महो वरजान गोमतो देव एषः | अपः सिषासन सवरप्रतीतो बर्हस्पतिर्हन्त्यमित्रमर्कैः ||
6.73.e: Bṛhaspati in war hath won rich treasures, hath won, this God, the great stalls filled with cattle.  Striving to win waters and light, resistless, Bṛhaspati with lightning smites the foeman.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा धारयेथामसुर्यं पर वामिष्टयो.अरमश्नुवन्तु | दमे-दमे सप्त रत्ना दधाना शं नो भूतं दविपदेशं चतुष्पदे ||
6.74.e: HOLD fast your Godlike sway, O Soma-Rudra: let these our sacrifices quickly reach you.  Placing in every house your seven great treasures, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा वि वर्हतं विषूचीममीवा या नो गयमाविवेश | आरे बाधेथां निरतिं पराचैरस्मे भद्रा सौश्रवसानि सन्तु ||
6.74.e: Soma and Rudra, chase to every quarter the sickness that hath visited our dwelling.  Drive Nirrti away into the distance, and give us excellent and happy glories.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा युवमेतान्यस्मे विश्वा तनूषु भेषजानि धत्तम | अव सयतं मुञ्चतं यन नो अस्ति तनूषु बद्धं कर्तमेनो अस्मत ||
6.74.e: Provide, O Soma-Rudra, for our bodies all needful medicines to heal and cure us.  Set free and draw away the sin committed which we have still inherent in our persons.

6.74.d: तिग्मायुधौ तिग्महेती सुशेवौ सोमारुद्राविह सु मर्ळतं नः | पर नो मुञ्चतं वरुणस्य पाशाद गोपायतं नः सुमनस्यमाना ||
6.74.e: Armed with keen shafts and weapons, kind and loving, be gracious unto us, Soma and Rudra.  Release us from the noose of Varuṇa; keep us from sorrow, in your tender loving-kindness.

6.75.d: जीमूतस्येव भवति परतीकं यद वर्मी याति समदामुपस्थे | अनाविद्धया तन्वा जय तवं स तवा वर्मणो महिमा पिपर्तु ||
6.75.e: THE warrior's look is like a thunderous rain-cloud's, when, armed with mail, he seeks the lap of battle.  Be thou victorious with unwounded body: so let the thickness of thy mail protect thee.

6.75.d: धन्वना गा धन्वनाजिं जयेम धन्वना तीव्राः समदो जयेम | धनुः शत्रोरपकामं कर्णोति धन्वना सर्वाः परदिशो जयेम ||
6.75.e: With Bow let us win kine, with Bow the battle, with Bow be victors in our hot encounters.  The Bow brings grief and sorrow to the foeman: armed with the Bow may we subdue all regions.

6.75.d: वक्ष्यन्तीवेदा गनीगन्ति कर्णं परियं सखायं परिषस्वजाना | योषेव शिङकते वितताधि धन्वञ जया इयं समने पारयन्ती ||
6.75.e: Close to his car, as fain to speak, She presses, holding her well-loved Friend in her embraces.  Strained on the Bow, She whispers like a woman-this Bowstring that preserves us in the combat.

6.75.d: ते आचरन्ती समनेव योषा मातेव पुत्रं बिभ्र्तामुपस्थे | अप शत्रून विध्यतां संविदाने आर्त्नी इमे विष्फुरन्तीमित्रान ||
6.75.e: These, meeting like a woman and her lover, bear, mother-like, their child upon their bosom.  May the two Bow-ends, starting swift asunder, scatter, in unison, the foes who hate us.

6.75.d: बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्रश्चिश्चा कर्णोति समनावगत्य | इषुधिः सङकाः पर्तनाश्च सर्वाः पर्ष्ठे निनद्धो जयति परसूतः ||
6.75.e: With many a son, father of many daughters, He clangs and clashes as he goes to battle.  Slung on the back, pouring his brood, the Quiver vanquishes all opposing bands and armies.

6.75.d: रथे तिष्ठन नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्र-यत्र कामयते सुषारथिः | अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत मनः पश्चादनु यछन्ति रश्मयः ||
6.75.e: Upstanding in the Car the skilful Charioteer guides his strong Horses on whithersoe’er he will.  See and admire the strength of those controlling Reins which from behind declare the will of him who drives.

6.75.d: तीव्रान घोषान कर्ण्वते वर्षपाणयो.अश्वा रथेभिः सहवाजयन्तः | अवक्रामन्तः परपदैरमित्रान कषिणन्ति शत्रून्रनपव्ययन्तः ||
6.75.e: Horses whose hoofs rain dust are neighing loudly, yoked to the Chariots, showing forth their vigour,  With their forefeet descending on the foemen, they, never flinching, trample and destroy them.

6.75.d: रथवाहनं हविरस्य नाम यत्रायुधं निहितमस्य वर्म | तत्रा रथमुप शग्मं सदेम विश्वाहा वयं सुमनस्यमानाः ||
6.75.e: Car-bearer is the name of his oblation, whercon are laid his Weapons and his Armour.  So let us here, each day that passes, honour the helpful Car with hearts exceeding joyful.

6.75.d: सवादुषंसदः पितरो वयोधाः कर्छ्रेश्रितः शक्तीवन्तो गभीराः | चित्रसेना इषुबला अम्र्ध्राः सतोवीरा उरवो वरातसाहाः ||
6.75.e: In sweet association lived the fathers who gave us life, profound and strong in trouble,  Unwearied, armed with shafts and wondrous weapons, free, real heroes, conquerors of armies.

6.75.d: बराह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः शिवे नो दयावाप्र्थिवी अनेहसा | पूषा नः पातु दुरिताद रताव्र्धो रक्षा माकिर्नो अघशंस ईशत ||
6.75.e: The Brahmans, and the Fathers meet for Soma-draughts, and, graciously inclined, unequalled Heaven and Earth.  Guard us trom evil, Pūṣan, guard us strengtheners of Law: let not the evil-wisher master us.

6.75.d: सुपर्णं वस्ते मर्गो अस्या दन्तो गोभिः संनद्धा पतति परसूता | यत्रा नरः सं च वि च दरवन्ति तत्रास्मभ्यमिषवः शर्म यंसन ||
6.75.e: Her tooth a deer, dressed in an eagle's feathers, bound with cow-hide, launched forth, She flieth onward.  There where the heroes speed hither and thither, there may the Arrows shelter and protect us.

6.75.d: रजीते परि वरंधि नो.अश्मा भवतु नस्तनूः | सोमो अधि बरवीतु नो.अदितिः शर्म यछतु ||
6.75.e: Avoid us thou whose flight is straight, and let our bodies be as stone.  May Soma kindly speak to us, and Aditi protect us well.

6.75.d: आ जङघन्ति सान्वेषां जघनानुप जिघ्नते | अश्वाजनि परचेतसो.अश्वान समत्सु चोदय ||
6.75.e: He lays his blows upon their backs, he deals his blows upon their thighs.  Thou, Whip, who urgest horses, drive sagacious horses in the fray.

6.75.d: अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुं जयाया हेतिं परिबाधमानः | हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान पुमान पुमांसं परि पातु विश्वतः ||
6.75.e: It compasses the arm with serpent windings, fending away the friction of the bowstring:  So may the Brace, well-skilled in all its duties, guard manfully the man from every quarter.

6.75.d: आलाक्ता या रुरुशीर्ष्ण्यथो यस्या अयो मुखम | इदं पर्जन्यरेतस इष्वै देव्यै बर्हन नमः ||
6.75.e: Now to the Shaft with venom smeared, tipped with deer-horn, with iron mouth,  Celestial, of Parjanya's seed, be this great adoration paid.

6.75.d: अवस्र्ष्टा परा पत शरव्ये बरह्मसंशिते | गछामित्रान्प्र पद्यस्व मानूषां कं चनोच्छिषः ||
6.75.e: Loosed from the Bowstring fly away, thou Arrow, sharpened by our prayer.  Go to the foemen, strike them home, and let not one be left alive.

6.75.d: यत्र बाणाः सम्पतन्ति कुमारा विशिखा इव | तत्रा नो बरह्मणस पतिरदितिः शर्म यछतु विश्वाहा शर्म यछतु ||
6.75.e: There where the flights of Arrows fall like boys whose locks are yet unshorn.  Even there may Brahmaṇaspati, and Aditi protect us well, protect us well through all our days.

6.75.d: मर्माणि ते वर्मणा छादयामि सोमस्त्वा राजाम्र्तेनानु वस्ताम | उरोर्वरीयो वरुणस्ते कर्णोतु जयन्तं तवानु देवामदन्तु ||
6.75.e: Thy vital parts I cover with thine Armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee.  Varuṇa give thee what is more than ample, and in thy triumph may the Gods be joyful.

6.75.d: यो नः सवो अरणो यश्च निष्ट्यो जिघांसति | देवास्तंसर्वे धूर्वन्तु बरह्म वर्म ममान्तरम ||
6.75.e: Whoso shall seek to hurt us, whether he be a strange foe or one of us,  May the Gods dismember him for the nearest, closest armour is prayer.

7.1.d: अग्निं नरो दीधितिभिररण्योर्हस्तच्युती जनयन्त परशस्तम | दूरेद्र्शं गर्हपतिमथर्युम ||
7.1.e: THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands' swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni,  Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the homestead.

7.1.d: तमग्निमस्ते वसवो नय रण्वन सुप्रतिचक्षमवसे कुतश्चित | दक्षाय्यो यो दम आस नित्यः ||
7.1.e: The Vasus set that Agni in the dwelling, fair to behold, for help from every quarter:  Who, in the home for ever, must be honoured.

7.1.d: परेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहि पुरो नो.अजस्रया सूर्म्या यविष्ठ | तवां शश्वन्त उप यन्ति वाजाः ||
7.1.e: Shine thou before us, Agni, well-enkindled, with flame, Most Youthful God, that never fadeth.  To thee come all our sacrificial viands.

7.1.d: पर ते अग्नयो.अग्निभ्यो वरं निः सुवीरासः शोशुचन्त दयुमन्तः | यत्रा नरः समासते सुजाताः ||
7.1.e: Among all fires these fires have shone most brightly, splendid with light, begirt by noble heroes,  Where men of lofty birth sit down together.

7.1.d: दा नो अग्ने धिया रयिं सुवीरं सवपत्यं सहस्य परशस्तम | न यं यावा तरति यातुमावान ||
7.1.e: Victorious Agni, grant us wealth with wisdom, wealth with brave sons, famous and independent,  Which not a foe who deals in magic conquers.

7.1.d: उप यमेति युवतिः सुदक्षं दोषा वस्तोर्हविष्मती घर्ताची | उप सवैनमरमतिर्वसूयुः ||
7.1.e: To whom, the Strong, at morn and eve comes, maid-like, the ladle dropping oil, with its oblation.  Wealth-seeking comes to him his own devotion.

7.1.d: विश्वा अग्ने.अप दहारातीर्येभिस्तपोभिरदहो जरूथम | पर निस्वरं चातयस्वामीवाम ||
7.1.e: Burn up all malice with those flames, O Agni, wherewith of old thou burntest up Jarutha,  And drive away in silence pain and sickness.

7.1.d: आ यस्ते अग्न इधते अनीकं वसिष्ठ शुक्र दीदिवः पावक | उतो न एभि सतवथैरिह सयाः ||
7.1.e: With him who lighteth up thy splendour, Agni, excellent, pure, refulgent, Purifier,  Be present, and with us through these our praises.

7.1.d: वि ये ते अग्ने भेजिरे अनीकं मर्ता नरः पित्र्यासः पुरुत्रा | उतो न एभिः सुमना इह सयाः ||
7.1.e: Agni, the patriarchal men, the mortals who have in many places spread thy lustre,—  Be gracious to us here for their sake also.

7.1.d: इमे नरो वर्त्रहत्येषु शूरा विश्वा अदेवीरभि सन्तु मायाः | ये मे धियं पनयन्त परशस्ताम ||
7.1.e: Let these men, heroes in the fight with foemen, prevail against all godless arts of 4magic,—  These who ipprove the noble song I sing thee.

7.1.d: मा शूने अग्ने नि षदाम नर्णां माशेषसो.अवीरता परित्वा | परजावतीषु दुर्यासु दुर्य ||
7.1.e: Let us not sit in want of men, O Agni, without descendants, heroleu, about thee:  But, O House-Friend, in houses full of children.

7.1.d: यमश्वी नित्यमुपयाति यज्ञं परजावन्तं सवपत्यं कषयं नः | सवजन्मना शेषसा वाव्र्धानम ||
7.1.e: By sacrifice which the Steeds' Lord ever visits, there make our dwelling rich in seed and offspring,  Increasing still with lineal successors.

7.1.d: पाहि नो अग्ने रक्षसो अजुष्टात पाहि धूर्तेरररुषो अघायोः | तवा युजा पर्तनायून्रभि षयाम ||
7.1.e: Guard us, O Agni, from the hated demon, guard us from malice of the churlish sinner:  Allied with thee may I subdue assailants.

7.1.d: सेदग्निरग्नीन्रत्यस्त्वन्यान यत्र वाजी तनयो वीळुपाणिः | सहस्रपाथा अक्षरा समेति ||
7.1.e: May this same fire of mine surpass all others, this fire where offspring, vigorous and firm-handed,  Wins, on a thousand paths, what ne’er shall perish.

7.1.d: सेदग्निर्यो वनुष्यतो निपाति समेद्धारमंहस उरुष्यात | सुजातासः परि चरन्ति वीराः ||
7.1.e: This is that Agni, saviour from the foeman, who guards the kindler of the flame from sorrow:  Heroes of noble lineage serve and tend him.

7.1.d: अयं सो अग्निराहुतः पुरुत्रा यमीशानः समिदिन्धेहविष्मान | परि यमेत्यध्वरेषु होता ||
7.1.e: This is that Agni, served in many places, whom the rich lord who brings oblation kindles,  And round him goes the priest at sacrifices.

7.1.d: तवे अग्न आहवनानि भूरीशानास आ जुहुयाम नित्या | उभा कर्ण्वन्तो वहतू मियेधे ||
7.1.e: Agni, may we with riches in possession bring thee continual ofierings in abundance,  Using both means to draw thee to our worship.

7.1.d: इमो अग्ने वीततमानि हव्याजस्रो वक्षि देवतातिमछ | परतिन ईं सुरभीणि वयन्तु ||
7.1.e: Agni, bear thou, Eternal, these most welcome oblations to the Deities' assembly:  Let them enjoy our very fragrant presents.

7.1.d: मा नो अग्ने.अवीरते परा दा दुर्वाससे.अमतये मा नो अस्यै | मा नः कषुधे मा रक्षस रतावो मा नो दमे मा वन आ जुहूर्थाः ||
7.1.e: Give us not up, Agni, to want of heroes, to wretched clothes, to need, to destitution.  Yield us not, Holy One, to fiend or hunger; injure us not at home or in the forest.

7.1.d: नू मे बरह्माण्यग्न उच्छशाधि तवं देव मघवद्भ्यः सुषूदः | रातौ सयामोभयास आ ते यूयं पात सवस्तिभिः सदा नः ||
7.1.e: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on our chiefs and nobles.  Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.1.d: तवमग्ने सुहवो रण्वसन्द्र्क सुदीती सूनो सहसो दिदीहि | मा तवे सचा तनये नित्य आ धं मा वीरो अस्मन नर्यो वि दासीत ||
7.1.e: Thou Agni, swift to hear, art fair of aspect: beam forth, O Son of Strength, in full effulgence.  Let me not want, with thee, a son for ever: let not a manly hero ever fail us.

7.1.d: मा नो अग्ने दुर्भ्र्तये सचैषु देवेद्धेष्वग्निषु पर वोचः | मा ते अस्मान दुर्मतयो भर्माच्चिद देवस्य सूनो सहसो नशन्त ||
7.1.e: Condemn us not to indigence, O Agni, beside these flaming fires which Gods have kindled;  Nor, even after fault, let thy displeasure, thine as a God, O Son of Strength, o’ertake us.

7.1.d: स मर्तो अग्ने सवनीक रेवानमर्त्ये य आजुहोति हव्यम | सदेवता वसुवनिं दधाति यं सूरिरर्थी पर्छमान एति ||
7.1.e: O Agni, fair of face, the wealthy mortal who to the Immortal offers his oblation.  Hath him who wins him treasure by his Godhead, to whom the prince, in need, goes supplicating.

7.1.d: महो नो अग्ने सुवितस्य विद्वान रयिं सूरिभ्य आ वहा बर्हन्तम | येन वयं सहसावन मदेमाविक्षितास आयुषा सुवीराः ||
7.1.e: Knowing our chief felicity, O Agni, bring hither ample riches to our nobles,  Wherewith we may enjoy ourselves, O Victor, with undiminished life and hero children.

7.1.d: नू मे बरह्माण्यग्न ... ||
7.1.e: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on bur chiefs and nobles.  Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.2.d: जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बर्हद यजतं धूमम्र्ण्वन | उप सप्र्श दिव्यं सानु सतूपैः सं रश्मिभिस्ततनः सूर्यस्य ||
7.2.e: GLADLY accept, this day, our fuel, Agni: send up thy sacred smoke and shine sublimely.  Touch the celestial summits with thy columns, and overspread thee with the rays of Sūrya.

7.2.d: नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप सतोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः | ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियन्धाः सवदन्ति देवा उभयानि हव्या ||
7.2.e: With sacrifice to these we men will honour the majesty of holy Narāśaṁsa-  To these the pure, most wise, the thought. inspirers, Gods who enjoy both sorts of our oblations.

7.2.d: ईळेन्यं वो असुरं सुदक्षमन्तर्दूतं रोदसी सत्यवाचम | मनुष्वदग्निं मनुना समिद्धं समध्वराय सदमिन महेम ||
7.2.e: We will extol at sacrifice for ever, as men may do, Agni whom Manu kindled,  Your very skilful Asura, meet for worship, envoy between both worlds, the truthful speaker.

7.2.d: सपर्यवो भरमाणा अभिज्ञु पर वर्ञ्जते नमसा बर्हिरग्नौ | आजुह्वाना घर्तप्र्ष्ठं पर्षद्वदध्वर्यवो हविषा मर्जयध्वम ||
7.2.e: Bearing the sacred grass, the men who serve him strew it with reverence, on their knees, by Agni.  Calling him to the spotted grass, oil-sprinkled, adorn him, ye Adhvaryus, with oblation.

7.2.d: सवाध्यो वि दुरो देवयन्तो.अशिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता | पूर्वी शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वञ्जन ||
7.2.e: With holy thoughts the pious have thrown open Doors fain for chariots in the Gods’ assembly.  Like two full mother cows who lick their youngling, like maidens for the gathering, they adorn them.

7.2.d: उत योषणे दिव्ये मही न उषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः | बर्हिषदा पुरुहूते मघोनी आ यज्ञिये सुविताय शरयेताम ||
7.2.e: And let the two exalted Heavenly Ladies, Morning and Night, like a cow good at milking,  Come, much-invoked, and on our grass be seated ' wealthy, deserving worship, for our welfare.

7.2.d: विप्रा यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारू मन्ये वां जातवेदसा यजध्यै | ऊर्ध्वं नो अध्वरं कर्तं हवेषु ता देवेषु वनथो वार्याणि ||
7.2.e: You, Bards and Singers at men's sacrifices, both filled with wisdom, I incline to worship.  Send up our offerings when we call upon you, and so among the Gods obtain us treasures.
May Bhāratī with all her Sisters, Iḷā accordant with the Gods, with mortals Agni,  Sarasvatī with all her kindred Rivers, come to this grass, Three Goddesses, and seat them.
Well pleased with us do thou, O God, O Tvaṣṭar, give ready issue to our procreant vigour,  Whence springs the hero, powerful, skilled in action, lover of Gods, adjuster of the press-stones.
Send to the Gods the oblation, Lord of Forests, and let the Immolator, Agni, dress it.  He as the truer Priest shall offer worship, for the God'sgenerations well he knoweth.
Come thou to us, O Agni, duly kindled, together with the potent Gods and Indra.  On this our grass sit Aditi, happy Mother, and let our Hail! delight the Gods Immortal.

7.3.d: अग्निं वो देवमग्निभिः सजोषा यजिष्ठं दूतमध्वरेक्र्णुध्वम | यो मर्त्येषु निध्रुविरतावा तपुर्मूर्धा घर्तान्नः पावकः ||
7.3.e: ASSOCIATE with fires, make your God Agni envoy at sacrifice, best skilled in worship,  Established firm among mankind, the Holy, flame-crowned and fed with oil, the Purifier.

7.3.d: परोथदश्वो न यवसे.अविष्यन यदा महः संवरणाद वयस्थात | आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरध सम ते वरजनं कर्ष्णमस्ति ||
7.3.e: Like a steed neighing eager for the pasture, when he hath stepped forth from the great enclosure:  Then the wind following blows upon his splendour, and, straight, the path is black which thou hast travelled.

7.3.d: उद यस्य ते नवजातस्य वर्ष्णो.अग्ने चरन्त्यजरा इधानाः | अछा दयामरुषो धूम एति सं दूतो अग्न ईयसे हि देवान ||
7.3.e: From thee a Bull but newly born, O Agni, the kindled everlasting flames rise upward.  Aloft to heaven thy ruddy smoke ascendeth: Agni, thou speedest to the Gods as envoy.

7.3.d: वि यस्य ते पर्थिव्यां पाजो अश्रेत तर्षु यदन्ना समव्र्क्तजम्भैः | सेनेव सर्ष्टा परसितिष ट एति यवं न दस्म जुह्वा विवेक्षि ||
7.3.e: Thou whose fresh lustre o’er the earth advanceth when greedily with thy jaws thy food thou eatest.  Like a host hurried onward comes thy lasso: fierce, with thy tongue thou piercest, as ’twere barley.

7.3.d: तमिद दोषा तमुषसि यविष्ठमग्निमत्यं न मर्जयन्त नरः | निशिशाना अतिथिमस्य योनौ दीदाय शोचिराहुतस्य वर्ष्णः ||
7.3.e: The men have decked him both at eve and morning, Most Youthful Agni, as they tend a courser.  They kindle him, a guest within his dwelling: bright shines the splendour of the worshipped Hero.

7.3.d: सुसन्द्र्क ते सवनीक परतीकं वि यद रुक्मो न रोचस उपाके | दिवो न ते तन्यतुरेति शुष्मश्चित्रो न सूरः परति चक्षि भानुम ||
7.3.e: O fair of face, beautiful is thine aspect when, very near at hand, like gold thou gleamest,  Like Heaven's thundering roar thy might approaches, and like the wondrous Sun thy light thou showest.

7.3.d: यथा वः सवाहाग्नये दाशेम परीळाभिर्घ्र्तवद्भिश्च हव्यैः | तेभिर्नो अग्ने अमितैर्महोभिः शतं पूर्भिरायसीभिर्नि पाहि ||
7.3.e: That we may worship, with your Hail to Agni! with sacrificial cakes and fat oblations,  Guard us, O Agni, with those boundless glories as with a hundred fortresses of iron.

7.3.d: या वा ते सन्ति दाशुषे अध्र्ष्टा गिरो वा याभिर्न्र्वतीरुरुष्याः | ताभिर्नः सूनो सहसो नि पाहि समत सूरीञ जरितॄञ जातवेदः ||
7.3.e: Thine are resistless songs for him who offers, and hero-giving hymns wherewith thou savest;  With these, O Son of Strength, O Jātavedas, guard us, preserve these princes and the singers.

7.3.d: निर्यत पूतेव सवधितिः शुचिर्गात सवया कर्पा तन्वा रोचमानः | आ यो मात्रोरुशेन्यो जनिष्ट देवयज्याय सुक्रतुः पावकः ||
7.3.e: When forth he cometh, like an axe new-sharpened, pure in his form, resplendent in his body,  Sprung, sought with eager longing, from his Parents, for the Gods’ worship, Sage and Purifier:

7.3.d: एता नो अग्ने सौभगा दिदीह्यपि करतुं सुचेतसं वतेम | विश्वा सतोत्र्भ्यो गर्णते च सन्तु यूयं पात ... ||
7.3.e: Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding.  All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.4.d: पर वः शुक्राय भानवे भरध्वं हव्यं मतिं चाग्नये सुपूतम | यो दैव्यानि मानुषा जनूंष्यन्तर्विश्वानि विद्मना जिगाति ||
7.4.e: BRING forth your gifts to his refulgent splendour, your hymn as purest offering to Agni,  To him who goes as messenger with knowledge between all songs of men and Gods in heaven.

7.4.d: स गर्त्सो अग्निस्तरुणश्चिदस्तु यतो यविष्ठो अजनिष्ट मातुः | सं यो वना युवते शुचिदन भूरि चिदन्ना समिदत्ति सद्यः ||
7.4.e: Wise must this Agni be, though young and tender, since he was born, Most Youthful, of his Mother;  He who with bright teeth seizeth fast the forests, and eats his food, though plenteous, in a moment.

7.4.d: अस्य देवस्य संसद्यनीके यं मर्तासः शयेतं जग्र्भ्रे | नि यो गर्भं पौरुषेयीमुवोच दुरोकमग्निरायवे शुशोच ||
7.4.e: Before his presence must we all assemble, this God's whom men have seized in his white splendour.  This Agni who hath brooked that men should seize him hath shone for man with glow insufferable.

7.4.d: अयं कविरकविषु परचेता मर्तेष्वग्निरम्र्तो नि धायि | स मा नो अत्र जुहुरः सहस्वः सदा तवे सुमनसः सयाम ||
7.4.e: Far-seeing hath this Agni been established, deathless mid mortals, wise among the foolish.  Here, O victorious God, forbear to harm us: may weforever share thy gracious favour.

7.4.d: आ यो योनिं देवक्र्तं ससाद करत्वा हयग्निरम्र्तानतारीत | तमोषधीश्च वनिनश्च गर्भं भूमिश्च विश्वधायसं बिभर्ति ||
7.4.e: He who hath occupied his God-made dwelling, Agni, in wisdom hath surpassed Immortals.  A Babe unborn, the plants and trees support him, and the earth beareth him the All-sustainer.

7.4.d: ईशे हयग्निरम्र्तस्य भूरेरीशे रायः सुवीर्यस्य दातोः | मा तवा वयं सहसावन्नवीरा माप्सवः परि षदाम मादुवः ||
7.4.e: Agni is Lord of Amṛta. in abundance, Lord of the gift of wealth and hero valour,  Victorious God, let us not sit about thee like men devoid of strength, beauty, and worship.

7.4.d: परिषद्यं हयरणस्य रेक्णो नित्यस्य रायः पतयः सयाम | न शेषो अग्ने अन्यजातमस्त्यचेतानस्य मा पथो वि दुक्षः ||
7.4.e: The foeman's treasure may be won with labour: may we be masters of our own possessions.  Agni, no son is he who springs from others: lengthen not out the pathways of the foolish.

7.4.d: नहि गरभायारणः सुशेवो.अन्योदर्यो मनसा मन्तवा उ | अधा चिदोकः पुनरित स एत्या नो वाज्यभीषाळ एतु नव्यः ||
7.4.e: Unwelcome for adoption is the stranger, one to be thought of as another's offipring,  Though grown familiar by continual presence. May our strong hero come, freshly triumphant.
Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us O thou Victor, from dishonour.  Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable, in thousands.
Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding.  All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.5.d: पराग्नये तवसे भरध्वं गिरं दिवो अरतये पर्थिव्याः | यो विश्वेषामम्र्तानामुपस्थे वैश्वानरो वाव्र्धे जाग्र्वद्भिः ||
7.5.e: BRING forth your song of praise to mighty Agni, the speedy messenger of earth and heaven,  Vaiśvānara, who, with those who wake, hath waxen great in the lap of all the Gods Immortal.

7.5.d: पर्ष्टो दिवि धाय्यग्निः पर्थिव्यां नेता सिन्धूनां वर्षभ सतियानाम | स मानुषीरभि विशो वि भाति वैश्वानरो वाव्र्धानो वरेण ||
7.5.e: Sought in the heavens, on earth is Agni stablished, leader of rivers, Bull of standing waters.  Vaiśvānara when he hath grown in glory, shines on the tribes of men with light and treasure.

7.5.d: तवद भिया विश आयन्नसिक्नीरसमना जहतीर्भोजनानि | वैश्वानर पूरवे शोशुचानः पुरो यदग्ने दरयन्नदीदेः ||
7.5.e: For fear of thee forth fled the dark-hued races, scattered abroad, deserting their possessions,  When, glowing, O Vaiśvānara, for Pūru, thou Agni didst light up and rend their castles.

7.5.d: तव तरिधातु पर्थिवी उत दयौर्वैश्वानर वरतमग्ने सचन्त | तवं भासा रोदसी आ ततन्थाजस्रेण शोचिषा शोशुचानः ||
7.5.e: Agni Vaiśvānara, both Earth and Heaven submit them to thy threefold jurisdiction.  Refulgent in thine undecaying lustre thou hast invested both the worlds with splendour.

7.5.d: तवामग्ने हरितो वावशाना गिरः सचन्ते धुनयो घर्ताचीः | पतिं कर्ष्टीनां रथ्यं रयीणां वैश्वानरमुषसां केतुमह्नाम ||
7.5.e: Agni, the tawny horses, loudly neighing our resonant hymns that drop with oil, attend thee;  Lord of the tribes, our Charioteer of riches, Ensign of days, Vaiśvānara of mornings.

7.5.d: तवे असुर्यं वसवो नय रण्वन करतुं हि ते मित्रमहो जुषन्त | तवं दस्यून्रोकसो अग्न आज उरु जयोतिर्जनयन्नार्याय ||
7.5.e: In thee, O bright as Mitra, Vasus seated the might of Aduras, for they loved thy spirit.  Thou dravest Dasyus from their home, O Agni, and broughtest forth broad light to light the Ārya.

7.5.d: स जायमानः परमे वयोमन वायुर्न पाथः परि पासि सद्यः | तवं भुवना जनयन्नभि करन्नपत्याय जातवेदो दशस्यन ||
7.5.e: Born in the loftiest heaven thou in a moment reachest, like wind, the place where Gods inhabit.  Thou, favouring thine offspring, roaredst loudly when giving life to creatures, Jātavedas.

7.5.d: तामग्ने अस्मे इषमेरयस्व वैश्वानर दयुमतीं जातवेदः | यया राधः पिन्वसि विश्ववार पर्थु शरवो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ||
7.5.e: Send us that strength, Vaiśvānara, send it, Agni, that strength, O Jātavedas, full of splendour,  Wherewith, all-bounteous God, thou pourest riches, as fame wide-spreading, on the man who offers.

7.5.d: तं नो अग्ने मघवद्भ्यः पुरुक्षुं रयिं नि वाजं शरुत्यं युवस्व | वैश्वानर महि नः शर्म यछ रुद्रेभिरग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ||
